heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants must not exceed 36 months of full-time doctoral study by December 31 of the application year
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is applying for CGRS-D funding
heuristics.action: Submit application before completing 36 months of full-time doctoral enrollment counted to December 31 of the application year
heuristics.because: Exceeding 36 months of doctoral study disqualifies the applicant from CGRS-D eligibility
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: OGS requires a minimum A− (80%) average over the preceding two full-time years of study
heuristics.condition: When a graduate student at an Ontario university applies for the Ontario Graduate Scholarship
heuristics.action: Applicant must demonstrate a minimum A− (80%) average over the preceding two full-time years of study and be enrolled full-time
heuristics.because: Failure to meet the academic threshold makes the applicant ineligible regardless of other qualifications
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities OGS program page; University of Toronto SGS OGS page

heuristics.rule: Apply for NSF GRFP in senior year of undergraduate study
heuristics.condition: When a US citizen, national, or permanent resident is in their final year of undergraduate study and intends to pursue a STEM PhD
heuristics.action: Submit NSF GRFP application before PhD enrollment to avoid the 12-month enrollment restriction
heuristics.because: NSF GRFP eligibility requires that the applicant has not been enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at time of application; applying as a senior undergrad avoids this restriction entirely
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP official documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: Vanier eligibility window closes at 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is being considered for Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship nomination
heuristics.action: Ensure candidate has completed no more than 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year
heuristics.because: Exceeding 20 months disqualifies the candidate from Vanier eligibility, which has a narrower window than CGRS-D
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: OGS is capped at 2 awards at master's level and 4 awards at doctoral level
heuristics.condition: When a student has already received OGS funding at the master's or doctoral level
heuristics.action: Master's students must not exceed 2 OGS awards (before end of 2nd year); doctoral students must not exceed 4 OGS awards (before end of 5th year)
heuristics.because: Exceeding these limits renders the student ineligible for additional OGS funding
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities OGS program page

heuristics.rule: Verify program CIP code with DSO before accepting admission offer
heuristics.condition: When an international student on F-1 is evaluating graduate programs and post-graduation work authorization
heuristics.action: Confirm the specific CIP code of the degree program with the Designated School Official (DSO) prior to accepting, not after
heuristics.because: STEM OPT extension (24 additional months) is available only for degrees on the STEM Designated Degree Program List as determined by CIP code, not program name; the difference is 12 months vs. 36 months of OPT
heuristics.regulatory_basis: ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List; standard OPT 12 months, STEM OPT extension 24 months

heuristics.rule: A person may submit a maximum of three lifetime applications for CGRS-D
heuristics.condition: When a doctoral student is planning to apply for CGRS-D
heuristics.action: Track total number of CGRS-D applications submitted across all attempts; do not exceed three
heuristics.because: The three-application lifetime cap is a hard eligibility limit; exceeding it bars further applications
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: OGS cannot be combined with other Ontario government student assistance in the same period
heuristics.condition: When a student holds or is applying for other Ontario government student assistance concurrently with OGS
heuristics.action: Student must not hold OGS simultaneously with other Ontario government student assistance in the same period
heuristics.because: Simultaneous receipt of OGS and other Ontario government student assistance is prohibited
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities OGS program page

heuristics.rule: International PhD students must negotiate harder on institutional fellowship packages
heuristics.condition: When an international student is negotiating a PhD funding offer
heuristics.action: Explicitly ask each program what fellowship support is available to international students, and treat comparable domestic/international packages as effectively underfunding the international student
heuristics.because: International students cannot access the federal fellowship pool (NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART, Ford Foundation) that domestic students can, creating a structural funding asymmetry
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship — citizenship/residency eligibility requirements

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants who have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC are ineligible
heuristics.condition: When a student previously received a doctoral-level award from any of the three Tri-Council agencies
heuristics.action: Do not apply for CGRS-D; eligibility is forfeited
heuristics.because: Prior receipt of any Tri-Council doctoral scholarship is an explicit disqualifying condition for CGRS-D
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: Students cannot hold OGS and QEII-GSST simultaneously
heuristics.condition: When a STEM student at an Ontario university is eligible for both OGS and QEII-GSST
heuristics.action: Student must choose one award; holding both simultaneously is not permitted
heuristics.because: Concurrent receipt of OGS and QEII-GSST is explicitly prohibited
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities / institutional pages for QEII-GSST

heuristics.rule: Ask explicitly whether GRFP stipend is additive or substitutive before using fellowship as negotiating leverage
heuristics.condition: When a GRFP winner is negotiating with a PhD program
heuristics.action: Ask the department directly whether the GRFP $37,000 stipend and $16,000 cost-of-education allowance are additive to the standard package or substitute for department funding
heuristics.because: Not all departments count GRFP stipend toward their standard package; failure to ask may result in no net financial gain despite winning the fellowship
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP official documentation — strategic implications

heuristics.rule: Vanier nominees cannot have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC
heuristics.condition: When a department is selecting candidates for Vanier nomination
heuristics.action: Confirm candidate has not previously received a doctoral-level Tri-Council scholarship before nominating
heuristics.because: Prior receipt of a Tri-Council doctoral award is an explicit disqualifying condition for Vanier
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: International students on study permits are eligible for OGS through a separate institutional allocation
heuristics.condition: When an international student on a study permit at an Ontario university applies for OGS
heuristics.action: Student may apply; institutions receive a set allocation specifically for international students, typically 15–30% of total OGS allocations
heuristics.because: OGS eligibility explicitly extends to international students on study permits, but through a distinct allocation pool that varies by institution
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities OGS program page

heuristics.rule: Check for block grants and training grants at target programs
heuristics.condition: When a domestic STEM PhD applicant is evaluating funding at target programs
heuristics.action: Ask whether the program has NSF, NIH, or DoD training grants that provide guaranteed fellowship support to incoming students
heuristics.because: Block grants provide guaranteed institutional fellowship support independent of advisor grant availability, reducing funding risk
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP and federal fellowship program official documentation — fellowship strategy section

heuristics.rule: International students may receive up to 15% of available CGRS-D awards
heuristics.condition: When an international student applies for CGRS-D at a Canadian institution
heuristics.action: Verify with the administering agency whether international students are included in the allocation for the relevant discipline
heuristics.because: International students compete within a capped 15% allocation, significantly reducing available awards compared to domestic students
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: OGS application must be submitted through the institution's graduate studies office within the institution's internal deadline
heuristics.condition: When a student intends to apply for OGS for the following academic year
heuristics.action: Apply through the institution's graduate studies office during the typical October–November application period; follow the institution's internal deadline
heuristics.because: Each institution sets its own internal deadline and selection process within provincial requirements; missing the institutional deadline forfeits eligibility for that cycle
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities OGS program page; institutional SGS pages

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D applicants must apply to the single agency matching their primary research discipline
heuristics.condition: When a student is in an interdisciplinary field and determining which Tri-Council agency to apply to
heuristics.action: Submit to one agency only, selected based on primary discipline; NSERC for natural sciences/engineering, SSHRC for social sciences/humanities/arts, CIHR for health research
heuristics.because: Each applicant submits to only one agency; submitting to multiple agencies is not permitted
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — agency assignment rules

heuristics.rule: BC PNP International Post-Graduate Category allows PhD and master's graduates from BC institutions to apply for provincial nomination without a job offer
heuristics.condition: When an international graduate (PhD or master's) has graduated from a BC institution and seeks permanent residence
heuristics.action: Applicant may apply for BC PNP provincial nomination toward permanent residence with no job offer required
heuristics.because: The BC PNP International Post-Graduate Category explicitly waives the job offer requirement for qualifying graduates
heuristics.regulatory_basis: BC PNP International Post-Graduate Category (official BC provincial nominee program)

heuristics.rule: Direct agency CGRS-D submissions are due October 17 at 8:00 PM ET
heuristics.condition: When a student is submitting a CGRS-D application directly to the agency rather than through their institution
heuristics.action: Submit through ResearchNet by October 17 at 8:00 PM ET
heuristics.because: The direct agency deadline is a fixed hard deadline; late submissions are not accepted
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — application deadlines

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D holders may still be eligible for OGS top-up depending on institutional policy
heuristics.condition: When a student holds a CGRS-D and is enrolled at an Ontario university
heuristics.action: Check with the institution whether OGS top-up is available; eligibility varies by institution
heuristics.because: Stacking rules between OGS and CGRS-D are institution-dependent, not uniformly prohibited at the provincial level
heuristics.regulatory_basis: University of Toronto SGS OGS page; Queen's, York, Western institutional pages

heuristics.rule: Vanier students cannot apply directly; nominations must be submitted by the institution
heuristics.condition: When a student wishes to be considered for a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship
heuristics.action: Request consideration from the department/institution, which must nominate the candidate on the student's behalf
heuristics.because: Direct student applications are not accepted; the institution controls nomination eligibility and submission
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program documentation — process

heuristics.rule: Vanier holders typically receive an institution top-up instead of OGS
heuristics.condition: When a student holds a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship and is enrolled at an Ontario university
heuristics.action: Expect an institutional top-up rather than OGS; confirm with the institution
heuristics.because: Vanier holders are typically directed to institutional top-up mechanisms rather than OGS allocation
heuristics.regulatory_basis: University of Toronto SGS OGS page; institutional pages

heuristics.rule: CGRS-D selection criteria are weighted equally: 50% Research Potential, 50% Experience & Achievements
heuristics.condition: When a student is preparing a CGRS-D application
heuristics.action: Allocate equal preparation effort to the research proposal (quality, methodology, significance, originality, ethical conduct, communication) and to documenting achievements (academic record, scholarships, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement)
heuristics.because: Both criteria carry equal formal weight in adjudication; neglecting either half disadvantages the application
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — selection criteria

heuristics.rule: Up to 10 additional CGRS-D awards are reserved for self-identified Black student researchers
heuristics.condition: When a self-identified Black student researcher is applying for CGRS-D
heuristics.action: Self-identify as a Black student researcher in the application to be considered for the reserved allocation
heuristics.because: A dedicated pool of up to 10 additional awards exists specifically for this group, separate from the general competition
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — special provisions

heuristics.rule: Indigenous CGRS-D applicants may receive consideration beyond institutional quotas
heuristics.condition: When an Indigenous applicant is applying for CGRS-D through an institution with a quota
heuristics.action: Note Indigenous status in the application; the application may be considered outside standard institutional quota limits
heuristics.because: Official policy explicitly provides for consideration beyond institutional quotas for Indigenous applicants
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR CGRS-D program documentation — special provisions

heuristics.rule: The 2024 budget stipend increases apply only to Tri-Council grant recipients, not to students funded through supervisor research grants
heuristics.condition: When assessing whether a PhD student will benefit from the 2024 federal budget increase to graduate stipends
heuristics.action: Confirm whether the student holds a Tri-Council award; students funded solely through supervisor grants are excluded from the increase
heuristics.because: The CAD $825 million allocation over five years explicitly excludes graduate students funded through supervisor research grants
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Canada 2024 Federal Budget — graduate funding provisions; Chemistry World 2024 reporting

heuristics.rule: Ask to speak with a PhD student in year 4 or 5 in that specific lab, not a general program ambassador
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD advisor or program before accepting an offer...
heuristics.action: ...specifically request contact with year 4-5 students in that advisor's lab, not first-year students or program-selected contacts
heuristics.because: Year 4-5 students are in the most vulnerable period — funding is ending, dissertation may be stalling — and their experience is the most predictive of what you will actually face

heuristics.rule: If 1 in 4 PhD students would change advisors in retrospect, advisor selection is the highest-variance decision in the entire PhD application process — not program rank, not funding type.
heuristics.condition: When choosing between PhD programs where multiple offers are on the table...
heuristics.action: ...weight the specific advisor relationship above program prestige or location, and conduct structured due diligence on the advisor before committing
heuristics.because: 25% advisor regret rate means the prior probability of choosing a bad advisor without deliberate vetting is extremely high

heuristics.rule: Ask target programs for the exact percentage of graduates who obtained tenure-track faculty positions in the last 5 years before assuming academic placement is viable
heuristics.condition: When a prospective PhD student says their goal is to become a professor...
heuristics.action: ...demand the program's actual 5-year tenure-track placement rate; if it exceeds 30%, the program is above average — meaning most programs will be below 30%
heuristics.because: Nationally only 34% of S&E PhDs go to academia at all, and tenure-track is a subset of that; programs rarely volunteer this data, and advisors may have outdated mental models from their own hiring era

heuristics.rule: Treat any program with a 10-year completion rate below 60% as a red flag requiring explanation
heuristics.condition: When comparing PhD program offers and completion rate data is available...
heuristics.action: ...request the program's 10-year completion rate and apply a 60% floor as a minimum threshold before proceeding
heuristics.because: CGS data shows 25-43% of PhD students never finish; a below-60% rate indicates structural problems in funding, mentorship, or program design, not just individual student failure

heuristics.rule: Ask a prospective advisor directly: 'How often do you meet one-on-one with PhD students and what does that look like weekly?' — and treat vague answers as a red flag.
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: ...demand specifics on meeting cadence and mentoring style, not just research fit
heuristics.because: 50% of PhD students get less than one hour per week with their advisor; access asymmetry is common and predictable, not exceptional

heuristics.rule: Add 3-5 years to any biology PhD career timeline to account for mandatory postdoc before competitive faculty candidacy
heuristics.condition: When evaluating time-to-career-stability for biological or biomedical sciences PhDs...
heuristics.action: ...treat the effective career start as 10-12 years post-bachelor's, not 5-6 years, and factor in postdoc-level salaries (~$52,000-$65,000/year) during that period
heuristics.because: 57.8% of bio/biomedical PhDs go directly to postdocs; the postdoc is not optional but a mandatory intermediate step, making the real cost of this path significantly higher than the PhD duration alone suggests

heuristics.rule: Assume a 2-3 year funding gap between what is promised and when you will actually finish
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD funding package that guarantees 4-5 years of support...
heuristics.action: ...plan financially for 6-7 years minimum and ask explicitly what happens to students after funded years end
heuristics.because: National median time to degree is 7.3 years; most funding guarantees only 4-5 years; the gap is where attrition and financial crises concentrate

heuristics.rule: Treat institutional mental health resources as a near-zero asset unless independently verified — only 26% of students who used them found them helpful.
heuristics.condition: When a program touts its 'student wellness resources' as a selling point...
heuristics.action: ...discount that claim heavily and instead ask current students whether they have actually used those services and found them useful
heuristics.because: Formal availability of mental health resources does not correlate with actual effectiveness; 2 out of 3 users found institutional support unhelpful

heuristics.rule: Use 'definite commitment at graduation' rate — not eventual employment rate — as the honest metric for program-field career outcomes
heuristics.condition: When comparing career outcomes across fields or programs...
heuristics.action: ...ask what percentage of graduates had committed plans on graduation day, not whether they eventually found employment
heuristics.because: Fields like humanities (65.8%) and biomedical (68.2%) show that over 1 in 3 graduates have no definite plans at graduation, which is the most accurate signal of genuine career risk at the moment it matters most

heuristics.rule: A strong publication record in a faculty member does not predict good advising
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential PhD advisor based on their CV or lab prestige...
heuristics.action: ...treat publication record as orthogonal to mentorship quality and separately investigate mentorship behaviors through student conversations
heuristics.because: National Academies finding: mentorship is a learned skill, not a personality trait; negative mentorship patterns (credit-taking, absence, exploitation) are invisible in a publication list

heuristics.rule: High satisfaction scores in PhD surveys do not validate structural conditions — they reflect socialization and sunk-cost commitment, not absence of problems.
heuristics.condition: When a program cites high student satisfaction rates as evidence of program quality...
heuristics.action: ...look past the aggregate satisfaction number and probe specific structural variables: advisor access, bullying rates, career placement, mental health outcomes
heuristics.because: 75% satisfaction coexists with 36% seeking mental health help, 21% being bullied, and 79% reporting career uncertainty — satisfaction is not a proxy for healthy conditions

heuristics.rule: Disregard an advisor's anecdotal academic job market experience if they entered academia before 2010
heuristics.condition: When an advisor or faculty mentor describes academic hiring norms, timelines, or odds...
heuristics.action: ...cross-reference with current NSF SED or equivalent data, not the advisor's personal experience
heuristics.because: Academic placements have dropped 20 percentage points across S&E over 20 years (54% in 2003 to 34% in 2023); advisors who entered in 2005 are working from a mental model that no longer reflects current market conditions

heuristics.rule: Build a mentorship committee of at least 3 people before the end of your first year
heuristics.condition: When starting a PhD program with a single assigned advisor...
heuristics.action: ...proactively cultivate co-advisors, engaged thesis committee members, and peer mentors in senior years rather than waiting for the program to structure this
heuristics.because: Single-advisor models create a single point of failure; National Academies data shows multiple mentoring relationships improve completion and career outcomes

heuristics.rule: Ask programs for concrete placement data — specifically: what percentage of graduates get faculty positions, what percentage go to industry, and who are recent graduates working for — before accepting any offer.
heuristics.condition: When evaluating career preparation quality of a PhD program...
heuristics.action: ...request actual graduate outcomes data rather than accepting vague statements about career support
heuristics.because: Only 29% of students received useful non-academic career advice from their program, and 60% relied on personal research for career planning — programs systematically overstate career preparation

heuristics.rule: Choose CS/Engineering PhD over life sciences PhD when career optionality is a priority
heuristics.condition: When a student is choosing between fields and values having multiple viable career exit points...
heuristics.action: ...weight CS/Engineering more heavily because industry transition requires no retraining or identity shift, whereas biology-to-industry often requires reframing and humanities-to-nonacademic is a cultural identity shift
heuristics.because: Industry/business now employs 47% of new PhDs, but the friction of transition varies dramatically by field; CS PhDs move to industry without postdoc while biology PhDs face retraining barriers and humanities PhDs face institutional culture that actively discourages non-academic paths

heuristics.rule: Ask for the advisor-specific time-to-degree, not the program average
heuristics.condition: When evaluating time-to-completion expectations for a PhD program...
heuristics.action: ...ask 'what is the average time to degree for students who have graduated from this specific lab in the last 5 years' rather than accepting department-level statistics
heuristics.because: Advisor-specific time-to-degree varies enormously within the same program; department averages obscure individual advisor patterns that directly predict your experience

heuristics.rule: Check a Canadian professor's lab website and grant status before emailing them
heuristics.condition: When identifying target supervisors for a Canadian PhD application...
heuristics.action: ...look for 'prospective students' notes on lab websites and verify active grants via NSERC Award Search or CIHR database before investing time in an outreach email
heuristics.because: Many professors post that they are not taking students that cycle, and unfunded professors cannot commit to supporting a PhD student regardless of interest — contacting them wastes both parties' time

heuristics.rule: Ask current 3rd-5th year students what they actually earn, not what the offer letter states
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a Canadian PhD funding offer...
heuristics.action: ...contact current advanced PhD students in the lab/department and ask their annual total income directly
heuristics.because: Offer letters often reflect first-year or best-case funding; later years frequently drop when fellowships expire or supervisor grants shrink

heuristics.rule: If you are Indian or Chinese national, the Canadian PhD path dominates the US PhD path on immigration grounds alone
heuristics.condition: When an Indian or Chinese national is choosing between a US PhD and a Canadian PhD of comparable research quality...
heuristics.action: ...strongly weight Canadian PhD unless the US program is top-10 in the field with no Canadian equivalent
heuristics.because: US EB-2/EB-3 green card backlogs for Indian and Chinese nationals exceed 50 years, making the US path practically a dead end for permanent residency, while Canadian CEC-based PR takes 18-30 months from PhD graduation

heuristics.rule: Ask the advisor's internship philosophy before committing — it immediately reveals which track they optimize for
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a prospective PhD advisor for an industry research career...
heuristics.action: ...ask directly: 'What's your philosophy on PhD student internships?' and listen for whether they proactively name companies vs. express reluctance
heuristics.because: An advisor who views internships as disruptions creates a structural disadvantage for industry placement regardless of program rank or advisor reputation

heuristics.rule: If 2–3 former students independently volunteer the same concerns about an advisor without prompting, weight that signal heavily regardless of the advisor's prestige
heuristics.condition: When conducting due diligence on a known difficult advisor by contacting former lab members
heuristics.action: Treat independently corroborated negative patterns as near-conclusive evidence, not anecdote
heuristics.because: Independent convergence without prompting eliminates the risk of a single disgruntled outlier and reflects a systemic pattern rather than a personal conflict

heuristics.rule: Ask prospective co-advisors to each describe what a completed dissertation looks like before committing
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a co-advising arrangement before accepting an offer...
heuristics.action: ...ask each advisor independently 'What does a completed dissertation in this area look like to you?' and compare their answers
heuristics.because: Divergent answers reveal a future conflict that the student — not the advisors — will be forced to resolve mid-PhD

heuristics.rule: You are applying to an advisor, not a program
heuristics.condition: When evaluating PhD programs...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize identifying and confirming interest from a specific advisor over program prestige or ranking
heuristics.because: The advisor controls your funding, research direction, graduation timeline, and career network — a bad advisor at a top program produces worse outcomes than a good advisor at a lower-ranked program

heuristics.rule: A coursework-only MS without research output rarely strengthens a PhD application
heuristics.condition: When pursuing an MS specifically to improve PhD application competitiveness...
heuristics.action: ...require a thesis option and produce at least one first-authored abstract, poster, or working paper
heuristics.because: PhD programs evaluate research potential, and they need concrete evidence of research ability — coursework grades alone don't provide that signal

heuristics.rule: A coursework-only MS does not strengthen a PhD application unless paired with independent research output
heuristics.condition: When a student completes or plans a coursework MS and intends to apply to PhD programs afterward
heuristics.action: Proactively secure a formal RA position or produce at least one co-authored paper or first-author abstract during the MS
heuristics.because: PhD programs evaluate research potential through demonstrated research evidence; coursework alone gives them nothing to assess that dimension

heuristics.rule: Negotiate before acceptance, never after
heuristics.condition: When you have received a PhD offer and are deciding whether to accept...
heuristics.action: ...use the window between receiving and accepting the offer to negotiate stipend, summer funding, travel budget, and start date
heuristics.because: Once you accept, negotiation leverage disappears entirely — departments have no incentive to improve terms for a candidate who has already committed

heuristics.rule: Apply to programs with 3+ potential advisors, not 1
heuristics.condition: When targeting a specific program for a single faculty member...
heuristics.action: ...identify at least 2 backup advisors in the same department before applying
heuristics.because: If your primary target lacks bandwidth that year, the application fails entirely — single-advisor targeting is high-variance with no fallback

heuristics.rule: If multiple current students give evasive, defensive, or universally positive answers about their advisor, treat it as a negative signal — not a positive one
heuristics.condition: When conducting informational interviews with current PhD students during program visits or decision-making
heuristics.action: Weight generic praise and non-answers the same as negative signals; seek out specific, nuanced responses as the baseline for 'things are fine'
heuristics.because: People who are well-mentored give specific, detailed responses; uniformly positive or vague answers across multiple students indicate either fear of retaliation or coached responses

heuristics.rule: Check faculty rank before evaluating research fit — 'Assistant Professor' means pre-tenure risk exists regardless of how exciting the research is
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a prospective PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: ...look up their faculty rank and years at institution first, before going deep on research alignment
heuristics.because: Research fit is irrelevant if the advisor leaves mid-program; rank is publicly available and takes 30 seconds to verify

heuristics.rule: A top-10 program with a poor advisor match produces worse outcomes than a top-30 program with an excellent advisor match
heuristics.condition: When choosing between a higher-ranked program with weak faculty fit and a lower-ranked program with strong advisor alignment
heuristics.action: Prioritize advisor match and research fit over program rank
heuristics.because: PhD outcomes are advisor-specific, not institution-specific — the advisor's placement record, funding, and mentorship quality drive actual career results

heuristics.rule: A gap year only improves admission outcomes if it produces a measurable new input that wasn't there before
heuristics.condition: When considering declining an offer to reapply next cycle
heuristics.action: Identify specifically what new credential, relationship, or output the gap year will generate — if you cannot name it, don't take the gap year
heuristics.because: Reapplying with the same profile one year later produces the same result; admissions committees evaluate inputs, not elapsed time

heuristics.rule: Verify international student eligibility explicitly before investing time in a UK PhD application
heuristics.condition: When a UK PhD advertisement says 'funding available'...
heuristics.action: ...contact the department directly to confirm whether the funding is open to international (non-UK/EU) applicants before writing any application materials
heuristics.because: Many UK PhD advertisements describe funding that is structurally restricted to UK/EU citizens — international students who don't check waste significant application effort on ineligible positions

heuristics.rule: Verify the CIP code before enrolling, not the program name
heuristics.condition: When an international student is evaluating any MS program that might qualify for STEM OPT...
heuristics.action: ...confirm the exact CIP code with the DSO and cross-check it against the DHS STEM OPT Designated Degree Program List before accepting admission
heuristics.because: A program branded as 'Data Analytics' or 'Applied AI' may or may not qualify for STEM OPT depending on its CIP code — the name is marketing, the code is legal reality, and the difference is 24 months of work authorization

heuristics.rule: In humanities PhD programs, evaluate department funding guarantees before evaluating the advisor
heuristics.condition: When comparing humanities PhD offers...
heuristics.action: ...ask 'What does the department guarantee for ALL PhD students, and for how many years?' before asking anything about the advisor's grants
heuristics.because: Humanities funding flows from departmental cohort packages, not from an individual advisor's grants — the STEM logic of 'does your advisor have an active grant?' is structurally irrelevant here

heuristics.rule: Ask about internal funding deadlines on first contact with a Canadian department, not at application time
heuristics.condition: When initiating contact with a Canadian PhD program...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly ask 'What are the internal scholarship deadlines for incoming PhD students?' before focusing on the program application deadline
heuristics.because: Internal awards like OGS close in October–November, months before program application deadlines of December–January — missing them forfeits a funding source that cannot be recovered that cycle

heuristics.rule: If any portion of the stipend is contingent on winning external competitions, discount it entirely when assessing baseline livability
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PhD offer includes OGS, CGRS-D, or Vanier as part of the funding package...
heuristics.action: ...calculate whether the guaranteed floor (excluding competitive awards) covers your cost of living before accepting
heuristics.because: External award competitions are not guaranteed; students who budget assuming they will win and then don't face severe financial stress mid-PhD

heuristics.rule: Apply for PGWP within 180 days of graduation confirmation — treat this as a hard, non-negotiable deadline
heuristics.condition: When you receive official confirmation of PhD program completion...
heuristics.action: ...immediately initiate the PGWP application through the IRCC portal, do not wait for convocation or final transcript
heuristics.because: Missing the 180-day window permanently eliminates PGWP eligibility — there is no extension and no appeal pathway

heuristics.rule: Use LinkedIn to verify where an advisor's students actually interned — not where the advisor claims connections
heuristics.condition: When an advisor claims industry connections or a pipeline to top AI labs...
heuristics.action: ...search LinkedIn for the advisor's past PhD students and trace their actual internship history
heuristics.because: Claimed connections are cheap; verifiable placement history (Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta AI) is the authoritative signal of real pipeline access

heuristics.rule: Ask a difficult advisor 'tell me about a student who didn't work out in your lab' and evaluate the framing of their answer, not just the content
heuristics.condition: When meeting a prospective advisor known for difficult interpersonal behavior during a campus visit
heuristics.action: Listen for whether the answer is reflective and self-aware versus defensive or blame-assigning
heuristics.because: How an advisor explains past student failures reveals their attributional style — whether they accept partial responsibility or externalize it entirely predicts how they will treat you when things go wrong

heuristics.rule: If the proposed co-advisors have never co-advised before, treat yourself as a first experiment and price that risk accordingly
heuristics.condition: When a co-advising pair has no prior joint advising history...
heuristics.action: ...ask explicitly 'Have you co-advised a PhD student before?' and if no, weight this heavily against the arrangement or negotiate formal safeguards
heuristics.because: Untested co-advising pairs have not resolved their disagreements about research direction, milestone standards, or accountability — the student absorbs the cost of their learning curve

heuristics.rule: Apply to 8–12 programs total, no more and no less
heuristics.condition: When building your graduate school application portfolio...
heuristics.action: ...target exactly 8–12 programs split across 2–3 reach, 4–5 core, and 2–3 safe programs
heuristics.because: Fewer than 8 creates catastrophic risk in a bad admissions cycle; more than 12 yields diminishing returns while consuming significant time and application fees

heuristics.rule: In US R1 STEM programs, an unfunded MS can signal inability to get direct PhD admission rather than added qualification
heuristics.condition: When applying to top US CS or STEM PhD programs with an MS from a non-top program...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly frame the MS as a field change or research pivot, not as a credential upgrade
heuristics.because: US R1 PhD programs default to direct bachelor's-to-PhD entry; an MS without a clear explanatory narrative reads as a failed direct admission attempt

heuristics.rule: If your goal is PhD preparation, choose thesis MS over coursework MS by default
heuristics.condition: When a student is deciding between MS tracks and has a stated goal of entering a PhD program
heuristics.action: Select the thesis track MS even at the cost of longer duration or narrower breadth
heuristics.because: Thesis MS directly produces the advisor relationship, research output, and oral defense experience that PhD applications require

heuristics.rule: Lead with enthusiasm before raising competing offers
heuristics.condition: When you want to use a competing offer as leverage...
heuristics.action: ...express genuine interest first in an initial response, then raise the competing offer explicitly with a specific number in a follow-up call or email
heuristics.because: Opening with a competing offer reads as transactional and can damage the relationship before it starts; expressing interest first frames the negotiation as trying to make the right choice, not extracting maximum value

heuristics.rule: Contact faculty 3–6 months before the deadline, not weeks before
heuristics.condition: When applying to research-based PhD or MS programs...
heuristics.action: ...reach out to 2–3 target advisors per program with a tailored one-paragraph summary and a specific question about their current work
heuristics.because: A positive response creates internal advocacy; the faculty member can champion your file during committee review in a way no SOP can replicate

heuristics.rule: Ask about first-author publication counts by year 3–4 to detect advisor exploitation patterns
heuristics.condition: When evaluating an advisor who runs a large lab or whose own publication output is very high
heuristics.action: Ask current and former students how many first-author papers students typically have by years 3–4; compare across labs in the same field
heuristics.because: Exploiter advisors extract student labor for their own output while deprioritizing student authorship, leaving students with weak CVs relative to time invested — this pattern is directly detectable through publication data

heuristics.rule: A pre-tenure advisor who has already graduated 1–2 PhD students is substantially safer than one whose first cohort is still in early years
heuristics.condition: When a pre-tenure advisor seems like a strong fit...
heuristics.action: ...search Google Scholar, dissertation acknowledgments, and thesis databases to verify whether they have prior PhD graduates
heuristics.because: Successfully guiding someone to completion is the one demonstrated capability that most reduces first-cohort risk; everything else is untested

heuristics.rule: Never join a lab whose advisor has no active grants
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD offer where the advisor's current grant status is unknown or inactive
heuristics.action: Verify active grants before accepting — if none exist, treat the offer as high-risk
heuristics.because: No active grants means no RA funding, no research budget, and likely no graduation support — the stipend offer may disappear mid-program

heuristics.rule: Diagnose the root cause of the rejection before deciding whether reapplication is viable
heuristics.condition: When your application didn't produce your target outcome
heuristics.action: Map your rejection to a specific fixable cause (no research experience, no faculty contact, unfocused application) vs. an unfixable one (profile fundamentally below target) before committing to a gap year
heuristics.because: Some gaps close in a year; others don't, and confusing them leads to wasted time and resources

heuristics.rule: For students from India or China prioritizing long-term settlement, treat Canadian PhD as the default comparator against US PhD
heuristics.condition: When an international student from a high-backlog nationality (India, China) is comparing US vs. non-US PhD options...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly model the PR timeline under each pathway before comparing stipend or program prestige
heuristics.because: US green card backlogs for Indian and Chinese nationals can exceed 20 years, while Canada's Express Entry pathway can deliver PR within 3–5 years of PhD completion — this asymmetry can outweigh stipend differences

heuristics.rule: Use 3-attempt cumulative H-1B probability to set expectations, not single-year odds
heuristics.condition: When an international student is planning around STEM OPT as a pathway to permanent US employment...
heuristics.action: ...calculate the probability of getting zero H-1B selections across all 3 attempts: 1 - (1 - annual_rate)^3, and treat that failure probability as a real scenario requiring a written Plan B
heuristics.because: At ~15% annual entry-level selection rate, roughly 6 in 10 STEM OPT holders will exhaust all 3 attempts without an H-1B — planning only for the success scenario is statistically irresponsible

heuristics.rule: A 5-year funding package in humanities covers roughly half the degree — treat years 6–9 as an unplanned funding problem unless you have a concrete plan
heuristics.condition: When a humanities program offers a 5-year guaranteed funding package...
heuristics.action: ...ask what percentage of students in recent cohorts finished within that window and what the department does for ABD students in years 6–8
heuristics.because: Median humanities time-to-degree is 8.4–9.5 years; a 5-year package is the norm, not a full coverage promise — most students face an unfunded gap that extends time-to-degree further

heuristics.rule: Treat the Canadian professor outreach call like a job interview, not a casual informational chat
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian professor responds positively to your email and schedules a video call...
heuristics.action: ...prepare your research background, formulate specific questions about the lab, demonstrate knowledge of their recent work, and explicitly ask about RA funding availability and whether you can speak with current students
heuristics.because: In Canadian PhD admissions the supervisor's decision is often the de facto admission decision — the formal application ratifies what the professor has already committed to

heuristics.rule: Apply a CAD-to-USD haircut of ~25-27% when comparing Canadian and US stipends, then add back ~$2,000-$6,000 USD for avoided US health insurance costs
heuristics.condition: When an international student is comparing a Canadian PhD offer to a US PhD offer on dollar amounts...
heuristics.action: ...convert CAD to USD at current exchange rate, then adjust upward by $2,000-$4,000 to account for Canadian universal healthcare savings
heuristics.because: Raw dollar comparisons overstate the US advantage; health insurance is a major hidden cost in the US system that Canada eliminates

heuristics.rule: Check Ontario PhD Graduate Stream or BC International Post-Graduate PNP eligibility the day you graduate
heuristics.condition: When graduating from an Ontario or BC university with a PhD...
heuristics.action: ...immediately evaluate PNP eligibility before pursuing Express Entry CEC route
heuristics.because: A PNP nomination adds 600 CRS points, effectively guaranteeing an ITA, and some streams require no work experience — acting immediately preserves the 2-year post-graduation eligibility window

heuristics.rule: For academic-track PhDs, program rank matters more than advisor fit; for industry-track PhDs, advisor industry connections matter more than program rank
heuristics.condition: When choosing between a higher-ranked program with a less connected advisor vs. a lower-ranked program with an advisor who has strong industry lab relationships...
heuristics.action: ...weight program rank heavily if targeting faculty positions, weight advisor industry connections heavily if targeting research scientist roles
heuristics.because: Academic hiring is top-heavy and credential-driven by institution; industry research hiring is relationship- and internship-pipeline-driven

heuristics.rule: Before weighting a brilliant jerk's placement advantage, verify whether their success rate is actually higher or whether they simply produce more students total
heuristics.condition: When comparing placement outcomes between a high-prestige difficult advisor and a lower-profile good mentor
heuristics.action: Divide successful placements by total students advised, not just count the visible successes
heuristics.because: Prominent advisors have longer lists of successful alumni because of volume; the per-student success rate may be no better, and the per-student harm rate may be significantly worse

heuristics.rule: Establish a formal primary advisor of record before starting, not after problems emerge
heuristics.condition: When entering any co-advising arrangement...
heuristics.action: ...confirm in writing who handles stipend, visa documentation, milestone sign-offs, and day-to-day guidance
heuristics.because: Diffuse accountability means each advisor assumes the other is handling critical issues — formal primary designation prevents both from under-attending to your progress

heuristics.rule: Confirm advisor interest at 5+ programs before submitting applications
heuristics.condition: When applying to PhD programs cold without prior faculty contact...
heuristics.action: ...reach out to potential advisors and secure confirmed interest before finalizing your list
heuristics.because: Applications where an advisor already knows your name convert at significantly higher rates than cold applications submitted without any faculty contact

heuristics.rule: Match MS thesis topic to target PhD field, not to general research interest
heuristics.condition: When choosing an MS thesis topic with the goal of transitioning to a specific PhD program...
heuristics.action: ...select a thesis topic that directly overlaps with the research focus of your target PhD programs
heuristics.because: A thesis on Topic A strengthens PhD applications in Topic A; a thesis on an unrelated topic provides weak evidence of fit regardless of quality

heuristics.rule: Ask programs explicitly whether a project-track MS counts as research experience for PhD applications
heuristics.condition: When considering a 'master's by project' or 'project option' middle-ground track
heuristics.action: Contact target PhD programs and ask: 'Will a master's project (not a thesis) satisfy your research experience requirement?'
heuristics.because: Project tracks vary widely in how PhD programs treat them — assuming equivalence to a thesis MS is a common and costly error

heuristics.rule: Always convert stipend to 12-month annualized value before comparing offers
heuristics.condition: When comparing stipend amounts across programs...
heuristics.action: ...ask whether the stated stipend covers 9 or 12 months and calculate the true annualized equivalent
heuristics.because: A $34K/9-month stipend is effectively $28K/year; a lower headline number with 12-month guarantee can be worth more than a higher number that leaves summers unfunded

heuristics.rule: Use advisor placement record as the primary advising quality signal
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: ...look up where the last 5 PhD graduates went (industry vs. academia, which institutions or companies) before any other evaluation
heuristics.because: Placement outcomes are objective, historical, and reflect what the advisor actually delivers — not what they promise during recruitment

heuristics.rule: If 3 or more of the last 8 students left a lab without finishing, do not treat this advisor as low-risk regardless of prestige
heuristics.condition: When researching a potential advisor's track record with previous students
heuristics.action: Count departures relative to total students mentored; a base rate of 37%+ departures is a structural signal about the advisor, not coincidence
heuristics.because: Individual incidents can be explained away; a pattern of departures reflects consistent conditions in the advising relationship that you are unlikely to be exempt from

heuristics.rule: If an advisor evades or becomes uncomfortable answering direct questions about their tenure timeline, treat that evasiveness as a red flag, not just an awkward moment
heuristics.condition: When you ask a prospective advisor 'where are you in your tenure process?' and they deflect...
heuristics.action: ...weigh their response style as data about how they handle uncomfortable professional realities with students
heuristics.because: A mentor who can't discuss institutional risk with a prospective student under low stakes is unlikely to communicate well about harder problems later

heuristics.rule: If you're qualified for a funded PhD, paying for an unfunded MS is a dominated choice
heuristics.condition: When an international student is deciding between a self-funded professional MS and a funded PhD program
heuristics.action: Apply for the funded PhD instead — it costs less, produces a stronger credential, and provides better immigration pathways
heuristics.because: An unfunded 2-year MS costs $150,000–$200,000 total; a funded PhD pays a stipend, waives tuition, and restarts OPT — better financial and career outcome in most cases

heuristics.rule: A funded PhD with a good advisor at rank 20 outperforms an unfunded or advisor-mismatched PhD at rank 5
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to decline a lower-ranked funded offer for a more prestigious but worse-fit program
heuristics.action: Prioritize funding and advisor match over program prestige, unless you can name a specific advisor at the target program and verify that prestige matters for your career path
heuristics.because: Prestige without fit is expensive and rarely delivers the expected premium on measurable outcomes

heuristics.rule: Treat EU MSCA Doctoral Network positions as the primary funding target for international students considering Europe
heuristics.condition: When an international student is applying to EU PhD programs and needs funded positions with no citizenship restriction...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize MSCA DN positions over country-specific or university-specific funding since MSCA is explicitly open to any nationality
heuristics.because: Most EU national and university PhD funding has citizenship or residency preferences; MSCA is structurally designed for international mobility and has no nationality restriction

heuristics.rule: Include opportunity cost in MS ROI or the calculation is fictitious
heuristics.condition: When calculating whether an unfunded MS is financially worth it...
heuristics.action: ...add foregone salary (what you would have earned working instead) to tuition and living costs to get the true investment figure, then divide by realistic annual salary premium
heuristics.because: Students who calculate only tuition underestimate total cost by 40-80%, which systematically makes bad programs look viable — a $80K tuition degree can have a $200K real cost once opportunity cost is included

heuristics.rule: If a humanities advisor has not placed any students into tenure-track positions in the past 5 years, treat it as a red flag regardless of their personal prestige
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential humanities PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: ...specifically ask how many students they have placed into tenure-track or visiting positions in the past 5 years
heuristics.because: Advisor letters and network relationships are a primary mechanism for academic job placement in humanities — an advisor who hasn't placed students recently may lack active field connections even if their own CV is strong

heuristics.rule: Contact 4–6 Canadian supervisors before submitting any formal application
heuristics.condition: When applying to Canadian PhD programs as an international student unfamiliar with the system...
heuristics.action: ...identify and reach out to 4–8 target supervisors in August–September of the prior year before touching any formal application portal
heuristics.because: Canadian programs are supervisor-first; applying without a named willing supervisor often results in outright rejection or indefinite limbo regardless of application quality

heuristics.rule: Treat any PhD offer below CAD $28,000/year in Toronto or Vancouver as financially precarious, not just 'modest'
heuristics.condition: When evaluating stipend adequacy in high cost-of-living Canadian cities...
heuristics.action: ...use $28,000-$32,000 CAD/year as the practical comfort threshold, not the published institutional minimum
heuristics.because: A $24,000 CAD stipend in Toronto equals ~$1,833/month pre-tax, which barely covers rent for a 1BR apartment leaving near-zero margin for all other expenses

heuristics.rule: Take the French language test (TEF/TCF) if you have any French background, regardless of fluency level
heuristics.condition: When building your Express Entry CRS profile as a PhD graduate...
heuristics.action: ...invest time in French language preparation and testing even at moderate proficiency levels
heuristics.because: French proficiency adds 15-50 CRS points depending on level — a high-ROI intervention that can push a borderline CRS score above draw cutoffs

heuristics.rule: If your actual goal is SWE, do not pursue a PhD — calculate the opportunity cost explicitly before applying
heuristics.condition: When a student is considering a PhD primarily to improve competitiveness for software engineering roles...
heuristics.action: ...calculate the 4–5 year opportunity cost ($500,000–$600,000 pretax) against the marginal or negative PhD premium for SWE roles
heuristics.because: PhD SWEs and MS SWEs are compensated identically at the same level at most companies, and PhD candidates may be filtered as overqualified

heuristics.rule: If you cannot identify a co-advisor, a protective DGS, and a personal support structure before accepting, treat a brilliant jerk advisor as categorically higher risk
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to join a known difficult advisor's lab
heuristics.action: Treat support structure as a prerequisite condition, not a nice-to-have
heuristics.because: The same toxic advisor dynamic produces very different outcomes depending on whether buffering structures exist; without them, the worst-case probability increases substantially

heuristics.rule: If you feel like you are managing the relationship between your two advisors, name it explicitly and force a joint meeting
heuristics.condition: When one advisor asks what the other said, or asks you to withhold information from the other...
heuristics.action: ...say 'I'm finding it difficult to reconcile your feedback — can the three of us meet together?' rather than continuing to absorb the tension
heuristics.because: Triangulation is an inappropriate burden on the student; naming it forces the advisors to own their dynamic directly

heuristics.rule: Ask former lab members whether they would choose the advisor again
heuristics.condition: When screening a potential PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: ...speak to 3–5 current and recent students, specifically including those who have already left the lab, and ask explicitly whether they would choose that advisor again
heuristics.because: Current students may feel social pressure to respond positively; recently departed students are more likely to give unfiltered assessments of the actual advising relationship

heuristics.rule: The advisor's recommendation letter content, not the degree itself, is the primary value output of a stepping-stone MS
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether an MS program will actually help your PhD application...
heuristics.action: ...assess whether the program will generate a letter saying 'demonstrated research independence and original thinking' versus 'performed well in coursework'
heuristics.because: PhD admissions committees use letters to assess research potential; coursework-focused letters are inadequate for this purpose even from strong institutions

heuristics.rule: If you've already started a coursework MS and want a PhD, approach faculty for RA positions immediately — one paper changes the application significantly
heuristics.condition: When a student mid-coursework MS realizes they want to apply to PhD programs
heuristics.action: Approach faculty in your department for RA or research collaboration opportunities as early as possible
heuristics.because: Even one RA position resulting in a first-author abstract or co-authored paper materially shifts the PhD application from weak to credible

heuristics.rule: Use specific competing numbers, not vague alternatives
heuristics.condition: When negotiating using a competing offer...
heuristics.action: ...state the specific dollar amount and specific benefits (e.g., '12-month summer support'), not just that you 'have other options'
heuristics.because: Vague references to other options give programs nothing to respond to; a specific number creates a concrete target for them to match or exceed

heuristics.rule: Treat GPA trend as more important than GPA peak
heuristics.condition: When initial screening reviewers scan applications in 30–60 seconds...
heuristics.action: ...frame your academic trajectory explicitly if you had early struggles followed by strong recent performance
heuristics.because: Committees scan for improvement signals as a proxy for intellectual maturity and completion likelihood, not raw GPA maximums

heuristics.rule: When choosing between a known toxic advisor with high prestige and a good advisor with moderate prestige, default to the good advisor unless the prestige advantage is concretely quantifiable
heuristics.condition: When the research fit hierarchy leads you toward an advisor with a documented difficult reputation
heuristics.action: Verify whether 'their students get the jobs I want' is actually true — not just 'everyone says they're brilliant' — before weighting prestige advantage
heuristics.because: The worst-case outcome with a toxic advisor (leaving the field, lasting psychological harm) is substantially worse than the worst case with a good-enough advisor; the expected value calculation favors lower risk once worst-case is weighted appropriately

heuristics.rule: An assistant professor in year 5 or 6 of a 6–7 year tenure clock is approaching a binary outcome — treat this as a near-term disruption risk, not a theoretical one
heuristics.condition: When a pre-tenure advisor is within 1–2 years of their tenure review...
heuristics.action: ...factor in that a tenure decision will occur while you are likely still in years 1–3 of your program, the highest-cost period for advisor departure
heuristics.because: Students in years 1–3 bear the highest cost of advisor departure; timing the overlap between your early years and the advisor's tenure review is a concrete risk calculation

heuristics.rule: For academic job market targets, program prestige in your specific subfield matters more than overall ranking
heuristics.condition: When a student is targeting a tenure-track position and comparing programs
heuristics.action: Research subfield-specific reputation and hiring committee filtering practices, not just overall US News rank
heuristics.because: Hiring committees at research universities filter by program pedigree in first-round cuts — but subfield standing matters more than composite institutional rank

heuristics.rule: Use the 'accept and transfer' path before defaulting to a gap year
heuristics.condition: When you have a funded offer that isn't your first choice
heuristics.action: Accept, generate research output in year 1, then reapply to target programs with real research credentials and a PI letter from your current advisor
heuristics.because: This preserves stipend income, generates stronger application materials under real research conditions, and avoids losing a year if the transfer doesn't succeed

heuristics.rule: Ask UK supervisors whether recent students graduated within the funded period as a proxy for project viability
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a UK PhD supervisor whose project sounds well-scoped...
heuristics.action: ...ask directly 'Have any of your recent students graduated within the funded period (3–3.5 years)?' before accepting
heuristics.because: UK funding typically covers only 3–3.5 years; a supervisor whose students consistently run over is signaling either poor scoping, poor mentorship, or both — and the unfunded tail falls entirely on the student

heuristics.rule: Target large known H-1B sponsors exclusively if you are an international new grad
heuristics.condition: When an international MS student is job-searching with a graduation within 12 months...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize applications to companies with documented high H-1B approval volumes (Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Google, TCS-tier) and de-prioritize SMEs that rarely sponsor
heuristics.because: Sponsorship requirement — not skill gap — is the primary cause of international students receiving 30% fewer offers; concentrating applications on proven sponsors is a structural fix, not an optimization

heuristics.rule: Negotiate teaching obligations by year, not just stipend amount, when evaluating humanities PhD offers
heuristics.condition: When comparing humanities program funding packages...
heuristics.action: ...find out which years require teaching, how many sections per semester, and whether there is a dissertation writing fellowship year without teaching obligations
heuristics.because: Teaching in humanities requires 10–20 hours/week and directly extends time-to-degree; a higher stipend with heavier teaching obligations may cost more in total degree length than a lower stipend with a protected dissertation year

heuristics.rule: Get funding commitment in writing before accepting a Canadian PhD offer
heuristics.condition: When receiving a Canadian PhD offer letter...
heuristics.action: ...verify whether the letter contains a specific, documented funding commitment and do not accept until it does
heuristics.because: Canadian PhD funding is not program-guaranteed like many US funded PhDs — students have arrived without confirmed packages, and verbal commitments are not enforceable

heuristics.rule: Treat Montreal and Edmonton as structurally better financial environments for PhD students than Toronto or Vancouver, all else equal
heuristics.condition: When choosing between Canadian universities with similar research fit and stipend levels...
heuristics.action: ...weight cost of living heavily; a $26,000 CAD stipend in Montreal is meaningfully more livable than the same amount in Vancouver or Toronto
heuristics.because: Montreal 1BR rent is $1,300-$1,800/month versus $2,100-$3,000/month in Vancouver — the same dollar amount produces radically different quality of life

heuristics.rule: Track your NOC code from day one of PGWP employment, not retroactively
heuristics.condition: When starting work on a PGWP after PhD graduation...
heuristics.action: ...verify your job description matches a TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 NOC code before accepting the role, and keep documentation
heuristics.because: Only TEER 0-3 work experience counts toward the 1,560-hour CEC requirement; hours in TEER 4/5 roles (administrative, retail) are wasted toward PR eligibility

heuristics.rule: Investigate co-supervision PhD programs at target industry labs before defaulting to a standard university PhD
heuristics.condition: When a student's target employer is a major AI lab (Google, Meta AI, Microsoft Research, OpenAI)...
heuristics.action: ...research whether that lab has a formal PhD co-supervision or residency program before choosing a standard academic program
heuristics.because: Co-supervision programs offer faster publication timelines, more applied research, and supplemented compensation — a structurally different and often superior path for industry research goals

heuristics.rule: For non-academic career paths, discount the prestige premium from a brilliant jerk advisor if your target role is more than 3 years post-graduation
heuristics.condition: When the primary argument for a difficult advisor is their name recognition and placement network
heuristics.action: Research whether advisor name effects actually persist in your specific target industry and role
heuristics.because: The advisor name effect decays within 2–3 years of employment for most non-academic paths, making the long-term cost-benefit calculation less favorable to enduring toxicity

heuristics.rule: Use a secondary co-advisor defensively when your primary is pre-tenure or has limited bandwidth — but recruit them before a crisis, not during one
heuristics.condition: When your primary advisor is pre-tenure, travels extensively, or has bandwidth constraints...
heuristics.action: ...identify and formally recruit a senior tenured co-advisor before starting, specifying meeting frequency and letter-writing role upfront
heuristics.because: A co-advisor recruited during a crisis has no institutional history with your work and limited leverage to intervene effectively

heuristics.rule: Track where the last 5 graduated students are now
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential PhD advisor's quality...
heuristics.action: ...look up the employment outcomes, job titles, and time-to-degree of the advisor's last 5 PhD graduates
heuristics.because: Past placement outcomes are a concrete, verifiable indicator of advisor effectiveness and network quality — more reliable than reputation or self-reported metrics

heuristics.rule: If PhD rejection had an identifiable root cause, the MS must directly address that root cause to be useful
heuristics.condition: When considering an MS after PhD rejection...
heuristics.action: ...diagnose whether the rejection was due to weak research experience, low GPA, poor fit, or SOP quality — then verify the MS program fixes the specific problem
heuristics.because: A coursework-only MS doesn't fix weak undergraduate research; repeating an application without new evidence produces the same outcome

heuristics.rule: Direct coursework waiver questions to the DGS, not the prospective advisor
heuristics.condition: When you want to negotiate credit for prior graduate coursework...
heuristics.action: ...ask the Director of Graduate Studies during the visit, not your prospective advisor
heuristics.because: Advisors typically don't control program requirements; the DGS has actual authority over waivers and transfer credit decisions

heuristics.rule: Weight a specific letter from a direct research supervisor over a prestigious but distant endorsement
heuristics.condition: When choosing recommenders...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize writers who supervised your thesis or research project and can speak to specific capability over well-known names who know you only superficially
heuristics.because: Committees read letters as informal peer reviews — specificity about research ability signals readiness; vague praise from a famous name does not

heuristics.rule: Ask 'What specifically needs to change for you to approve submission?' to diagnose a Perfectionist Blocker advisor
heuristics.condition: When a student's work is in extended revision with no clear completion criteria from the advisor
heuristics.action: Force the advisor to articulate concrete, satisfiable conditions for approval — or escalate to the Director of Graduate Studies
heuristics.because: Perfectionist Blockers operate by keeping criteria vague and perpetually raising the bar; making the conditions explicit either produces actionable feedback or exposes that the advisor has no clear threshold

heuristics.rule: Verify active funded grants via NSF/NIH Award Search before accepting any offer from a pre-tenure advisor
heuristics.condition: When assessing funding stability with a pre-tenure advisor...
heuristics.action: ...run their name through NSF and NIH public award databases to confirm active grants
heuristics.because: Active funded grants substantially reduce voluntary departure risk because transferring grant management is costly and complex — it creates institutional friction against leaving

heuristics.rule: An advisor with 15+ PhD students cannot provide adequate mentorship to any individual student
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential advisor who has a very large current lab
heuristics.action: Treat high advisor-to-student ratio as a negative signal and investigate mentorship quality directly with current students
heuristics.because: Mentorship is finite — advising attention diluted across 15 students means less feedback, slower progress, and weaker career support per student

heuristics.rule: Ask for deferral before declining
heuristics.condition: When you want the program in hand but need one more year for a specific opportunity
heuristics.action: Explicitly ask the program if a deferred start is possible before declining the offer
heuristics.because: Deferral is more efficient than declining and reapplying, and many programs allow it under specific circumstances that applicants never ask about

heuristics.rule: For Canadian PhD students, apply for tri-council fellowships in year one regardless of stipend adequacy
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PhD student has adequate RA/TA funding and is not feeling financial pressure...
heuristics.action: ...still apply for NSERC CGS-D, SSHRC Doctoral, or CIHR fellowships in year one because they are portable and prestigious
heuristics.because: Tri-council fellowships follow you to any eligible institution, strengthen your CV for academic and industry job markets, and signal research independence to future employers — the opportunity cost of not applying is permanently foregone

heuristics.rule: If country of birth is India or China, treat US permanent residency as effectively unavailable when modeling ROI
heuristics.condition: When an Indian or Chinese national is calculating whether an unfunded US MS makes financial sense...
heuristics.action: ...model the career as ending at H-1B status with no realistic green card path, and recalculate break-even assuming eventual departure or third-country transition
heuristics.because: EB-2/EB-3 backlogs for India and China are 50+ years, meaning even a successful H-1B holder cannot achieve long-term US residency through employment-based pathways in a career-relevant timeframe

heuristics.rule: For humanities programs, ask for specific tenure-track placement numbers — not narrative language about career outcomes
heuristics.condition: When a humanities program describes placement outcomes using phrases like 'many students go on to academic careers'...
heuristics.action: ...ask for the specific number of students placed into tenure-track or visiting positions from the past 3–5 cohorts
heuristics.because: Placement rates at even top-10 programs are 30–50%; vague language masks significant variation and program-specific decline in outcomes

heuristics.rule: Do not spend time or money on GRE preparation for Canada-only PhD applications
heuristics.condition: When applying exclusively or primarily to Canadian PhD programs...
heuristics.action: ...skip GRE preparation entirely and reallocate that effort to supervisor outreach, publication review, and research statement development
heuristics.because: Most Canadian PhD programs do not require the GRE, making GRE prep a direct misallocation of finite preparation time and money

heuristics.rule: Ask explicitly what happens to your funding if your supervisor's grant runs out before you finish
heuristics.condition: When finalizing a PhD offer with a specific supervisor...
heuristics.action: ...directly ask the supervisor this question and assess the clarity and confidence of their answer before committing
heuristics.because: Supervisor grant expiry is a common but rarely disclosed risk that can leave students mid-PhD with no funding and no clear resolution path

heuristics.rule: Use your PGWP status as a negotiating asset with Canadian employers by explicitly framing it as zero administrative burden
heuristics.condition: When job searching in Canada on a PGWP...
heuristics.action: ...proactively tell employers: 'I have a 3-year open work permit — you don't need to sponsor or file anything for me. I can start immediately.'
heuristics.because: Many Canadian employers avoid international candidates assuming sponsorship complexity; clarifying PGWP removes this objection and levels the playing field with domestic candidates

heuristics.rule: Ask for the placement list of the last 5 PhD graduates, not general claims about program quality
heuristics.condition: When evaluating any PhD program during visit days...
heuristics.action: ...ask specifically: 'Where did your last 5 PhD graduates go?' and assess the ratio and quality of academic vs. industry placements
heuristics.because: Aggregate program reputation lags current advisor-specific placement reality; recent concrete placements are more predictive than rankings

heuristics.rule: Before deciding you are different from the students who were harmed by a difficult advisor, explicitly check whether you internalize criticism, have a history of anxiety, or require validation to stay motivated
heuristics.condition: When reasoning 'I can handle it' about a known toxic advisor
heuristics.action: Assess your specific psychological risk profile honestly rather than assuming untested resilience
heuristics.because: The students who were most harmed also believed they were different; resilience under novel high-stakes interpersonal stress cannot be assumed from general confidence

heuristics.rule: Require both co-advisors to sign off on your dissertation proposal together, in the same document
heuristics.condition: When milestone standards are ambiguous in a co-advised arrangement...
heuristics.action: ...get joint written sign-off on the dissertation proposal before advancing, not verbal agreement from each separately
heuristics.because: Separate verbal agreements allow each advisor to apply their own standards at defense time, creating the conditions for a contentious or failed defense

heuristics.rule: For US immigration stability goals, treat a funded PhD as an immigration instrument, not just an academic credential
heuristics.condition: When an international student wants to remain in the US long-term and is concerned about H-1B lottery odds...
heuristics.action: ...factor in that a funded PhD provides 5+ years of F-1 legal stay, resets OPT, and builds the publication record that may qualify for EB-1A or O-1 visa pathways that bypass the lottery
heuristics.because: A funded PhD provides compounding immigration benefits (extended legal stay, OPT reset, advanced degree H-1B pool access, lottery-bypass visa eligibility) that a self-funded MS does not

heuristics.rule: Ask about summer funding explicitly — it is rarely disclosed proactively
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD offer where summer funding is not mentioned...
heuristics.action: ...directly ask whether the stipend is 9 or 12 months and how students typically fund their summers
heuristics.because: Programs rarely volunteer that 'stipend' means 9 months; students who don't ask often discover the gap only when summer arrives, creating financial crises mid-degree

heuristics.rule: Name 2–3 faculty and connect to their recent work in your SOP
heuristics.condition: When writing a statement of purpose for a research program...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly name target faculty and reference their current projects, not just their general research area
heuristics.because: This triggers faculty interest during review and demonstrates you've read their actual work, not just their department page

heuristics.rule: Treat program attrition above 30% as requiring explicit explanation before accepting admission
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD program's overall health and risk profile
