heuristics.action: Ask the DGS directly about the attrition rate and its causes; compare to field averages; seek out former students who left
heuristics.because: High attrition reflects structural program conditions — advisor quality, funding precarity, culture — that will affect you regardless of your individual circumstances

heuristics.rule: Establish a co-advisor relationship with a tenured faculty member from day one, not as a fallback plan but as a genuine mentorship structure
heuristics.condition: When you decide to accept an offer with a pre-tenure advisor...
heuristics.action: ...formalize a co-advisor relationship with a tenured faculty member before or immediately upon arrival
heuristics.because: An existing relationship with another faculty member dramatically reduces disruption cost if the primary advisor leaves; a relationship formed in crisis is worth much less

heuristics.rule: Check actual alumni placement outcomes before trusting prestige assumptions
heuristics.condition: When a student is optimizing for industry careers but considering a high-ranked program known for academic placements
heuristics.action: Ask the department where the last 5–10 cohorts actually went — not what the rank implies
heuristics.because: A top-5 program whose graduates mostly go into academia is a poor choice for industry-bound students regardless of prestige

heuristics.rule: Ask for program-specific employment data, not school-wide data
heuristics.condition: When evaluating an MS program's career outcomes...
heuristics.action: ...request placement rates and employer names specific to that program cohort for the last 2 years, and verify whether those employers are H-1B sponsors
heuristics.because: School-wide employment statistics aggregate high-performing programs with low-performing ones, making a 30% placement program look acceptable when aggregated with a 90% placement engineering program

heuristics.rule: If a humanities advisor takes more than 3 months to return dissertation chapter drafts, treat this as a structural advising problem, not a temporary one
heuristics.condition: When evaluating prospective advisors by speaking with their current students...
heuristics.action: ...ask specifically how long it typically takes the advisor to return chapter drafts
heuristics.because: Slow manuscript feedback is one of the primary mechanisms through which humanities time-to-degree extends beyond the funding window — this adds unfunded years directly

heuristics.rule: Establish a pre-committed exit threshold with specific criteria before joining a high-risk advisor relationship
heuristics.condition: When the decision to join a difficult advisor is made despite known risks
heuristics.action: Define in advance the specific conditions under which you will switch advisors or leave the program, and write them down
heuristics.because: Having a pre-committed exit plan with concrete criteria makes the initial decision less irreversible and reduces the sunk-cost pressure that keeps students in harmful situations longer than they should stay

heuristics.rule: Choose program location based on OPT job search geography, not just academic fit
heuristics.condition: When comparing otherwise similar programs in different locations...
heuristics.action: ...weight programs in major tech hubs (Bay Area, NYC, Seattle, Boston) more heavily for students targeting US employment
heuristics.because: Programs in tech hubs provide 3–6 months of practical job search advantage through denser employer presence, stronger alumni networks, and on-campus recruiting — a structural advantage that compounds during the limited OPT window

heuristics.rule: Interpret 'very independent' from current students as a warning, not a compliment
heuristics.condition: When talking to current PhD students about their advisor...
heuristics.action: ...probe what 'independence' means in practice: how often do they meet, who initiates, how are roadblocks resolved
heuristics.because: 'Very independent' is the polite description for Ghost advisors who provide minimal mentorship — the framing obscures a structural advising deficiency

heuristics.rule: Program location creates structural career advantages that rankings don't capture
heuristics.condition: When comparing otherwise similar programs in different geographies, especially for international students on OPT
heuristics.action: Favor programs in tech hubs or major metro areas if US industry employment is the goal
heuristics.because: OPT has a hard job-search deadline — Bay Area or NYC proximity provides denser recruiting pipelines, networking events, and internship access that structurally improve job search outcomes

heuristics.rule: In Canadian humanities programs, apply for SSHRC Doctoral Fellowships regardless of institutional funding — treat them as portable supplements that increase your total funded years
heuristics.condition: When enrolled in or applying to a Canadian humanities PhD program...
heuristics.action: ...plan to apply for SSHRC Doctoral Fellowships ($20,000–$35,000 CAD/year) in addition to departmental funding
heuristics.because: SSHRC fellowships are portable across eligible Canadian universities and can materially extend the funded period beyond what the department guarantees

heuristics.rule: Secure the receiving advisor before initiating the conversation with your current advisor
heuristics.condition: When considering switching PhD advisors...
heuristics.action: Informally confirm the new advisor's willingness to take you before having any formal conversation with your current advisor
heuristics.because: The post explicitly describes this as Step 1, and the new advisor stated she would accept but that the student needed to handle the relationship with the original advisor themselves — having a confirmed landing spot removes the biggest risk of the transition
heuristics._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

heuristics.rule: Keep cold-contact emails under 250 words, structured in exactly 3 short paragraphs
heuristics.condition: When sending unsolicited cold-contact emails (套磁) to potential PhD advisors...
heuristics.action: Limit total length to 250 words across 3 paragraphs: (1) who you are + specific paper reference, (2) your most relevant research with concrete method/problem/limitation, (3) a specific question or request to connect
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters confirmed that shorter emails had higher response rates; the original poster attributes this to professors not reading beyond one screen, and comment [1] corroborates with personal experience of improved response rate after cutting from 500+ to shorter format
heuristics._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

heuristics.rule: Check a prospective advisor's grant status before accepting an offer
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD offer and assessing advisor stability...
heuristics.action: Look up the advisor's active grants on NIH Reporter or NSF Award Search, and check the project end dates relative to your expected enrollment period
heuristics.because: A grant expiring within 1-2 years of enrollment puts RA funding at direct risk; the original poster's advisor had only one year left on his main grant at the time of the offer, and funding became uncertain by the second year
heuristics._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

heuristics.rule: Send 20-30 targeted, personalized cold emails rather than 100+ generic ones
heuristics.condition: When cold emailing professors for PhD positions without existing connections
heuristics.action: Limit volume, invest per-email research time — read at least one recent paper, include two professor-specific sentences minimum
heuristics.because: Response rate for genuinely personalized emails is 10-20%; marginal response rate on generic emails is near zero, making volume a false proxy for effort

heuristics.rule: Position yourself as a problem-solver and team player, not a paper-publisher, when transitioning to industry
heuristics.condition: When a PhD holder is applying to industry roles after an academic career
heuristics.action: Reframe CV and narratives around impact, transferable skills, and team contributions rather than publication count or research depth
heuristics.because: Paul Agapow, who made the transition from Imperial College Group Leader to AstraZeneca/GSK, explicitly advises this — industry hiring evaluates different signals than academic hiring committees

heuristics.rule: Ask explicit questions about unfunded extensions before accepting a PhD offer
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD offer with a defined funded period...
heuristics.action: Ask: Has your department granted unfunded extensions? How often? What are late submission fee structures? Are TA positions available to bridge gaps?
heuristics.because: All four real student cases in the source involved unfunded extension periods that were not discussed in admissions materials, creating financial and psychological crises

heuristics.rule: Ask advisor-specific structure and feedback questions before accepting a PhD offer
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a PhD offer and choosing between labs or programs...
heuristics.action: Ask: lab meeting frequency, feedback style, mental health leave policy, and whether you can speak to current/former students
heuristics.because: Peer-reviewed data across 50 PhD students identifies unstructured research, inadequate mentorship, and negative feedback as top causes of PhD depression — these are assessable before you join

heuristics.rule: Request specific feedback from rejecting programs before reapplying
heuristics.condition: When you have been rejected from a graduate program and are considering reapplication...
heuristics.action: Contact faculty or admissions staff to ask directly what aspect of your application fell short — research potential, GPA, SOP framing, LOR quality, or fit
heuristics.because: Dr. Pugh's account shows that without faculty feedback identifying 'scholarly potential' as the gap, she would not have known what to fix; generic 'get more experience' without diagnosis wastes the gap year

heuristics.rule: Never choose a PhD program based on a single professor — require at least three faculty members you want to work with
heuristics.condition: When evaluating PhD programs and deciding whether to accept an offer
heuristics.action: Identify at least three faculty members whose research genuinely excites you before committing to a program
heuristics.because: If the one professor you came for leaves, gets tenure denied, loses funding, or turns out to be a poor mentor, you have no fallback — your entire PhD trajectory collapses around a single point of failure

heuristics.rule: If your long-term goal is an academic career in China, prioritize building domestic networks during PhD, not just publications
heuristics.condition: When a Chinese student is choosing between domestic and overseas PhD with plans to return to Chinese academia
heuristics.action: Factor in the strength of your advisor's domestic network and the density of senior peers (师兄师姐) in your target institutions, not just lab prestige
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters note Chinese academia still operates as a relationship society where senior peers in powerful positions directly enable hiring, thesis defense, and publication access
heuristics._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

heuristics.rule: Email a professor directly before applying to confirm they are accepting new students
heuristics.condition: When identifying potential PhD advisors through school websites...
heuristics.action: Send a cold email (套磁) to gauge interest and confirm available slots before investing application effort
heuristics.because: Not every professor accepts new students each cycle, and spots are typically limited — confirmed by the commenter as common practice
heuristics._source: zhihu_海外PhD申请中_如何选择导师.txt

heuristics.rule: Time cold emails to arrive near the professor's local office hours window
heuristics.condition: When cold-emailing CS professors at US research universities who receive high email volume
heuristics.action: Calculate the professor's local time and send the email just before or just after their scheduled office hours, when they are more likely to be at their desk and checking email
heuristics.because: The top answer, written by someone who screened emails for a professor, states that email timing matters more than email quality for high-volume programs — professors at top-30 CS programs don't have time to read every cold email, so catching them at a natural inbox-checking moment increases read probability
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Cold contact emails are a filter, not a booster — they can only hurt you, not help you beyond a baseline
heuristics.condition: When preparing a cold outreach email to a prospective PhD advisor
heuristics.action: Treat the email as a minimum-bar exercise: avoid all negative signals rather than trying to impress; focus energy on strengthening the underlying research profile instead
heuristics.because: The advisor explicitly states that cold emails and CVs are 'minus points, not plus points' — the real decision variables are funding availability and research background strength
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Check whether the program uses committee-based admissions or PI-funded admissions before deciding whether to cold-email professors
heuristics.condition: When applying to a US PhD program and deciding whether to contact professors (套磁)...
heuristics.action: Research the funding model first: if the department funds students centrally (e.g., via TA requirements), cold emailing has little effect; if PIs fund their own students, contacting professors directly can significantly improve admission odds
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters across different fields confirm that professor influence over admissions is directly tied to whether that professor is financially responsible for the student — in committee systems, a single professor's endorsement carries little weight
heuristics._source: zhihu_美国的PhD是都需要套磁吗.txt

heuristics.rule: If your advisor and school are both strong, go directly to PhD without working first
heuristics.condition: When a student has a solid PhD offer with a reputable advisor and is deciding between PhD and industry work
heuristics.action: Accept the PhD offer directly rather than working first or deferring
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters agree that a good offer is rare and timing matters — working first in China makes it nearly impossible to prepare for PhD applications due to 996 work culture, and the PhD title unlocks options (research scientist roles, faculty, EB1) that are otherwise inaccessible
heuristics._source: zhihu_计算机视觉读博还是工作.txt

heuristics.rule: If you are asking whether you should pursue a PhD, the answer is probably no
heuristics.condition: When someone posts publicly asking strangers whether they should pursue a PhD
heuristics.action: Treat the act of asking as a signal of insufficient intrinsic motivation — default toward not pursuing
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters converge on the point that genuine fit for research is largely intrinsic; those who are truly suited generally already know it and do not need external validation

heuristics.rule: Switch advisors earlier rather than later to minimize sunk cost and time loss
heuristics.condition: When you have identified a serious advisor mismatch (ghost advisor, no publications, no grant funding)...
heuristics.action: Initiate the switch as early as possible, ideally before year 3-4
heuristics.because: The original poster lost 8-10 months switching in year 3; comment [4] reports losing ~1.5 years switching in year 5, and is now in year 7. Multiple comments corroborate that earlier action has substantially lower cost
heuristics._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

heuristics.rule: Send cold-contact emails 3–6 months before the application deadline (July–September for fall cycle)
heuristics.condition: When planning the timing of PhD advisor outreach for a fall semester start...
heuristics.action: Send emails in July–September, well before the October–December deadline window
heuristics.because: Comment [2] corroborates the original post: professors in CS often decide their recruiting slate during the summer, and late outreach (e.g., October) results in responses saying slots are already filled
heuristics._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

heuristics.rule: Contact former (graduated) lab members, not just current students, when vetting an advisor
heuristics.condition: When doing due diligence on a potential PhD advisor...
heuristics.action: Find students who graduated from the lab in the past 5 years via LinkedIn and reach out directly to ask about mentorship quality and lab culture
heuristics.because: Current students have incentives to speak positively; departed students are more likely to share honest assessments — one commenter's contact explicitly warned that the advisor was not suitable as a sole advisor (corroborated by original poster and comment [2])
heuristics._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

heuristics.rule: Contact professors 3-6 months before the application deadline
heuristics.condition: When planning a cold email outreach campaign for PhD admission
heuristics.action: Begin outreach early enough to allow follow-up, a scheduled call, and relationship-building before formal application submission
heuristics.because: Early contact allows time to follow up and schedule a call before application deadlines close — late contact collapses this window entirely

heuristics.rule: Avoid extended postdoc roles if industry is the actual goal
heuristics.condition: When a PhD graduate is uncertain about academia vs. industry and considers a postdoc as a holding pattern
heuristics.action: Do not default to a second or third postdoc — transition to industry directly or after a single postdoc if domain knowledge requires it
heuristics.because: Paul Agapow explicitly cautions that extended postdoc roles signal continued academic commitment to industry hiring managers, who read them as failed academic careers rather than deliberate training

heuristics.rule: When multiple red flags co-occur, require explicit written clarification before accepting
heuristics.condition: When a PhD position shows 3+ concurrent warning signs (non-responsive PI, departed previous student, unusual IT/admin expectations, high-pressure culture)...
heuristics.action: Initiate a direct conversation addressing each concern explicitly and document responses in email
heuristics.because: The PhysicsForums thread shows individual red flags may be explainable, but a pattern of multiple flags together warrants explicit expectation-setting and paper trail for self-protection

heuristics.rule: Treat TA obligations as a mental health buffer, not just a funding mechanism
heuristics.condition: When a PhD student feels TA work is 'distracting' from research...
heuristics.action: Reframe TA work as a source of structure, concrete task completion, and positive reinforcement that research rarely provides
heuristics.because: The study found students identified twice as many positive factors as negative in teaching, and twice as many negative as positive in research — TA work structurally offsets research's mental health risks

heuristics.rule: Address the specific identified weakness in the gap year, not everything generally
heuristics.condition: When you have identified a concrete weakness (e.g., perceived as practitioner not scholar, weak research experience, poor LOR)...
heuristics.action: Design gap year activities that directly close that specific gap rather than padding your CV broadly
heuristics.because: The source synthesis explicitly states 'generic get more experience advice is less useful than targeted gap-filling' and Pugh's success came from strategically selecting an AmeriCorps position that addressed the scholarly potential critique specifically

heuristics.rule: Choose a great advisor with mediocre everything else over a great program with a documented red-flag advisor
heuristics.condition: When deciding between School A (strong advisor, weaker resources) and School B (strong resources, advisor with documented issues)
heuristics.action: Prioritize advisor quality; decline the program with documented advisor problems regardless of prestige or resources
heuristics.because: The advisor-student relationship directly determines whether you graduate; lab culture and facilities are secondary — you cannot change a PI's fundamental approach, but you can navigate resource gaps

heuristics.rule: Even if doing a domestic PhD, overseas experience (joint training or postdoc) is effectively mandatory for competitive academic positions in China
heuristics.condition: When a student plans to pursue domestic PhD and then Chinese university faculty positions
heuristics.action: Plan for at least one overseas research visit or postdoc stay as a non-optional career step
heuristics.because: Commenters note that top Chinese talent recruitment programs (千人/青千) require overseas work and research experience, and joint-training or postdoc abroad is described as 必经之路 (a required path)
heuristics._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

heuristics.rule: Target newly joining (pre-arrival) assistant professors for cold emails
heuristics.condition: When you have average-to-competitive but not exceptional credentials and want higher response rates
heuristics.action: Search individual faculty personal websites for phrases like 'I will be joining [university] in 2024/2025' to find professors who haven't yet appeared on the department page, and email them directly
heuristics.because: These professors have unfilled labs, no established student pipeline, and receive far fewer cold emails than listed faculty — the top answer describes being 'counter-cold-emailed' twice by such professors who found the applicant's profile independently
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Use an institutional or internationally recognized email address for cold outreach
heuristics.condition: When sending cold contact emails to foreign professors
heuristics.action: Use a university or workplace email; if unavailable, use Gmail, Hotmail, or Yahoo — never QQ or numeric-username addresses
heuristics.because: Multiple commenters note that QQ email addresses with numeric usernames trigger spam filters or signal unfamiliarity to professors who don't know Chinese email services
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: If a professor is also on the admissions committee, securing their interest before the decision round is especially high-leverage
heuristics.condition: When a target advisor sits on the admissions committee...
heuristics.action: Prioritize contacting that professor; their dual role means they can advocate directly during committee review
heuristics.because: Commenter from UA neuroscience GIDP explicitly notes that if the professor you contacted is on the committee and your scores meet the bar, admission is nearly certain
heuristics._source: zhihu_美国的PhD是都需要套磁吗.txt

heuristics.rule: Do not plan your PhD output in advance — treat paper count projections as dangerous overconfidence
heuristics.condition: When a prospective PhD student pre-commits to a specific publication count as justification for pursuing a PhD
heuristics.action: Adopt a 'cautiously optimistic' (谨慎乐观) stance and avoid anchoring decisions on projected top-venue paper counts
heuristics.because: The top commenter argues that if you can already 'guarantee' stable top-conference output before starting, the PhD lacks challenge and depth — and such projections are almost always wrong
heuristics._source: zhihu_计算机视觉读博还是工作.txt

heuristics.rule: Evaluate the advisor's actual incentive structure before committing to a PhD
heuristics.condition: When considering a PhD program under a specific advisor
heuristics.action: Assess whether the advisor has concrete incentives to support your career post-graduation, not just your labor during enrollment
heuristics.because: The top answer describes a pattern where advisors extract labor during the program but are indifferent to the student's employment outcome at graduation, citing the explicit dynamic of low stipends and instrumental use of students for funded projects

heuristics.rule: Involve the DGS (Director of Graduate Studies) to formalize advisor changes rather than handling it bilaterally
heuristics.condition: When the advisor switch conversation has been initiated and the current advisor has not formally blocked it...
heuristics.action: Bring in the DGS to handle formal process — committee restructuring, official paperwork, and institutional mediation
heuristics.because: The original poster describes the DGS as the mechanism that completed the formal transition including committee rebuilding; this is corroborated as a structural step, not optional
heuristics._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

heuristics.rule: Ask a specific, substantive question about the advisor's most recent paper (published within 3 months)
heuristics.condition: When crafting the hook of a cold-contact email...
heuristics.action: Read the advisor's latest paper, identify a genuine question about experimental design or methodology, and lead with that question
heuristics.because: Comment [4] independently corroborates this: a specific question about an experiment design led to a 20-minute Zoom call and direct shortlisting; the original post states 'whether the professor responds depends on whether your question is interesting enough, not just how strong your background is'

heuristics.rule: Use program ranking only as a tiebreaker, not as a primary selection criterion
heuristics.condition: When comparing PhD offers across programs of different prestige...
heuristics.action: Prioritize advisor fit, funding stability, and mentorship quality first; invoke ranking only when other factors are approximately equal
heuristics.because: Advisor quality and program ranking are weakly correlated — the same department can house both highly productive mentors and ghost advisors; the original poster chose a top-5 program over a better-fit advisor and regretted it (corroborated by comment [4])
heuristics._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

heuristics.rule: Keep the cold email short enough to fit without scrolling
heuristics.condition: When drafting a cold email to a professor
heuristics.action: Cut the email until it fits on one screen; prioritize the value proposition over background narration
heuristics.because: Author analysis identifies email length as a primary failure cause — professors do not read long unsolicited emails

heuristics.rule: If you are targeting academic careers, assess country-specific odds before committing to the path
heuristics.condition: When an international PhD student is planning a long-term academic career trajectory
heuristics.action: Research the specific national job market for your field before treating 'academia' as a single undifferentiated option
heuristics.because: The source explicitly documents that UK and Australia markets are severely contracted (austerity, Brexit, pandemic cuts), while US and Canada markets are less brutal — the same PhD and the same ambition yield very different outcomes depending on target country

heuristics.rule: Investigate career outcomes of previous students, not just whether they stayed or left
heuristics.condition: When trying to evaluate a PI or lab's quality...
heuristics.action: Ask whether previous students successfully transitioned into desired career paths rather than focusing on attrition alone
heuristics.because: Commenter Office_Shredder explicitly identifies this as more informative than departure status alone — a student who left may have gone on to a better opportunity

heuristics.rule: Treat advisor compassion as the single most important variable in PhD survival — not program ranking
heuristics.condition: When choosing between a high-ranked program with an emotionally distant advisor and a lower-ranked program with a supportive one...
heuristics.action: Prioritize advisor emotional support and mentorship quality heavily, especially if you have any prior history of anxiety or depression
heuristics.because: Across 4 UK student cases, individual supervisor compassion — not institutional support — was the main variable determining whether students survived a personal or funding crisis

heuristics.rule: Apply to more programs in the reapplication cycle, not just the same ones
heuristics.condition: When reapplying after a rejection cycle...
heuristics.action: Expand the application list beyond the programs you previously applied to
heuristics.because: Community synthesis across thegradcafe and studentdoctor identifies this as a consistent recommendation — reapplying only to programs that already rejected you without broadening your pool repeats the same risk exposure

heuristics.rule: Check whether a professor's publication record consists primarily of co-authorships with their own current or former students
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a potential PhD advisor's publication history during the application or interview stage
heuristics.action: Look up the advisor's recent papers and check co-author affiliations; if nearly all are current or former advisees, ask why they don't publish with peers in the field
heuristics.because: Insularity in publishing signals poor peer collaboration skills, which limits the professional network the advisor can offer you and may indicate other dysfunctional relational patterns

heuristics.rule: Overseas PhD training provides a durable advantage for publishing in top English-language journals
heuristics.condition: When research output in international journals is the primary career metric
heuristics.action: Prefer overseas PhD if top-tier international publication is a goal, especially in STEM fields
heuristics.because: Commenters cite that top journals are predominantly overseas-based, advisors abroad are more likely to be reviewers or editors at those journals, and the English writing environment directly improves publication competitiveness
heuristics._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

heuristics.rule: For CS applications, include a personal website with GitHub before emailing; a CV PDF attachment alone is insufficient
heuristics.condition: When applying to CS or CS-adjacent PhD programs at US universities
heuristics.action: Build a personal website that hosts your CV, GitHub projects, and publications before sending any cold emails; reference it in the email body instead of attaching a PDF
heuristics.because: Multiple answers independently state that CS professors use GitHub activity to assess coding ability for applicants without publications, and that lacking a personal website signals ignorance of academic community norms — the top answer explicitly says 'no personal website = extremely disadvantaged, even for career-changers'
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Use a three-paragraph structure for cold outreach emails: self-introduction, research background, alignment with advisor's work
heuristics.condition: When writing a cold contact email to a PhD advisor
heuristics.action: Paragraph 1: who you are and how you found them. Paragraph 2: your research background and results. Paragraph 3: connect your work explicitly to their published research and ask about openings
heuristics.because: Multiple answers independently converge on this same structure, suggesting it reflects what professors expect to see
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Even in committee-based systems, cold emailing is worth attempting if it can leave a positive impression or surface mutual fit
heuristics.condition: When a program uses committee admissions but you have a strong research match with a specific professor...
heuristics.action: Still reach out, framing the email around research interest and unstated strengths not visible in the application — do not assume it is useless
heuristics.because: Best answer notes that exceptionally strong students who contact professors may still receive advocacy even in committee systems, and commenter 2 confirms impression-building has value even without a formal offer
heuristics._source: zhihu_美国的PhD是都需要套磁吗.txt

heuristics.rule: For US PhD students in AI/CV, use summer internships at US companies to supplement stipend income rather than relying solely on stipend
heuristics.condition: When a PhD student in the US is concerned about financial constraints during the degree
heuristics.action: Plan for summer internships ($8K+/month at top US companies) as a financial buffer
heuristics.because: One commenter explicitly calculated that US internship income is sufficient to fund a car and travel, and another noted that returning to China for internships avoids OPT complications
heuristics._source: zhihu_计算机视觉读博还是工作.txt

heuristics.rule: Do not treat a PhD as a mechanism for social class mobility if your parents lack professional capital
heuristics.condition: When a student from a non-professional-class background is considering a PhD as a path to higher social status or income
heuristics.action: Stress-test the assumption that the degree alone changes structural outcomes; evaluate concrete employment data for PhD graduates in the field
heuristics.because: The top answer argues at length that structural starting conditions — parental profession, network, capital — remain largely unchanged by a PhD, and that the degree primarily adds years of low income without guaranteed status gain

heuristics.rule: Assess the DGS's disposition before initiating formal advisor-switch proceedings
heuristics.condition: When planning to escalate an advisor mismatch to the DGS...
heuristics.action: Informally gauge whether your department's DGS tends to advocate for students or for faculty before formally engaging them
heuristics.because: Comment [6] (56 likes) explicitly warns that DGS behavior varies significantly by department — some help students, some side with advisors — and this can determine whether the formal process goes smoothly or becomes adversarial
heuristics._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

heuristics.rule: Check the advisor's homepage for explicit instructions before emailing
heuristics.condition: When identifying which professors to cold-contact...
heuristics.action: If the professor's webpage states 'I do not accept unsolicited emails' or 'contact through the formal application system,' skip the email and express interest through the SOP instead
heuristics.because: Comment [3] flags this as a concrete rule with an actionable alternative; ignoring such instructions signals poor attention to detail to the very person evaluating you
heuristics._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

heuristics.rule: Identify 3+ target advisors you would genuinely work with before applying, then filter by responsiveness and bandwidth
heuristics.condition: When building a PhD application list...
heuristics.action: Cold-email each target advisor early and assess who responds, engages substantively, and signals availability to take new students
heuristics.because: Responsiveness during the pre-application stage is a signal of mentorship style and current bandwidth; advisors who do not respond to prospective students are unlikely to become attentive mentors
heuristics._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

heuristics.rule: Request a conversation, not a position commitment, in the initial email
heuristics.condition: When making the ask in a cold email
heuristics.action: Ask for a 15-20 minute call or meeting, not for a direct offer or confirmation of open positions
heuristics.because: Asking for a commitment in a first contact is too high a bar; a conversation ask lowers friction and is more likely to receive a yes

heuristics.rule: If savings run out during an unfunded extension, prioritize part-time or full-time work over accumulating university debt where thesis submission fees are involved
heuristics.condition: When a PhD student has exhausted funding and faces late submission fees...
heuristics.action: Use savings to finish if possible; otherwise find part-time or full-time work before allowing debt to university to accumulate
heuristics.because: Anonymous Story 3 student explicitly advises this after surviving 15 months of full-time employment to fund completion, and Story 4 confirms savings of only two months was insufficient

heuristics.rule: Interview invitations without offers signal a competitive-but-adjustable profile worth reapplying
heuristics.condition: When you received interview invitations in your application cycle but received no offers...
heuristics.action: Treat this as a strong signal to reapply with targeted adjustments rather than abandon the pursuit
heuristics.because: Community consensus from multiple forums identifies 'interview invitations but no offers' as evidence that your fundamental profile clears the bar — the failure point is at the close, which is more correctable than a pre-screen rejection

heuristics.rule: Treat current student enthusiasm during campus visits as a signal, not just a formality
heuristics.condition: When attending PhD visit weekends or interviews and speaking with current graduate students
heuristics.action: Listen for hesitation, pauses, and qualified praise ('yeah...it's a really great program') and probe for patterns across multiple students
heuristics.because: Students who genuinely enjoy their program express it naturally; muted or performative enthusiasm after a pause reveals what they cannot say directly

heuristics.rule: Open cold emails by naming the professor's research interests first, not by introducing yourself
heuristics.condition: When writing cold emails to professors whose papers you may not have read in depth
heuristics.action: Lead with one to two sentences identifying the professor's specific research focus or a paper title, explain why that direction matters, then introduce your own background
heuristics.because: Answer [2] explicitly frames cold-emailing as 'selling yourself to a customer' and states that professors, like anyone, are more likely to engage with someone who demonstrates interest in them first — this structure is described as the key differentiator between template emails that get ignored and ones that get replies
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Always include a subject line that clearly states your purpose and identity
heuristics.condition: When sending any cold outreach email to a professor
heuristics.action: Write a subject line such as 'Application for PhD Position from [Name]' or 'Inquiry about PhD Positions in Your Group'
heuristics.because: A missing or vague subject line causes emails to be treated as spam or ignored — multiple commenters flag this as a basic error
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Assess authorship position of students in an advisor's recent publications
heuristics.condition: When evaluating how much a potential advisor invests in student career development...
heuristics.action: Review the advisor's recent papers and check whether students appear as first or second authors; treat consistent advisor-first authorship with students absent from top positions as a warning signal
heuristics.because: A mentor who consistently takes first authorship over students may be limiting their publication record and career prospects (comment [3], 112 likes)
heuristics._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

heuristics.rule: Highlight external funding eligibility (e.g., DAAD, CSC) when emailing German professors
heuristics.condition: When cold emailing professors at German universities for PhD positions
heuristics.action: Explicitly mention any scholarship eligibility that would remove the professor's financial burden for hiring you
heuristics.because: PhD in Germany is an employment contract — the hiring cost barrier is real and external funding removes it entirely, making candidates significantly more attractive

heuristics.rule: Obtain at least one new strong recommendation letter emphasizing research capability before reapplying
heuristics.condition: When reapplying after a rejection cycle...
heuristics.action: Secure a new LOR from someone who can specifically speak to your research potential, ideally acquired during the gap year
heuristics.because: Community synthesis identifies LOR quality as one of the five key weakness categories, and a new letter from a gap year supervisor signals growth and addresses the most common SOP-adjacent weakness simultaneously

heuristics.rule: Avoid programs that require PhD students to TA 2–3 courses per semester alongside research
heuristics.condition: When evaluating the TA load expectations of a PhD program during interviews or offer review
heuristics.action: Ask directly how many courses TAs are expected to teach per semester and whether this is standard for the full program duration
heuristics.because: Excessive TA loads signal that the program is using PhD students as cheap labor rather than investing in their research development, structurally delaying graduation

heuristics.rule: Use Gmail or institutional .edu email for cold emails; avoid QQ, 163, or 126 email addresses
heuristics.condition: When sending cold emails to US or international professors from China
heuristics.action: Send all cold emails from a Gmail account or your university's official email address
heuristics.because: Answer [1] includes a firsthand account of a professor confirming that 126.com emails were automatically routed to spam by his institution's mail system, nearly costing the applicant an offer
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Self-funded applicants (e.g. CSC scholarship holders) have meaningfully more leverage in cold outreach
heuristics.condition: When a student has secured external funding before contacting advisors
heuristics.action: State the funding source clearly in the email — it shifts the conversation because the advisor's budget constraint is removed
heuristics.because: The primary commenter identifies funding availability as one of only two real decision variables, making self-funding a direct unlock
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

heuristics.rule: Respond graciously to a 'no' reply — it may produce a referral
heuristics.condition: When a professor responds to a cold email declining to take students
heuristics.action: Thank them professionally and express openness to being referred to colleagues in the field
heuristics.because: A gracious reply to a no has been noted to lead to colleague recommendations — the network value of a declined response is non-zero

heuristics.rule: For senior (full) professors, read their high-citation representative works, not just recent papers
heuristics.condition: When cold-emailing established full professors rather than assistant professors
heuristics.action: Find their top-cited papers via Google Scholar and reference those in your email, not their most recent publications
heuristics.because: The top answer explains that full professors' recent papers are often written entirely by students or postdocs with the professor's name added — their representative works are what they care about personally and remember as defining contributions
heuristics._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

decision_factors.factor: Months of full-time doctoral study completed at time of application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for CGRS-D (cap: 36 months by December 31) and Vanier (cap: 20 months as of May 1); exceeding the threshold results in disqualification
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count full-time doctoral enrollment months from program start date to the relevant deadline date specified for each award

decision_factors.factor: Academic average (minimum A− / 80%)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines basic eligibility for OGS; students below this threshold are ineligible regardless of other qualifications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate GPA over the preceding two full-time years of study; must meet or exceed A− (80%)

decision_factors.factor: Citizenship/immigration status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for all major US federal fellowship programs; international students on F-1/J-1 are excluded from NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Hertz Foundation, and Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: US citizen, national, or permanent resident = eligible for federal fellowships; F-1/J-1 visa holders = excluded from all listed federal programs

decision_factors.factor: Prior receipt of Tri-Council doctoral scholarship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Disqualifies applicant from both CGRS-D and Vanier; a hard ineligibility condition with no exceptions stated
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether candidate has ever received a doctoral-level award from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC

decision_factors.factor: Full-time enrollment status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OGS requires full-time enrollment; part-time students are ineligible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm enrollment classification with the institution's graduate studies office

decision_factors.factor: Enrollment duration at time of NSF GRFP application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Applicants enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at time of application are ineligible for NSF GRFP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count months of PhD enrollment at time of application submission; must be 12 months or fewer, or not yet enrolled (final-year undergrad)

decision_factors.factor: Canadian citizenship, permanent residency, or protected person status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Domestic applicants compete in the main pool; international students are limited to 15% of available CGRS-D awards, significantly reducing odds
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify immigration status at time of application; international students must also confirm enrollment at a Canadian institution

decision_factors.factor: Citizenship and immigration status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OGS is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students on study permits; however, international students compete within a separate, smaller allocation (typically 15–30% of total)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm status category; international students should verify whether their institution has an international OGS allocation

decision_factors.factor: Degree program CIP code
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether an international student qualifies for 24-month STEM OPT extension; program name is not determinative — only the CIP code matters
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify specific CIP code with DSO against the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List; e.g., Computer Science CIP 11.07xx qualifies, Information Systems CIP 52.12xx does not

decision_factors.factor: Research discipline alignment with administering Tri-Council agency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which agency administers the application; submitting to the wrong agency or to multiple agencies is not permitted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match primary research discipline to agency: NSERC (natural sciences, engineering, math, CS), SSHRC (social sciences, humanities, arts), CIHR (health sciences, biomedical research); for interdisciplinary work, select by primary discipline

decision_factors.factor: Institutional OGS allocation size for international students
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The number of OGS awards available to international students varies by institution (typically 15–30% of total allocations); a smaller allocation means higher competition for international applicants
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the institution's graduate studies office for the specific international student OGS allocation

decision_factors.factor: Availability of institutional fellowships not tied to citizenship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students who cannot access federal fellowships, institutional fellowships are the primary non-RA/TA funding source
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask each program explicitly what fellowship support is available to international students and whether any departmental fellowships are citizenship-neutral

decision_factors.factor: Institutional nomination quota availability (Vanier)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Vanier nominations are institution-controlled and limited in number; a student cannot self-nominate regardless of qualification
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Inquire directly with department about whether it nominates Vanier candidates and the number of nominations available to the institution

decision_factors.factor: Research record (publications, conference presentations, awards)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Explicitly identified as a competitiveness factor for OGS selection beyond the minimum GPA threshold
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess number and quality of publications, presentations, and prior awards relative to peers in the same program

decision_factors.factor: Whether GRFP stipend is additive or substitutive
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A GRFP award may not increase net funding if the department substitutes department funding with the fellowship amount
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly; there is no uniform policy — varies by department

decision_factors.factor: Research Potential — proposal quality, methodology, significance, originality, critical thinking, ethical conduct, communication
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Constitutes 50% of CGRS-D selection score; directly affects award outcome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluated by adjudication committee against stated sub-criteria: proposal quality, methodology, significance, originality, critical thinking, ethical conduct, communication

decision_factors.factor: Research statement quality
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Explicitly identified as a competitiveness factor for OGS selection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether the research statement is compelling and clearly articulated within the institutional application

decision_factors.factor: Field of study for NDSEG eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: NDSEG is restricted to specific enumerated STEM fields; applicants in non-listed fields are ineligible regardless of citizenship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the applicant's field is in the NDSEG list: aeronautical/astronautical engineering, biosciences, chemical engineering, chemistry, cognitive neuroscience, computer science, electrical engineering, geosciences, materials science, mathematics, mechanical engineering, naval architecture/ocean engineering, oceanography, physics

decision_factors.factor: Experience and Achievements — academic record, scholarships, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Constitutes 50% of CGRS-D selection score; directly affects award outcome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluated by adjudication committee against stated sub-criteria: academic record, prior scholarships received, teaching/mentoring, project management, community engagement

decision_factors.factor: Stage of study relative to OGS award limits
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Master's students become ineligible after 2 OGS awards or end of 2nd year; doctoral students after 4 OGS awards or end of 5th year
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count prior OGS awards received and current year of study against the applicable limits

decision_factors.factor: Prior receipt of a federal graduate fellowship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prior receipt of a federal graduate fellowship disqualifies an applicant from NSF GRFP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the applicant previously received any federal graduate fellowship? If yes, GRFP is not available

decision_factors.factor: Lifetime application count for CGRS-D
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students are limited to three lifetime applications; exceeding this forfeits eligibility permanently
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count all previous CGRS-D (and formerly CGS-D/PGS-D/SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship) applications submitted across all institutions

decision_factors.factor: Field of study (STEM vs. non-STEM) for QEII-GSST eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: QEII-GSST is specifically for STEM fields; non-STEM students are ineligible for this award
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm field of study qualifies as STEM under QEII-GSST program definition at the target institution

decision_factors.factor: RA vs. TA funding source
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RA funding is tied to advisor's grant availability (variable risk); TA funding is institutionally guaranteed; understanding the risk profile differs for planning and visa status stability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly whether funding is through RA (grant-dependent) or TA (institutionally guaranteed); evaluate advisor's grant status

decision_factors.factor: Leadership ability (Vanier-specific)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: One of three equally weighted Vanier selection criteria; absence of demonstrated leadership disqualifies candidates in committee review
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assessed equally alongside academic excellence and research potential; must be demonstrated not inferred

decision_factors.factor: Province of enrollment (Ontario vs. BC vs. Quebec vs. Alberta)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Provincial award availability, amounts, and eligibility rules differ significantly by province; Ontario has the most developed ecosystem (OGS, QEII-GSST); Quebec has FRQSC/FRQNT; BC and Alberta have separate programs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the province of the target institution and research available provincial awards specific to that province

decision_factors.factor: Whether student holds a Tri-Council award (for 2024 budget stipend increase)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Only Tri-Council award holders benefit from the 2024 federal budget stipend increases; supervisor-grant-funded students are excluded
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether student holds CGRS-D, Vanier, CGS-M, or other Tri-Council award at time of stipend disbursement

decision_factors.factor: Supervisor top-up policy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Supervisor top-up is identified as a variable component of total PhD compensation; total annual funding ranges shift substantially based on whether a supervisor contributes top-up
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly during admission: 'Does the supervisor top up federal or provincial awards?'

decision_factors.factor: Institutional base funding package
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Base stipend for funded PhD admits ranges from $18,000–$30,000/year across Ontario institutions; this is the floor before any awards are applied
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: 'What is the base funding package for incoming PhD students in this program?'

decision_factors.factor: French language ability for Quebec provincial awards
decision_factors.why_it_matters: FRQSC and FRQNT are primarily for Quebec residents or students at Quebec institutions; French language ability is described as an asset for these awards
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess French proficiency; confirm whether the target program is English-stream (where French is not always required)

decision_factors.factor: Advisor mentorship quality (behavioral, not reputational)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Advisor relationship problems are the most commonly cited reason for leaving a PhD program; mentorship quality predicts both completion and long-term career outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Talk to current year 4-5 students and recent graduates specifically; ask whether the advisor provides both career support (technical guidance, networking) AND psychosocial support (encouragement, validation); ask about meeting frequency and whether the advisor was available during difficult periods

decision_factors.factor: Advisor meeting frequency and mentoring structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Direct access to your advisor determines feedback quality, progress speed, and psychological safety — and 50% of students get under one hour per week, making this highly variable and consequential
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor directly about typical meeting cadence; ask current and former students in the lab independently to verify; ask how the advisor handled a student who was struggling

decision_factors.factor: Field-specific postdoc requirement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether your field mandates a postdoc before permanent employment fundamentally changes the financial and timeline cost of the PhD; it is not a personal choice but a structural requirement in some fields
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check NSF SED postdoc rates for your specific field; rates above 50% (bio: 57.8%, geosciences: 64.2%) signal that postdoc is effectively mandatory, not optional

decision_factors.factor: Stipend continuity and post-funding-package plan
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Funding interruptions are a primary predictor of attrition; the gap between guaranteed funding (4-5 years) and actual completion time (7+ years) creates a structural crisis point
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: 'What happens to students after their funded period ends?' and 'Are there cases of students whose funding was interrupted and how were they handled?'

decision_factors.factor: Advisor accountability mechanisms in the program
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When supervisors are the primary perpetrators in 48% of bullying cases and over 50% of bullied students feel unable to speak out, the presence or absence of formal oversight structures determines whether abuse can be addressed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether there is a thesis committee with mandatory annual reviews, a formal ombudsperson process, and whether students can change advisors without academic penalty

decision_factors.factor: Definite commitment rate at graduation by field
decision_factors.why_it_matters: This is the most honest available metric of career risk at the point of graduation; a low rate means a meaningful fraction of graduates face genuine uncertainty, not just delayed outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Reference NSF SED data by field; humanities/arts (65.8%) and biological sciences (68.2%) are lowest, meaning roughly 1 in 3 graduates have no plan on graduation day

decision_factors.factor: Program 10-year completion rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Completion rates vary 20-30 percentage points across institutions in the same field; low completion rates signal structural program problems, not just student self-selection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request the 10-year completion rate directly from the graduate coordinator; cross-reference with CGS data if available; below 60% should prompt specific follow-up questions

decision_factors.factor: Program's non-academic career support infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Over 50% of PhD students plan academic careers but the academic job market cannot absorb them — programs with no industry placement infrastructure leave students stranded
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask for placement outcomes data by career type for the last five cohorts; ask whether the program has industry partnerships, career workshops, or alumni networks outside academia

decision_factors.factor: 20-year trend direction in academic placements for your target field
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A field where academic placements have fallen 43 percentage points (math/stats) in 20 years has a structurally different risk profile than a field with stable industry demand; the trend tells you whether conditions are getting better or worse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare the field's 2003 vs. 2023 academic placement rates from NSF SED; math/stats dropped from 70% to 27%, physical sciences from ~55% to ~35%, all S&E from 54% to 34%

decision_factors.factor: Existence of formal recourse mechanisms for advisor relationship problems
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Programs without ombudspersons or student advocates concentrate all power in the advisor; when mentorship fails, students with no formal recourse face a choice between suffering and quitting
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'Does the program have an ombudsperson or student advocate for advisor relationship issues?' and verify it is genuinely independent from faculty

decision_factors.factor: Institutional mental health resource quality (not just availability)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 39% of PhD students score in moderate-to-severe depression range — 6x the general population rate — making mental health support a functional necessity, not a nice-to-have
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current students whether they have used mental health services and found them useful; ask about wait times and whether counselors have experience with PhD-specific stressors

decision_factors.factor: Career optionality by field (friction of industry transition)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Not all PhDs transition to industry with equal ease; the cultural, skills-retraining, and identity cost of leaving academia varies enormously by field and affects the real value of the degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: CS/Engineering: near-zero friction to industry. Biology: moderate retraining required. Humanities: high cultural/identity friction, programs rarely support non-academic paths

decision_factors.factor: Whether the program structures multiple mentoring relationships or relies on single-advisor model
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Single-advisor models create single points of failure; students in programs with structured thesis committees and peer mentorship have better completion and career outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether thesis committee members are actively engaged or ceremonial; ask whether there are formal peer mentorship programs; ask how co-advising is handled

decision_factors.factor: Lab/advisor culture around work hours
decision_factors.why_it_matters: ~50% of programs have a long-hours culture; 25% of students work 51-60 hours per week — this directly determines sustainability of the PhD and mental health outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current lab members what a typical week looks like; ask whether there are explicit expectations around evenings and weekends; observe whether the advisor emails students on weekends

decision_factors.factor: Program's actual tenure-track placement rate over the last 5 years
decision_factors.why_it_matters: National averages mask wide program-level variation; a program above 30% tenure-track placement is performing above the national norm and signals a genuinely strong academic pipeline
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly for the count of graduates in the last 5 years who obtained tenure-track positions; divide by total graduates to get the rate; be skeptical of vague or non-specific answers

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's current grant status and research activity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor whose grants have expired or whose research has stagnated cannot provide adequate career support, funding continuity, or networking opportunities
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check NSF/NIH award databases for current active grants; ask students whether the advisor has new projects starting; look at publication recency

decision_factors.factor: Financial sufficiency of funding
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 19% of PhD students hold outside jobs, 53% of them out of financial necessity — financial stress compounds mental health and career uncertainty pressures
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate whether the stipend covers actual cost of living in the program city including rent, not just nominal funding adequacy; ask students whether they can live on the stipend without supplementing

decision_factors.factor: Time-to-independent-career (not time-to-degree)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The PhD completion date is not the career start date in many fields; the real metric is when you reach financial and professional independence, which is dramatically longer in some fields
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For biology: add 3-5 years postdoc to PhD duration = 10-12 years from bachelor's. For CS: PhD duration is approximately equal to time-to-career. For humanities: add 3-10 years of adjunct/visiting roles

decision_factors.factor: Identity support environment (for underrepresented students)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Underrepresented students leave STEMM at higher rates due to lack of mentorship and identity conflicts with academic culture; this is a structural gap, not individual weakness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the advisor has successfully mentored students from similar backgrounds; ask whether the program has formal support structures for underrepresented groups; look at demographic data for completers vs. non-completers

decision_factors.factor: Primary employment destination in your field (academia vs. industry split)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you plan for academia but 47% of PhDs nationally go to industry — and that share is growing — your planning assumptions may be misaligned with structural market reality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check NSF SED sector breakdown for your specific field; note that industry now exceeds academia as the primary destination (47% vs. 34%) for S&E PhDs nationally

decision_factors.factor: Peer community quality and cohort social environment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Isolation from peer community is a predictor of attrition; cohort social environment provides informal support during the high-attrition years 5-7
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current students whether they have regular informal contact with peers; look for evidence of peer mentoring programs or cohort events

decision_factors.factor: Supervisor's active grant funding status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian PhD funding flows primarily from the supervisor's research grant — if the grant is inactive, depleted, or expiring, there may be no RA funding available regardless of admission interest
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search NSERC Award Search or CIHR funding database for the professor's name; check grant title, amount, and end date; cross-reference with lab website activity and recent publications

decision_factors.factor: Guaranteed funding floor vs. total package headline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The headline package often includes competitive awards that may not materialize; the floor determines actual financial security
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What is my funding if I win no external competitions?' and get a specific number; compare that floor to local cost of living

decision_factors.factor: Country of origin and its effect on US vs. Canada PR timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The US employment-based green card system is country-of-birth based, creating 50+ year backlogs for Indian and Chinese nationals, while Canada's Express Entry CRS system is country-neutral — this single factor can make the Canadian path 20-40x faster to PR
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the USCIS Visa Bulletin for your country's EB-2/EB-3 priority date cutoffs; compare to Canadian CEC processing time of 6-12 months post-eligibility

decision_factors.factor: Target career track (academic vs. industry research vs. SWE)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The optimal program, advisor, and strategy differ fundamentally across tracks — optimizing for the wrong track wastes years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly identify whether you want a faculty position, a research scientist role, or a software engineering role before applying — these are not equivalent endpoints

decision_factors.factor: Outcome distribution shape, not just expected value
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A higher average outcome from a brilliant jerk advisor can be dominated by the asymmetric severity and probability of the worst-case scenario, making expected value comparisons misleading
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Explicitly estimate best-case, median-case, and worst-case probabilities for each advisor option and compare the worst-case tails, not just the peaks

decision_factors.factor: Prior co-advising relationship between the two faculty
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Advisors who have co-advised before have already resolved disagreements about research direction, roles, and expectations — advisors who haven't have not, and the student pays the resolution cost
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: 'Have you two co-advised a PhD student before? What happened to that student?' Probe the outcome, not just the existence of the relationship

decision_factors.factor: Full funding status (tuition + stipend)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the degree costs money or generates income — a fully funded PhD eliminates tuition debt and provides living expenses, while an unfunded MS may require significant financial outlay
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm explicitly in the offer letter whether tuition is covered and whether a stipend is included; do not assume funding based on program reputation

decision_factors.factor: Thesis vs. coursework-only program structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Thesis programs produce research evidence that PhD admissions committees can evaluate; coursework-only programs do not, regardless of GPA achieved
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the program requires an original thesis with faculty advisor supervision, or whether it culminates in a capstone project or comprehensive exam only

decision_factors.factor: Post-graduation goal: industry vs. PhD vs. R&D
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The two MS tracks train fundamentally different skills and produce different credential signals — one is optimized for immediate industry integration, the other for research continuation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself: Is my next step a software engineer or PM role (coursework MS), a PhD application (thesis MS), or an industry research scientist / innovation lab role (thesis MS)?

decision_factors.factor: Stipend funding source (RA from advisor grant vs. TA from department)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RA funding from advisor grants is flexible and negotiable; TA stipends fixed by union contracts are not — the source determines whether any negotiation is even possible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: 'Is my funding an RA position from your grant, or a TA position from the department?' and 'Is the stipend set by union contract?'

decision_factors.factor: Faculty research fit and bandwidth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Admission is determined locally — a perfect candidate with no faculty match gets rejected; a moderately competitive candidate with strong faculty alignment gets admitted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Email target faculty directly before applying; check if they are listed as accepting students; look at their recent grant activity and publication output

decision_factors.factor: Advisor relationship quality and track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The advisor relationship is the single strongest predictor of PhD student mental health outcomes — stronger than funding, program rank, or research area; a toxic advisor compounds every other stressor in the program
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Interview current and former students in private settings; ask about responsiveness, emotional climate, publication authorship patterns, and student departure rates; look for specific vs. evasive answers

decision_factors.factor: Advisor tenure status and years on tenure clock
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether institutional departure risk exists at all; an advisor denied tenure must leave within 1–2 years, potentially mid-program
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check faculty rank on department website (Assistant = pre-tenure), ask directly about tenure timeline, calculate years at institution against typical 6–7 year clock

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's placement record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The single most predictive variable for academic career outcomes — more predictive than program rank because it reflects actual mentorship quality and professional network
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor directly where their former PhD students are now; cross-reference on LinkedIn; ask current students about post-graduation support

decision_factors.factor: Root cause of the admissions gap
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Reapplication ROI depends entirely on whether the gap year can fix the specific thing that caused the shortfall; unfixable gaps make reapplication a bad investment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit your application against the common root causes: research experience, faculty contact, GPA, GRE, application focus, faculty bandwidth — determine which applies and whether it's addressable in 12 months

decision_factors.factor: Immigration pathway clarity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The PhD destination determines which post-graduation immigration route is available — and those routes differ radically in probability, speed, and employer dependence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the full timeline from PhD completion to permanent residence for your specific nationality under each country's system; account for lottery risk (US H-1B), backlog years (US EB categories), and open-permit duration (UK Graduate Route, Canadian PGWP)

decision_factors.factor: STEM OPT CIP code eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a student gets 12 or 36 months of work authorization, which changes H-1B attempt count from 1 to 3 and fundamentally alters immigration probability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request the exact 6-digit CIP code from the program's DSO and verify it appears on the official DHS STEM OPT Designated Degree Program List before enrolling

decision_factors.factor: Department funding guarantee (years and amount)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In humanities, this is the primary financial structure — it determines how many years you are insulated from funding gaps, which directly affects whether you finish the degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What is the stipend amount and how many years is it guaranteed?' — get a written offer letter confirming this; also ask what percentage of recent cohorts finished within the window

decision_factors.factor: Supervisor's willingness to take students this cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In the Canadian system the supervisor's decision is functionally the admission decision — a professor not taking students means no viable application path at that institution regardless of program ranking
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check lab website for explicit 'prospective students' section; note any statements about current capacity; confirm directly in outreach email

decision_factors.factor: Funding duration (all 5 years vs. first 2 years only)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some Canadian programs guarantee funding only for initial years; students in years 4-6 face funding gaps that force them to over-TA or take on debt
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask specifically: 'Is this funding guaranteed for all 4-5 years or just the first 2?' and request this in writing if possible

decision_factors.factor: Research program quality differential between Canadian and US options
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the US program is top-10 in the field with no Canadian equivalent, the research and career capital difference may outweigh the immigration disadvantage — but this is a narrow exception
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether a genuinely comparable Canadian program exists in your subfield; assess advisor quality and lab output, not just university ranking

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's student placement history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The advisor's network and track record directly determine internship access, letter quality, and job placement probability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: LinkedIn search of past PhD students for internship history and post-graduation roles; ask directly which companies students have interned at in the last 3 years

decision_factors.factor: Research uniqueness — whether the advisor is the only viable option for a specific problem
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The calculus for accepting a difficult relationship changes meaningfully if the research problem is your genuine life's work and no alternative advisor comes close
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether any other faculty member in the world works on your exact problem at a level that would satisfy your research goals — distinguish 'best fit' from 'only fit'

decision_factors.factor: Funding structure — departmental guarantee vs. split grant funding
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Split grant funding doubles the single-point-of-failure risk; if either grant lapses, the student loses part or all of their stipend with no clear responsible party
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'Is my funding departmentally guaranteed, or does it come from both of your grants?' and 'What happens to my funding if one grant doesn't renew?' Ask about precedent with prior students

decision_factors.factor: Advisor funding continuity and graduation record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If an advisor's grant ends, student funding may end; if an advisor has not successfully graduated students recently, the risk of degree completion failure increases substantially
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor directly about their current grant status; check how many students have graduated from the lab in the last 3 years and where those students are now

decision_factors.factor: Advisor relationship quality and letter content
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The strength of a PhD application from an MS stepping stone depends almost entirely on whether the MS advisor can write a research-specific letter
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Before enrolling, ask prospective advisors directly whether they take MS students on active research projects and whether they write letters for PhD applications

decision_factors.factor: Research output during the MS
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PhD programs need evidence of research potential; a degree label alone does not supply it — the presence or absence of research output determines whether the MS strengthens a PhD application
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Will this program structure produce a thesis, publication, or formal RA position? If not, what independent pathway exists to generate research output?

decision_factors.factor: 9-month vs. 12-month stipend coverage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 9-month stipend leaves 3 months of income uncertain each year, which compounds significantly over a 5-year PhD and forces students to scramble for summer RA/TA/fellowship funding annually
