decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: 'Is the stipend guaranteed for 12 months, or does it cover 9 months?' and 'How do students in your group typically fund their summers?'

decision_factors.factor: Advisor advising quality (independent of program ranking)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The student–advisor relationship is the strongest predictor of PhD success — stronger than program ranking, funding, or any other factor; toxic or neglectful advisors produce failed or derailed PhDs regardless of institutional prestige
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track placement of last 5 graduates, review first-authorship patterns in publications, talk to current and former students, assess email responsiveness pre-admission

decision_factors.factor: Advisor toxicity type
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Different advisor dysfunction patterns have different recovery potential; a Ghost advisor is more recoverable with co-advisor support than an Emotionally Volatile advisor, and an Exploiter damages career outcomes differently than a Perfectionist Blocker
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map advisor behavior against specific patterns (Ghost, Perfectionist Blocker, Exploiter, Emotionally Volatile, Brilliant Jerk); ask former students directly about lab culture and what working with the advisor day-to-day is like

decision_factors.factor: Prior PhD graduation record of the advisor
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The single strongest signal that an advisor can actually guide someone to completion; pre-tenure advisors without prior graduates are unproven at the most critical capability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search Google Scholar for dissertation acknowledgments, check institution thesis databases, ask current students directly

decision_factors.factor: Funding security and structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the PhD is financially viable for an international student and whether the stipend will persist through the full program
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether stipend is guaranteed for 4–5 years regardless of advisor grant status, or year-by-year contingent on grants; verify advisor's active NSF/NIH/other grants

decision_factors.factor: Funding status of the offer in hand
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An unfunded or inadequately funded PhD is almost never the right choice; a funded offer changes the cost-benefit of accepting vs. reapplying entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the offer includes a full funding package (tuition plus stipend) vs. partial funding, loans, or self-pay — self-pay PhD without a plan is categorically different from a funded position

decision_factors.factor: Program length vs. career stage alignment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 3-year UK/EU PhD versus a 5–7-year US PhD represents 2–4 years of lost compounding on salary, investment, and career seniority — but also potentially a weaker foundation if the shorter program doesn't fit the student's preparation level
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether the student has a well-defined research question before starting; shorter programs (UK/EU) require research clarity on day one; US programs allow exploration through coursework and rotations

decision_factors.factor: Country of birth EB backlog
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For Indian and Chinese nationals, even a successful H-1B chain leads to a 50+ year green card wait, meaning the entire US career trajectory is built on a visa status that can be terminated — this negates the ROI assumption of long-term US employment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check current EB-2/EB-3 priority dates for your country of birth on the USCIS Visa Bulletin; if the cutoff date is more than 10 years behind, model as effectively unavailable

decision_factors.factor: Teaching obligation structure by year
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Teaching 1–2 sections per semester at 10–20 hours/week competes directly with dissertation writing time and is a primary driver of time-to-degree extension
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask which years require teaching, how many sections per semester, and whether there is any teaching-free dissertation writing year — compare across programs explicitly

decision_factors.factor: Institution location relative to immigration pathways
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Location affects post-graduation PR strategy — some Provincial Nominee Programs favor graduates from outside Toronto/Vancouver, and smaller institutions in those regions may provide faster PR pathways for certain streams
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research PNP streams available in the province of the target school; compare CRS points value of doctoral degree across scenarios; assess Ontario PhD Graduate Stream eligibility if applicable

decision_factors.factor: City cost of living relative to stipend level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same nominal stipend produces radically different financial stress depending on the city; a stipend adequate in Waterloo or Edmonton is precarious in Toronto or Vancouver
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check current 1BR rental prices in the program city; calculate post-tax monthly stipend and compare to monthly rent as a ratio

decision_factors.factor: CRS score competitiveness given personal profile
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A PhD adds 150 CRS points (vs 135 for master's), and with 1 year Canadian work experience the total can reach 480-520+ — but if your language scores or other factors produce a borderline CRS, you may need a PNP fallback
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use the IRCC CRS calculator with your projected profile; compare to historical draw cutoffs for CEC-only rounds (recently 425-475)

decision_factors.factor: Program ranking
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Matters significantly for academic track (top-5/10 programs dominate faculty placements); matters less for industry research track where advisor connections can compensate
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check assistant professor placement data by program; for industry track, rank-30 with strong industry advisor can outperform rank-10 with no industry connections

decision_factors.factor: Support structure availability — co-advisor, DGS posture, lab peer solidarity, personal support
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same advisor toxicity produces dramatically different outcomes depending on whether buffering structures exist in the environment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify co-advisor accessibility and willingness, ask other students whether the DGS has actively intervened in past student-advisor conflicts, observe lab interpersonal culture during visits

decision_factors.factor: Clarity of role division between co-advisors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Without explicit role assignment, both advisors default to assuming the other is handling administrative, milestone, and day-to-day responsibilities, causing gaps
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask each advisor to describe the division of responsibility in practice; compare their answers for consistency. Check whether formal paperwork exists

decision_factors.factor: Genuine interest in research as a practice
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PhD programs require 5–6 years of deep, slow, often frustrating research work; students without genuine research motivation face 40–50% dropout rates and significant opportunity cost if they leave without a degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly assess whether you have already done research and whether you found it intrinsically engaging — not just whether you performed well academically

decision_factors.factor: Whether the target PhD field in the US requires or expects an MS
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In fields like CS and STEM at US R1s, an MS is not required and may be viewed neutrally or negatively; in humanities and social sciences it is often expected
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review admissions profiles of recently admitted PhD students at target programs — note what fraction had prior master's degrees versus direct bachelor's entry

decision_factors.factor: Funding availability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Coursework MS programs are almost always self-funded at full tuition ($30,000–$80,000 for international students); thesis MS programs occasionally offer partial TA/RA funding — this changes the financial calculus significantly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly: Is TA or RA funding available for thesis MS students? What percentage of thesis MS students receive it?

decision_factors.factor: Conference travel support amount and source
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Support ranges from $500 to $5,000/year across programs; students who must self-fund conference travel face compounding inequity in networking and visibility over 5 years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What's the typical conference travel support for students in your group — is there a department fund or does it come from your research budget?'

decision_factors.factor: Advisor funding status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An unfunded advisor cannot support your research financially or pay your stipend, making the PhD structurally unsustainable regardless of intellectual fit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check active NSF/NIH grants on public databases or the advisor's CV for current funding

decision_factors.factor: Support structure buffering capacity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A co-advisor, engaged DGS, formal mentoring committee, and collaborative lab culture can meaningfully buffer a difficult primary advisor; isolation amplifies advisor toxicity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether co-advisors are available and used; assess whether DGS knows students by name and research area; evaluate whether formal mentoring committee meetings occur; ask about lab culture directly

decision_factors.factor: Active funded grant status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines both funding stability for your stipend and the practical friction against advisor departure; unfunded advisors have both incentive and ability to leave more easily
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Run advisor name through NSF Award Search and NIH Reporter; look for active (not expired) grants with multi-year durations remaining

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's current grant status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Directly controls RA funding availability, research budget, and advisor's capacity to support the student through graduation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search NIH Reporter, NSF Award Search, or ask the advisor directly about active funded projects; look for recent grant renewals

decision_factors.factor: Advisor match quality
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A PhD without a clear advisor match means uncertain mentorship, unclear research direction, and weakened job market positioning — more determinative than program ranking
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: do I know specifically who I would work with? Do I have genuine intellectual alignment with them? Have I read their recent work? Would they write me a strong letter?

decision_factors.factor: Nationality-specific green card backlog
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For Indian and Chinese nationals, US permanent residence through employer sponsorship can take decades; this fundamentally changes the value proposition of a US PhD relative to Canadian or European alternatives
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check current USCIS Visa Bulletin for EB-2/EB-3 cutoff dates for the applicant's country of birth; compare against Canadian Express Entry draw history for PhD-level candidates

decision_factors.factor: Field-level MS ROI
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 43% of MS programs have negative lifetime ROI even for domestic students; for international students facing employment gaps and immigration risk, negative-ROI fields become catastrophically negative
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference field against FRREOP data: CS/Engineering are reliably positive; Education, Arts, Social Sciences, Humanities are frequently negative; Business/MBA is highly variable

decision_factors.factor: Advisor job placement record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In humanities, the advisor's letters and network relationships with hiring committees are critical mechanisms for academic job placement — prestige alone does not substitute for active field connections
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the advisor directly: 'How many students have you placed into tenure-track or visiting positions in the past 5 years?' Cross-check with current students

decision_factors.factor: Internal funding deadline calendar
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Internal awards like OGS close before program application deadlines — missing them permanently forfeits funding that cannot be reapplied for mid-year
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Contact department graduate coordinator directly in early fall; ask explicitly for all scholarship deadlines for incoming students, not just the application deadline

decision_factors.factor: Field (STEM vs. humanities/social sciences)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM PhD stipends in Canada ($22,000-$45,000+) vastly exceed humanities stipends ($17,000-$28,000); the risk of funding gaps in years 5+ is concentrated in non-STEM fields
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the typical stipend range for the specific department and field, not just the university average

decision_factors.factor: Province of study and PNP stream availability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Graduating from Ontario or BC unlocks specific PhD graduate PNP streams with no job offer requirement, adding 600 CRS points and near-guaranteeing PR — graduating from provinces without such streams forces reliance on Express Entry CEC alone
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check OINP Ontario PhD Graduate Stream and BCPNP International Post-Graduate Category eligibility criteria for your specific institution before choosing a program

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's internship philosophy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor who discourages internships structurally disadvantages industry-track students regardless of other program strengths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly during visits; listen for specificity (names companies) vs. vagueness or discouragement

decision_factors.factor: Personal psychological risk profile
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Individual vulnerability to advisor toxicity varies substantially; the same environment that is survivable for one person is harmful for another
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly assess history of anxiety or depression, tendency to internalize criticism, need for explicit validation, and prior experience navigating toxic professional dynamics

decision_factors.factor: Alignment on dissertation scope and timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If co-advisors want different versions of your dissertation or different completion timelines, you will spend years reconciling their feedback rather than doing research
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask each advisor independently what a completed dissertation looks like and when they expect you to finish; surface divergence before committing

decision_factors.factor: Program location relative to target job market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: OPT job search must occur within a limited post-graduation window; proximity to employer density and alumni networks creates a structural advantage that cannot be replicated by applicant quality alone
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map the program's location against target employer presence; check whether major employers in your sector conduct on-campus recruiting at the program

decision_factors.factor: Research output produced during the MS
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even a single first-authored abstract, conference poster, or working paper demonstrably improves PhD application competitiveness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current MS students in the program whether they have produced any publishable or conference-ready work during the program

decision_factors.factor: Advisor relationship requirement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Thesis MS requires securing and maintaining an advisor — this introduces risk (advisor fit, availability, research direction) that coursework MS does not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Before committing to a thesis MS program, identify 2–3 faculty whose research aligns with yours and assess their availability to take new MS students

decision_factors.factor: Existence of a real competing offer with a specific number
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A concrete competing offer with a specific dollar amount is the single most effective negotiation lever; without it, requests for more money have little traction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate honestly whether you have an actual competing offer at a higher amount that you are genuinely considering accepting

decision_factors.factor: Publication authorship pattern
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether students appear as first authors indicates whether the advisor is developing independent researchers or extracting labor under their own name
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search the advisor's recent publications and check author order — consistent first-authored student papers versus advisor-first-authored papers on all work

decision_factors.factor: Funding contingency level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Funding contingent on advisor grants, competitive fellowship renewal, or TA position availability creates financial anxiety that compounds research anxiety; students with stable multi-year funding have one fewer major stressor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: Is funding guaranteed for the full program duration? What is the funding source — advisor grants, institutional fellowships, TA lines? What happens to funding if the advisor loses a grant?

decision_factors.factor: Department policy on advisor departure and bridge funding
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines what safety net exists if your advisor leaves; departments without clear policies leave students vulnerable to funding gaps and administrative limbo
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the DGS directly: 'What is your policy if a student's advisor leaves or is denied tenure?' Vague answers are a negative signal

decision_factors.factor: Time-to-degree
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Average completion in 4 years vs. 7 years is a massive difference in opportunity cost, earning years, and immigration timeline
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the department directly for median time-to-degree data; ask current students how long peers typically take

decision_factors.factor: Opportunity cost of the gap year
decision_factors.why_it_matters: One year foregone equals lost stipend income ($30K–$40K), lost research productivity, delayed career progression, and emotional cost of extended uncertainty — these are often underweighted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Model the dollar cost explicitly; also assess whether you can tolerate another year of limbo psychologically and socially

decision_factors.factor: Funding structure: employment contract vs. stipend vs. scholarship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employment contracts (Germany, Netherlands, Sweden, many EU countries) include social security contributions, benefits, and legal worker protections; stipends do not — this affects financial security, healthcare access, and long-term immigration point accumulation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly whether the PhD position is a Arbeitsvertrag/employment contract or a scholarship; verify whether social insurance contributions are included

decision_factors.factor: Program-specific employer pipeline to H-1B sponsors
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A program's value for international students is not its ranking but whether it places graduates at companies large enough and willing enough to sponsor H-1B
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask admissions or current students which specific companies recruited on campus in the last 2 years; cross-check those companies against USCIS H-1B disclosure data to confirm sponsorship history

decision_factors.factor: Program prestige and institutional affiliation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unlike STEM, humanities hiring committees filter by institutional affiliation at early screening stages — being from a top-10 program materially changes your probability of getting an academic job
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look at where tenure-track faculty at programs you aspire to work at received their PhDs; assess whether your target program appears in those hiring outcomes

decision_factors.factor: Funding structure composition (RA vs. TA vs. fellowship vs. external award)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The source and stability of funding differs significantly — RA funding is tied to supervisor grant health, TA funding is tied to teaching availability, fellowships and external awards are portable and not grant-dependent
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask supervisor directly: 'Do you have RA funding available for incoming students?' and 'What is the typical funding structure for your PhD students?'; ask to speak with a current student about their funding experience

decision_factors.factor: TAship hours requirement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: TAships supplement income but consume research time; heavy TAship loads (15+ hours/week) significantly delay thesis completion and extend time-to-degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current students how many hours per week TAships actually require vs. stated hours; ask if TAing is mandatory or optional

decision_factors.factor: Target industry and its geographic concentration
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Certain industries (specific finance sectors, VC, entertainment) are heavily concentrated in the US with limited Canadian equivalents — choosing Canada locks you out of those ecosystems regardless of immigration efficiency
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your target roles and companies; determine what fraction are US-only vs. available in Toronto or Vancouver

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's industry research partnerships and consulting relationships
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Active industry collaborations create internship pipelines, co-authored publications with industry researchers, and warm introductions to hiring managers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'Do you have active research collaborations with industry labs? Which ones?' and verify against advisor's recent publications and acknowledgments

decision_factors.factor: Boundedness of the difficult behavior
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A single bounded difficult behavior (harsh writing feedback) is more predictable and manageable than a globally toxic personality (volatility, exploitation, gaslighting)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Through former student interviews, identify whether the negative behavior is consistent and specific or variable and wide-ranging across relationship dimensions

decision_factors.factor: Complementarity vs. competition of expertise
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Complementary expertise adds without creating conflict; overlapping or competing expertise creates disagreements about research direction dressed as methodological feedback
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map each advisor's domain and methods expertise; check whether their contributions would address different gaps in your work rather than the same ones

decision_factors.factor: STEM Designated Degree Program status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the degree qualifies for 36-month STEM OPT extension versus standard 12-month OPT — a 24-month difference in legally authorized post-graduation work time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify the specific degree program's presence on the official STEM Designated Degree Program List; do not assume STEM OPT based on program subject area alone

decision_factors.factor: Institution research reputation in the relevant field
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An MS thesis from a strong research university carries more weight with PhD admissions than one from a teaching-focused institution, even if thesis quality is similar
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check faculty publication records, PhD placement rates of MS graduates, and whether the institution has active funded research labs in your area

decision_factors.factor: Breadth vs. depth preference
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Coursework MS provides breadth across many subfields; thesis MS narrows you to one research area — this affects both job market optionality and intellectual fit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you know what subfield you want to work in? If yes, depth (thesis) is viable. If you are still exploring, breadth (coursework) reduces premature specialization risk.

decision_factors.factor: Field-specific funding structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM programs funded by advisor grants have more stipend flexibility; humanities programs with flat cohort stipends have almost none; professional programs routinely negotiate merit scholarships
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the field's dominant funding model before entering any negotiation and calibrate expectations accordingly

decision_factors.factor: Research direction clarity in the applicant
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Committees reject vague applicants because they cannot match them to specific faculty; clarity enables the local matching mechanism that drives admission decisions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Can you articulate one specific research problem you want to work on and name 2–3 faculty whose current projects connect to it?

decision_factors.factor: Program attrition rate and time-to-degree variance
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High attrition (above 30%) and wide time-to-degree variance signal advisor-dependent outcomes and structural program problems that affect all students
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the DGS for attrition data; look at time-to-degree distribution (not just average); speak with students in later years of the program about their progress trajectory

decision_factors.factor: International student visa implications of program disruption
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Advisor departure creates visa complications (I-20 transfer, SEVIS coverage gaps, OPT timeline shifts) that domestic students don't face, making the same disruption more costly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask prospective advisor explicitly what would happen to your visa and OPT timeline if they left mid-program; assess whether they have thought through this scenario

decision_factors.factor: Program location relative to target job market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Proximity to employer hubs creates structural recruiting advantages — especially critical for international students with OPT deadlines
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map program location against target employer geography; ask alumni about recruiting pipeline access and internship frequency

decision_factors.factor: Whether prestige motivation is verified or assumed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Most prestige-motivated reapplication decisions are based on untested assumptions about whether ranking translates to better outcomes for a specific role
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Speak with graduates of the offer-in-hand program about their outcomes; verify whether your specific target role (academic job, industry research) actually requires the higher-ranked program

decision_factors.factor: Research project flexibility vs. fixedness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: UK and many EU PhDs admit students to execute pre-defined projects; US and Canadian programs typically allow students to develop their own direction — misalignment between student's desire for intellectual autonomy and program structure causes dropout and dissatisfaction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the supervisor directly: 'Is the research project fixed, or is there scope for me to develop my own direction within it?'; cross-check with current students in the lab

decision_factors.factor: True total cost including opportunity cost
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The break-even timeline — and therefore whether ROI is achievable within a realistic US employment window — depends on total real cost, not sticker tuition
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate: tuition + 2 years living expenses + foregone salary (what you would earn in your home country or current job during those 2 years)

decision_factors.factor: Advisor manuscript return speed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Slow feedback directly extends time-to-degree, which translates into unfunded years — this is one of the most concrete operational predictors of how long you will actually take to finish
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current advisees: 'How long does it typically take to get feedback on a dissertation chapter?' — anything over 3 months is a red flag

decision_factors.factor: Study permit processing timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students, a study permit takes 3–4 months to process and is tied to the specific institution and program — late application or program switching creates legal work authorization gaps
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count backward from program start date; ensure permit application submitted 3–4 months prior; confirm current processing times with IRCC

decision_factors.factor: Supervisor grant stability and funding track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In Canada, most non-Tri-Council PhD funding flows through supervisor research grants; a supervisor with expiring or thin grants is a direct financial risk to the student
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the supervisor directly about grant status and renewal timeline; check NSERC/CIHR/SSHRC public databases for recent awards to the supervisor

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency or learnability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French adds 15-50 CRS points — a high-ROI investment that can be the difference between receiving an ITA or waiting for draws to lower; also opens Quebec-specific pathways
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess existing French background; estimate realistic CLB level achievable with 3-6 months of study; calculate CRS impact using IRCC calculator

decision_factors.factor: Subfield choice within CS
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Industry demand and academic job market competitiveness vary dramatically by subfield — ML/AI has extreme industry demand but also the most competitive academic market; theory has moderate industry demand
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference the subfield table: ML/AI/NLP have highest industry demand; theory has moderate industry demand; HCI has moderate demand in both tracks

decision_factors.factor: Whether the placement advantage is driven by advisor letters
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the prestige premium depends on strong advocacy letters, students who have strained relationships with their advisor may not receive them, neutralizing the key benefit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask former students whether the advisor wrote strong, personalized advocacy letters or pro forma letters, and whether the quality correlated with relationship quality

decision_factors.factor: Whether both advisors are actively funded
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If both have active grants, co-advising provides a funding safety net; if neither is reliably funded, co-advising multiplies rather than mitigates financial risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask about current and upcoming grant cycles for both advisors; check public grant databases if available

decision_factors.factor: Industry placement track record for international students
decision_factors.why_it_matters: General placement statistics may not reflect outcomes for international students specifically, who face visa sponsorship requirements that narrow the eligible employer pool
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly for placement data broken out by visa status or international student outcomes; speak to current international students about their job search experience

decision_factors.factor: Career destination: whether PhD is actually required
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Many high-compensation careers (industry ML engineer, data scientist, senior software engineer) rarely require a PhD; pursuing a stepping-stone MS for these roles is financially irrational
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review job postings at target employers for your specific role; check LinkedIn profiles of people in those roles to see what credentials they hold

decision_factors.factor: Program duration and time-to-market
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Coursework MS is 1 year FT vs. 1.5–2 years for thesis MS — for international students with visa timelines or opportunity costs, this difference is material
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate the total cost difference (tuition + living expenses + lost income) of the additional 0.5–1 year and weigh against the PhD or R&D career benefit

decision_factors.factor: Advisor responsiveness and student funding history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor who has let students experience funding gaps signals either poor grant management or low investment in student welfare — both predict difficult PhD experiences
decision_factors.how_to_assess: During the visit, ask current students directly: 'Have you ever had a funding gap or scare during your PhD?'

decision_factors.factor: Prior research experience and methods training
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Committees evaluate readiness for doctoral research — prior research experience is the primary evidence of readiness, not GPA or coursework alone
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have supervised thesis, research assistantship, or independent project experience with clear outputs (papers, reports, presentations)

decision_factors.factor: Prestige advantage concreteness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prestige is frequently cited as justification for accepting a difficult advisor, but the advantage is often based on reputation rather than actual placement outcomes — a mismatch that leads applicants to overweight prestige
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check where the advisor's graduates from the last 5–7 years actually landed; verify whether those outcomes match your specific career goals; distinguish 'brilliant reputation' from 'students get the outcomes I want'

decision_factors.factor: Student's year in program at time of potential advisor departure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students in years 1–3 bear the highest cost of disruption; students in years 4–6 are often close enough to completion to weather it
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate whether the advisor's tenure review timeline overlaps with your first three years in the program

decision_factors.factor: Alumni network strength in target industry or geography
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Strong alumni networks actively help graduates find jobs; weak networks leave students to self-navigate a cold market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the department where alumni are; search LinkedIn for program alumni in your target role or geography; ask current students if alumni are responsive

decision_factors.factor: Immigration and visa status for international students
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A gap year for international students may require leaving the US or navigating visa status complications that US domestic applicants don't face
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine OPT remaining time; if OPT is available, a US-based gap year RA position is feasible; if not, assess whether home-country work and reapplication is viable

decision_factors.factor: Academic job market geography
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US PhD programs have structural advantages for US academic placements through network effects, recommendation letter weight, and conference visibility; European PhD holders face friction when competing for US academic jobs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review the placement record of the specific program (not just university prestige); ask where graduates in the last 5 cohorts ended up; distinguish between 'some graduates got academic jobs' and 'graduates got jobs at institutions comparable to your target'

decision_factors.factor: Existing employer relationship with sponsorship intent
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A student with a pre-existing employer who has committed to sponsoring H-1B bypasses the lottery dependency risk that invalidates most international MS ROI calculations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm in writing — not verbally — whether the employer will sponsor; verbal commitments from managers who cannot authorize HR policy are not reliable

decision_factors.factor: Advisor advising load and administrative roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor in a senior administrative role (chair, dean) or advising too many students simultaneously cannot read manuscripts promptly, reducing effective advising quality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask how many students the advisor is currently advising and whether they hold significant administrative responsibilities; ask whether they are actively taking new students

decision_factors.factor: U15 membership and institutional research infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The 15 major research universities vary significantly in funding culture, international student support, and immigration infrastructure — smaller institutions outside this group may offer different tradeoffs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether target institution is a U15 member; research immigration support services, international student population size, and industry/government research partnerships

decision_factors.factor: CAD/USD exchange rate impact for international students
decision_factors.why_it_matters: International students sending remittances home or comparing Canadian offers to US offers must account for the ~25-27% CAD discount against USD
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Convert all Canadian stipend figures to USD at current exchange rate (~0.73-0.75) before comparing to US program offers

decision_factors.factor: Salary differential between US and Canadian PhD positions
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US PhD stipends are generally higher in USD terms than Canadian CAD equivalents — the immigration certainty of Canada comes at a cost of lower income during the PhD and potentially post-PhD
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare specific program stipend offers in purchasing power parity terms; factor in cost of living differences between specific cities

decision_factors.factor: Existence of formal co-supervision programs at target industry labs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Represents a structurally distinct and potentially superior path for industry research goals — faster timelines, supplemented compensation, applied research
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research Google Brain Residency, Meta AI Research programs, Microsoft Research PhD fellowships, OpenAI collaborations before defaulting to standard programs

decision_factors.factor: Visibility of failed students — those who left, took much longer, or left academia unexpectedly
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The true success rate of an advisor can only be assessed against the full population of students who entered, not just the visible survivors
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Actively search LinkedIn and alumni lists for former lab members who left without finishing or who departed academia despite stated intentions; contact them directly

decision_factors.factor: Milestone requirements across departments
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Co-advisors from different departments may operate under different qualifying exam, proposal, and defense standards — ambiguity at these moments can stall or derail progress
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Before starting, clarify in writing what the milestone requirements are and have both advisors agree on a single standard

decision_factors.factor: Average time-to-degree and funding in later years
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Programs that offer strong first-year funding packages but do not guarantee funding in years 4–6 create financial risk exactly when students are most vulnerable — near completion but not yet graduated
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly what funding looks like in years 4, 5, and 6 of the program; ask current students how funding continuity has worked in practice

decision_factors.factor: Financial cost relative to expected salary delta
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 43% of master's programs yield negative financial returns; total real cost of an unfunded MS can reach $80,000–$200,000, which may not be recovered in fields with modest salary premiums
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate total cost including tuition, living expenses, and foregone salary opportunity cost; compare against median salary increase in target field within a 3–5 year recovery window

decision_factors.factor: GRE requirement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Thesis MS programs more commonly require GRE scores; coursework MS programs less often — this affects application feasibility for students with weak standardized test profiles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check each program's admissions requirements page explicitly; do not assume one track's requirements apply to the other

decision_factors.factor: Whether teaching requirements are negotiable in humanities
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In humanities, stipend flexibility is low but which years require teaching — and how much — is often negotiable and directly affects research productivity and time-to-degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the DGS: 'Which years require teaching assignments, and is there any flexibility in structuring that?'

decision_factors.factor: Letter quality and specificity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Committees read letters as informal peer reviews — vague letters from prominent but distant writers provide less signal than specific letters from direct supervisors
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether the writer supervised your actual research work and can name specific contributions and capabilities

decision_factors.factor: DGS engagement level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An engaged Director of Graduate Studies who knows students by name and research area provides a meaningful escalation pathway and accountability check on advisor behavior; a purely administrative DGS leaves students without recourse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: During visits, observe whether the DGS references specific students by name; ask students whether they feel comfortable going to the DGS with problems; ask what happens when advisor-student relationships break down

decision_factors.factor: Advisor accessibility and mentoring bandwidth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pre-tenure advisors under grant pressure may have unpredictable availability; high stress can create difficult lab environments despite good intentions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current students privately: 'How available is [Advisor] week to week?' and 'Has lab stress affected the working environment?'

decision_factors.factor: Program ranking
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Matters specifically for academic hiring pipelines, elite consulting/finance recruiting, and home-country brand recognition — not for most industry careers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether your specific career target (academic vs. industry vs. home country) is one where rank is a real screening filter

decision_factors.factor: Feasibility of securing a high-quality RA position
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The value of a gap year is only as high as the quality of what you produce in it — an RA position under a PI who writes strong letters is the highest-ROI gap year use
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify specific PIs with active grants who hire post-bacc RAs; lab manager and research coordinator roles at medical schools and research universities are the most accessible pathways

decision_factors.factor: Stipend in purchasing-power-adjusted terms
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Raw stipend comparisons are misleading; CAD $25K in Halifax has different purchasing power than USD $30K in Boston or £20K in London
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate monthly take-home after taxes and mandatory deductions; compare against local rent for a single person; assess whether stipend covers living costs without supplemental work

decision_factors.factor: Viability of Plan B without H-1B
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Because ~60% of STEM OPT holders statistically exhaust H-1B attempts, a student without a credible alternative path is taking a 60% chance of an unplanned outcome
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate concretely: Canadian graduate stream PR eligibility, home country job market with US MS credential, third-country options — vague 'I'll figure it out' is not a plan

decision_factors.factor: External fellowship infrastructure (Mellon, ACLS, Woodrow Wilson, FLAS)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: External fellowships are the primary mechanism for funding the years beyond the departmental guarantee — programs with strong track records of student fellowship success have better funded completion rates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'How many students currently hold external dissertation fellowships?' and 'Does the department have a completion fellowship for ABD students close to finishing?'

decision_factors.factor: Expected time to completion by field
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM PhDs in Canada complete in 5–6 years from a master's; humanities/social sciences run 6–8 years — this affects cumulative funding exposure, immigration timeline, and career entry age
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask department for median time-to-completion data by program; cross-reference with funding guarantee period (typically 4–5 years) to identify funding cliff risk

decision_factors.factor: Healthcare cost savings vs. US equivalent
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian provincial health coverage eliminates $2,000-$6,000/year in health insurance costs that US PhD students face; this meaningfully adjusts real purchasing power comparisons
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check provincial health plan costs for international students (e.g., Ontario UHIP ~$756/year, BC MSP subsidized); subtract from US health insurance cost to compute benefit

decision_factors.factor: Quebec vs. non-Quebec province placement
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Quebec operates a separate immigration system; Express Entry CEC does not apply, French is near-mandatory, and a separate CSQ process is required — this dramatically changes the PR pathway compared to other provinces
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine if program is in Quebec; if so, research CSQ Program Experience stream and assess French language requirements honestly

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's h-index and academic network breadth (for academic track)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Authoritative recommendation letters from well-networked advisors are a prerequisite for competitive academic hiring committee access
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check h-index in the subfield; ask how many hiring committee relationships the advisor has across institutions; assess grant history for funding runway

decision_factors.factor: Durability of prestige premium to target career path
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The value of an advisor's name recognition decays rapidly in non-academic careers, changing the cost-benefit tradeoff over time
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether people in your specific target role 5+ years post-graduation report that their advisor's name still affects their career outcomes

decision_factors.factor: Whether the co-advising arrangement is formal or informal
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Informal arrangements carry no institutional accountability structures — no paperwork, no formal role assignment, no program-level oversight
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether there is formal paperwork designating both as co-advisors of record; treat 'informal' as a red flag requiring further investigation

decision_factors.factor: Advisor contingency plan if advisor leaves mid-degree
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If an advisor leaves the university, student funding and research support may be disrupted or terminated, potentially stranding the student mid-degree
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program coordinator and the advisor directly what the policy is if a student's primary advisor departs; assess whether the department has a strong enough faculty bench for reassignment

decision_factors.factor: Topic overlap between MS thesis and target PhD research area
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PhD applications are evaluated on research fit; a thesis on an unrelated topic provides weaker fit evidence than a directly relevant one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your MS thesis topic against the stated research interests of faculty at target PhD programs; count how many faculty are working in adjacent areas

decision_factors.factor: Program ranking
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Matters for signaling and network access but is overweighted relative to advisor fit — a lower-ranked program with an excellent advisor produces better outcomes than a top-ranked program with a negligent one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use ranking as a tiebreaker after advisor fit, funding, and placement record are evaluated

decision_factors.factor: Availability of graduate-specific mental health resources
decision_factors.why_it_matters: General university counseling pools (shared with undergraduates) have long wait times and limited graduate student expertise; dedicated PhD counseling resources indicate institutional recognition of the structural problem
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask specifically whether there are graduate-student-only counseling slots, not just whether the university has a CAPS; ask current students whether they have used these resources and found them accessible

decision_factors.factor: Student's own independent intellectual thread
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students whose work is fully embedded in an advisor's project are more vulnerable to advisor departure; students with their own intellectual identity can continue through transitions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether your proposed research could exist independently of the advisor's specific grant or project trajectory

decision_factors.factor: Advisor-to-student ratio
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how much individual mentorship attention you will actually receive during the PhD
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count current PhD students in the advisor's lab; ask current students how often they meet with the advisor one-on-one

decision_factors.factor: MSCA mobility requirement compatibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: MSCA DN positions require that applicants have not resided in the host country for 12+ months in the past 3 years — students who have already studied or worked in the target country are ineligible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify residency history against MSCA eligibility rules before investing time in MSCA applications

decision_factors.factor: Annual salary premium of MS over next-best alternative
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The break-even timeline is salary premium divided into total cost — a small premium means the student must remain employed in the US for many years to recover investment
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research median salary for your specific role with and without MS in your target geography; do not use national averages if you are targeting a specific metro

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's subfield alignment with your project
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In humanities, advisor prestige matters less if their work does not speak directly to yours — their conceptual guidance and letter credibility are weakened if they are tangential to your project
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the advisor's recent publications; assess whether their methodological and topical concerns overlap meaningfully with your proposed project — not just the same period or region

decision_factors.factor: Opportunity cost calculation (especially for SWE-bound students)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 4–5 years of stipend ($32K–$40K/yr) vs. industry SWE salary ($150K–$200K/yr) represents $500K–$600K pretax foregone earnings
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate explicitly: multiply years-in-program by delta between stipend and market SWE salary; compare against realistic PhD premium for target role

decision_factors.factor: Type of funding mechanism (RA vs. TA vs. Fellowship)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RA ties your degree work to the advisor's grant and research agenda; TA trades research time for teaching stability; fellowships provide independence but are rare and have eligibility restrictions for international students
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the offer letter carefully to identify the specific funding mechanism; ask what percentage of students in the program receive each type and how funding typically transitions across years

decision_factors.factor: Application portfolio balance
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Applying only to reach schools risks complete rejection in a bad year; applying without fit wastes resources and admission chances
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether portfolio contains 2–3 ambitious targets, 4–5 realistic fits, and 2–3 safeties with strong faculty match

decision_factors.factor: Department culture
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Collegial, collaborative departments produce better student outcomes and more tolerable multi-year experiences; toxic cultures cause attrition and mental health costs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Visit if possible; observe seminar attendance and faculty-student interaction; speak privately with current PhD students without the advisor present

decision_factors.factor: Employment rate specific to that program cohort
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 44.6% average international student employment rate means some programs perform far worse; program-level data reveals actual pipeline strength
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request cohort-specific 6-month employment data from the program; if they cannot or will not provide it, that itself is signal

decision_factors.factor: Alternative career path realism
decision_factors.why_it_matters: With tenure-track placement rates of 30–50% even from top programs, a 9-year degree commitment requires modeling non-academic outcomes explicitly — this changes whether and where to apply
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research what alumni from the program who did not get tenure-track jobs are doing now; assess whether those outcomes are acceptable to you before committing

decision_factors.factor: Teaching assistant experience (academic vs. industry track)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: TA experience is an asset for academic track (demonstrates teaching competency for faculty applications); it is not a meaningful differentiator for industry research roles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether TA requirements serve or distract from your target track

decision_factors.factor: Career target specificity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A clearly defined industry career target may not require a PhD and may be better served by a 2-year MS with strong industry placement, while a research or academic career target strongly favors PhD
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify specific job titles you want within 5 years and research whether those roles require a PhD, prefer a PhD, or are equally accessible with an MS

decision_factors.factor: Cost of living relative to stipend
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The same dollar stipend produces dramatically different quality of life and savings depending on location — affects financial stress over 5–6 years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare stipend amount against city cost-of-living index; ask current students whether they can live comfortably on the stipend

decision_factors.factor: Immigration pathway viability (for international students)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 9-year degree with a geographically constrained academic job search creates compounding immigration uncertainty — OPT, H-1B timing, and work authorization all interact with an unpredictable job market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For Canadian programs: confirm PGWP eligibility for PhD graduates (3 years open work authorization); for US programs: map out realistic visa timelines against projected degree completion

decision_factors.factor: International student support infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: International students face unique bureaucratic, linguistic, and cultural challenges — strong ISSS and ESL resources reduce friction and risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check university ISSS website quality and responsiveness; ask international students about visa support experiences; assess community diversity in the department

decision_factors.factor: Subfield-specific reputation vs. overall rank
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Academic hiring is subfield-specific — a department ranked 20th overall but 5th in your subfield may yield better academic outcomes than the reverse
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look at subfield-specific rankings (e.g., CSRankings.org for CS, PGR for philosophy); check where subfield faculty publish and are cited

decision_factors.factor: MS vs. PhD structural funding difference
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The difference between a funded PhD and an unfunded MS can be $150,000–$200,000 in total cost — the largest financial variable in the decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether each program offers tuition waiver plus stipend or is tuition-paying; calculate total 2-year MS cost vs. 5-year PhD net income

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's active grant funding status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When a PI's grant ends, the student typically falls back on TA funding, which consumes 20+ hours per week on teaching and dramatically slows research progress
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly about current and upcoming grant cycles before joining a lab; check NSF/NIH award databases for grant expiration dates; ask current students whether they are on RA or TA
decision_factors._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

decision_factors.factor: Email timing relative to advisor's recruiting calendar
decision_factors.why_it_matters: CS advisors often informally commit recruiting slots during summer, months before official deadlines; late outreach finds a closed door regardless of applicant quality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Work backward from application deadline; aim for 3–6 months prior. If the deadline is December, July–September is the target window
decision_factors._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor grant funding stability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RA funding for PhD students typically comes directly from the advisor's grants; if a grant expires, the student may lose their stipend or be forced to switch projects or advisors mid-program
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search NIH Reporter (for biomedical/health fields) or NSF Award Search (for engineering/sciences) using the advisor's name; identify active grants and their end dates relative to the student's expected graduation
decision_factors._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

decision_factors.factor: Existing domain connections and LinkedIn relationships before outreach
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pre-existing connections in a field collapse the cold email requirement — targeted outreach to 5-6 known-position professors can outperform 300 cold emails in speed and yield
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count how many researchers in your target subfield you have meaningfully interacted with (conferences, LinkedIn, co-authorship) before beginning outreach

decision_factors.factor: Geographic flexibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Academic positions are sparse and location-specific; willingness to relocate dramatically expands viable options, while geographic constraints make academic careers near-impossible in most fields
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: am I willing to move anywhere in the country — or internationally — for a position, with no veto on location? If the honest answer is no, academic career viability drops sharply

decision_factors.factor: Availability and terms of unfunded extensions
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a student who needs more time than the funded period can continue without catastrophic financial or academic consequences
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the department directly: how often are extensions granted, are any funded, and what are the late submission fee structures

decision_factors.factor: Advisor feedback style (harsh vs. constructive)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Negative feedback from mentors was cited by 34% of students as a cause of depression; it exacerbates existing self-criticism and can compound into motivation loss and delayed graduation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current PhD students in the lab: 'How does the advisor respond to failed experiments or rejected manuscripts?' Look for emotional vocabulary in their answers, not just logistical ones

decision_factors.factor: Whether you received interview invitations in the prior cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Interview invitations confirm your profile clears basic admissions thresholds; zero interviews after two or more cycles suggests fundamental profile misalignment that a gap year alone is unlikely to fix
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review your full application cycle record — did any program invite you to interview, even informally?

decision_factors.factor: Advisor publication network (insular vs. broadly collaborative)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor who only publishes with their own students cannot connect you to the broader academic community, limiting your professional network and future collaborations at the moment you need them most — job market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search the advisor on Google Scholar; manually check the last 10–15 co-authors and identify what percentage are current or former students vs. peers at other institutions

decision_factors.factor: Intended career geography post-PhD
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The advantages of domestic vs. overseas PhD are almost entirely contingent on where the person plans to work — the two systems optimize for different outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: Do I plan to work in China, abroad, or am I genuinely undecided? Domestic PhD advantages (network, system knowledge, guanxi) only activate if returning to China
decision_factors._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor availability and student quota
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A professor may be a perfect research fit but have no open slots, making the application futile regardless of qualifications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Direct email outreach before or during application season to ask explicitly about availability
decision_factors._source: zhihu_海外PhD申请中_如何选择导师.txt

decision_factors.factor: Professor rank and career stage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Assistant professors (especially non-Chinese, non-Indian AP) have more time, more need for students, less cold-email volume, and are more likely to evaluate applicants on potential rather than credentials alone; full professors have fewer open slots and higher credential thresholds
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check department page for rank designation; check personal website for years since PhD and current lab size (8-10+ students = likely full, harder to get in)
decision_factors._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor funding and open slots
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Identified by the most detailed commenter as one of only two variables that actually determine admission — without funding, research fit is irrelevant
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check recent grants, lab website news, and ask directly in the email whether the advisor is currently recruiting
decision_factors._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

decision_factors.factor: PhD student funding source: department-funded (TA model) vs. PI-funded (RA model)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how much influence an individual professor has over admissions decisions — PI-funded systems give professors near-decisive power; department-funded systems route decisions through a committee where no single professor dominates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look at program website for funding structure; email current students; check whether the application asks you to name specific advisors; ask if students can freely switch advisors after enrollment
decision_factors._source: zhihu_美国的PhD是都需要套磁吗.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor and program quality
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple commenters identify this as the single most important variable — a weak advisor or program negates most of the PhD's long-term benefits
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research advisor's publication record, lab alumni placement (faculty vs. industry research vs. engineering), and whether the advisor has industry connections that enable internships
decision_factors._source: zhihu_计算机视觉读博还是工作.txt

decision_factors.factor: Intrinsic motivation for research vs. instrumental motivation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students motivated by avoiding the job market or by credential accumulation are more likely to experience misery during the PhD and worse outcomes at graduation than those with genuine research drive
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: would you pursue this research if the credential and salary were identical to a master's degree? If the answer requires significant hedging, motivation is likely instrumental

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's publication velocity and student authorship patterns
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A lab producing 3-4 papers per year with students as first authors signals active mentorship and fundable research — the inverse predicts slow progress and weak job market outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the advisor's Google Scholar for recent papers and look specifically at whether students appear as first authors; ask current or former students directly
decision_factors._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of research match demonstrated in the email
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Generic interest signals the applicant has not read the advisor's work; specific method/problem/limitation framing signals genuine intellectual engagement and saves the professor time evaluating fit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test: can the email only have been written for this specific professor, or could the name be swapped with any other? If swappable, it is too generic
decision_factors._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

decision_factors.factor: Funding guarantee structure (departmental vs. advisor's grant)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Department-guaranteed multi-year funding is stable regardless of individual advisor grant outcomes; advisor-grant-dependent funding creates vulnerability if the grant lapses or is not renewed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: 'Is the stipend guaranteed by the department for multiple years, or does it depend on your current grant funding?' — comment [6] provides exact language and confirms this is not considered an awkward question
decision_factors._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

decision_factors.factor: Whether the professor's lab is actively hiring
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Emailing a professor with no open positions or no active grant funding wastes both parties' time regardless of email quality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check lab website for hiring announcements, review recent grant disclosures, look for recently published papers with open author slots

decision_factors.factor: Timeline tolerance for financial and career uncertainty
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Academic career paths require 5-7 years post-PhD of postdoc uncertainty before knowing if the career is viable; industry offers earlier stability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess personal financial obligations, family situation, and psychological tolerance for multi-year ambiguity with no guaranteed outcome

decision_factors.factor: Supervisor responsiveness and advocacy behavior
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Multiple students note that supervisor compassion — not institutional support — was what kept them going; supervisors who actively advocate can reduce fees and obtain extensions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test response time during application (did PI respond to a one-week consideration request?); ask current students whether the PI has gone to bat for them with administration

decision_factors.factor: Lab/program structure (meeting frequency, milestone clarity)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unstructured research was cited by 38% of depressed PhD students; depression impairs executive function, and unstructured environments create a catastrophic combination — no external deadlines means no recovery scaffold
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'How often do you meet with your advisor one-on-one?' and 'Are there formal milestone check-ins outside of the dissertation committee?'

decision_factors.factor: Whether you can identify a specific, correctable weakness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A gap year only produces ROI if it closes a real gap; if you don't know what failed, additional time is likely to be unfocused and admissions outcomes may not improve
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have you received feedback from a rejecting program or faculty member that named a specific deficiency? If not, that diagnosis step must come first

decision_factors.factor: Documented advisor behavior patterns (broken promises, student departures, disorganization)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: These patterns directly predict PhD completion risk; a disorganized advisor who makes and breaks commitments is a structural blocker to graduation, not a manageable inconvenience
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask former students directly about advisor reliability; check attrition rate from the lab; ask the advisor about former students and what they are doing now

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's domestic network density
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In Chinese academia, the advisor's network directly enables student outcomes: job placement, thesis defense committee composition, publication access, and conference invitations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research how many of the advisor's former students are now faculty or in leadership positions at target institutions; check if advisor holds editorial roles at relevant journals
decision_factors._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

decision_factors.factor: Professor's national/cultural background
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The top answer argues that Chinese and Indian APs prioritize publications and undergraduate institution prestige above other factors and have the highest cold-email volume; non-Asian Western APs are described as more likely to evaluate potential and unique strengths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review professor's personal website, lab page, and hiring patterns of current students; note whether the lab page says 'self-motivated' (Chinese AP signal) vs. describes mentorship or training
decision_factors._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

decision_factors.factor: Applicant research background strength
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Identified alongside funding as the second of only two real decision variables — publications, research experience, and demonstrated competence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate own publication record, research output quality, lab affiliations, and whether experience overlaps with target advisor's current work
decision_factors._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

decision_factors.factor: Whether the target professor is on the admissions committee
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A professor who both wants you and sits on the committee can directly advocate during review, dramatically increasing your odds; a professor outside the committee has indirect influence at best
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check departmental governance pages or ask directly in your outreach email whether the professor is involved in admissions decisions
decision_factors._source: zhihu_美国的PhD是都需要套磁吗.txt

decision_factors.factor: Post-PhD immigration pathway
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A US PhD in AI/CV creates a credible EB-1A/EB-1B green card pathway that bypasses H-1B lottery; this dramatically changes long-term US career stability for international students
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the research field and expected publication/citation profile would support an extraordinary ability petition; consult alumni who have gone through EB-1 process
decision_factors._source: zhihu_计算机视觉读博还是工作.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's track record of placing students in target roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor with no history or incentive to help with job placement will not suddenly develop that incentive for a new student; the labor extraction dynamic described in the source is structural
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Find 3–5 past graduates of the specific advisor and check their current positions; ask directly during lab visits what the advisor does to support student job searches

decision_factors.factor: DGS disposition toward students vs. faculty in advisor conflicts
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The DGS controls the formal advisor-change process; a DGS who sides with faculty can create bureaucratic obstacles that trap a student or delay the switch significantly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask senior students or recent graduates how the DGS has handled past advisor conflicts; look for patterns in how long students stay with problematic advisors in the department
decision_factors._source: academia_读博第三年换导师全过程记录_给后来人参考.txt

decision_factors.factor: Whether the professor has stated a preference against unsolicited email
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Emailing a professor who has explicitly asked not to be contacted cold can actively hurt the application by creating a negative first impression
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the faculty webpage fully before sending; look for explicit statements about contact preferences
decision_factors._source: phd_application_套磁经验分享_发了60封邮件_8个回复_3个offer.txt

decision_factors.factor: Advisor meeting frequency and communication responsiveness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Infrequent meetings and slow email responses during the PhD translate directly to slower research progress, delayed feedback, and reduced mentorship — the original poster's advisor met with them once per semester and took 2 weeks to reply to emails
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current lab members how often the advisor meets one-on-one; ask the advisor directly about their preferred communication cadence; observe response time to your own pre-enrollment emails as a proxy
decision_factors._source: phd_application_选导师比选学校重要100倍_我的血泪教训.txt

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of research alignment between applicant and professor
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A personalized email that references a specific paper and demonstrates genuine research alignment is described as worth more than 20 copy-pasted messages
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Can you name a specific paper published in the last 2-3 years, describe what it found, and explain how your work connects to it? If not, alignment is insufficient

decision_factors.factor: Intrinsic motivation source — specialization vs. breadth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Academia rewards deep, narrow specialization in a single research question over decades; industry rewards problem diversity and fast feedback — misalignment causes burnout in either direction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: is the research question itself the end, or is it a tool for solving problems? If the question is the end, academia fits better; if it is a tool, industry fits better

decision_factors.factor: Lab culture around failure and null results
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students whose research produces null results face added psychological burden if the lab or department treats null results as failures rather than normal science
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current lab members how the PI responds when experiments don't produce publishable results; ask whether students have successfully defended theses with inconclusive findings

decision_factors.factor: Institutional mental health leave policy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: None of the 4 UK students interviewed received adequate institutional support during crises; the gap between policy and practice can mean losing funding or program standing during a mental health episode
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the graduate coordinator directly: 'If a student needs to take medical or mental health leave, what happens to their stipend, health insurance, and program standing?'

decision_factors.factor: Field type — STEM vs. non-STEM
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For STEM fields, targeted research experience in a gap year has demonstrably high ROI; for humanities and social sciences, funding competition is fierce regardless of additional experience, making the marginal improvement lower
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your field's admissions committees explicitly reward post-baccalaureate research experience in the way STEM programs do, or whether publications and writing samples are the primary signal

decision_factors.factor: Program TA load and structural use of PhD students
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Programs that systematically overload PhD students with teaching are trading student research progress for departmental instructional coverage — this extends time-to-degree and delays publications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask current students how many courses they TA per semester, whether this changes after the first year, and whether RA funding options exist as an alternative

decision_factors.factor: English academic writing and communication proficiency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Commenters across multiple answers agree that English writing ability is a long-term career constraint for researchers — more so than students initially expect
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current English writing level honestly; if weak, an overseas PhD environment provides structural improvement; domestic PhD does not
decision_factors._source: zhihu_国内读博和国外读博的优劣各在那些方面.txt

decision_factors.factor: Current lab size
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A lab with 8-10+ students has little capacity to add more; a lab with 0-3 students is actively seeking people
