warning_signs: Cold emails sent from a @qq.com, @163.com, or @126.com address
No response after two weeks despite professor being known to reply to others
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Writing an overly long email with too many attachments in the first contact
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students want to give maximum information to maximize chances; confuse thoroughness with effectiveness
failure_patterns.consequence: Email is flagged as spam by mail servers or ignored due to cognitive load — professor does not respond
warning_signs: Email exceeds four paragraphs in first contact
Multiple attachments included in initial outreach
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Counting on a 'pre-PhD apprenticeship' arrangement (effectively unpaid lab work in exchange for a future admission slot)
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Supply of PhD applicants exceeds slots; advisors exploit the queue by offering informal labor arrangements with vague future promises
failure_patterns.consequence: Student works for 1–3 years with no formal enrollment, no guaranteed admission, no income, and no recourse if the advisor withdraws the informal promise
warning_signs: Advisor uses language like 'when there's a spot' or 'you're definitely on my list'
Arrangement has no written contract or formal institutional status

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating an encouraging reply ('strongly encourage you to apply') as a near-certain admission signal and reducing application effort
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The language feels unusually strong and personal; applicants want to believe the positive signal is real and reduce anxiety by anchoring on it
failure_patterns.consequence: The top answer explicitly states this is template language used by many professors regardless of actual interest level — applicants who reduce their application pool based on this signal may end up without competitive alternatives
warning_signs: Professor's reply uses 'strongly encourage' or 'feel free to mention me in your statement'
Applicant receives this reply early in the cycle before application review has begun
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_申请国外_PhD_的时候如何与教授套磁.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Generic praise of the professor without demonstrating knowledge of their specific work
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students follow templates that include flattery but do not invest time in reading the professor's actual papers
failure_patterns.consequence: Professor recognizes the generic framing, infers low genuine interest, and deprioritizes the application
warning_signs: Email references 'your impressive research' without naming a specific paper or finding
Research fit paragraph is identical across emails sent to multiple professors
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_申请国外博士如何与教授_套磁.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant completed more than 36 months of full-time doctoral study by December 31 of the application year?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the doctoral study duration eligibility cap for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for CGRS-D; no further assessment needed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes this eligibility threshold; proceed to other criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant have a minimum A− (80%) average over the preceding two full-time years of study?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Basic academic eligibility threshold for OGS
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to assess citizenship/immigration status and enrollment status
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is ineligible for OGS regardless of other qualifications

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a US citizen, national, or permanent resident?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Ford Foundation, and Hertz Foundation fellowships
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to evaluate enrollment duration and field eligibility for specific federal fellowship programs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is excluded from all major US federal fellowship programs; focus on institutional fellowships, home country funding, and field-specific non-citizenship-restricted awards

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the prior award disqualification condition applicable to both CGRS-D and Vanier
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for both CGRS-D and Vanier
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes this eligibility threshold; proceed to other criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant enrolled full-time at an Ontario university?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Enrollment status eligibility requirement for OGS
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm citizenship/immigration status eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is ineligible for OGS; part-time enrollment disqualifies

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant been enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at the time of NSF GRFP application?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: NSF GRFP enrollment-duration eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for NSF GRFP; assess whether second-year window was already used
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant may be eligible; confirm no prior federal fellowship receipt

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously submitted three or more CGRS-D (or predecessor CGS-D/PGS-D/SSHRC Doctoral Fellowship) applications?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the three-application lifetime limit for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant has exhausted lifetime eligibility for CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant has remaining lifetime applications; proceed to evaluate application content

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or international student on a valid study permit?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Citizenship/immigration eligibility for OGS
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If international student on study permit, confirm whether the institution has an international OGS allocation and its size (typically 15–30%)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is ineligible for OGS

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously received a federal graduate fellowship?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: NSF GRFP prior-award disqualification criterion
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for NSF GRFP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Prior-award criterion does not bar application; proceed to other eligibility checks

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person, or an international student?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant competes in the main pool or within the 15% international student allocation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Domestic applicant competes in main pool
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: International applicant is limited to 15% allocation; verify whether the relevant agency includes international students in that allocation

diagnostic_questions.question: How many OGS awards has the applicant previously received at their current level of study (master's or doctoral)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has reached the OGS award cap (2 at master's level, 4 at doctoral level)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If at or above the cap, applicant is ineligible for further OGS awards at that level
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If below the cap, applicant may proceed with application

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the CIP code of the degree program the international student is considering, and is it on the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for 24-month STEM OPT extension, which determines total post-graduation work authorization (12 months vs. 36 months)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student is eligible for STEM OPT extension; standard OPT 12 months + STEM OPT 24 months = 36 months total
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student limited to 12 months standard OPT; immigration planning must account for shorter work authorization window

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the applicant's primary research discipline — natural sciences/engineering, social sciences/humanities/arts, or health sciences?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which Tri-Council agency (NSERC, SSHRC, or CIHR) administers the application
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Match to appropriate agency and confirm single-agency submission
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: For interdisciplinary applicants, require selection of primary discipline before submission

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant currently in or beyond the 3rd year of master's study, or the 6th year of doctoral study?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has exceeded the year-of-study eligibility cutoff for OGS
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for OGS based on year-of-study restriction
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant remains within the eligible study period

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the department treat GRFP stipend as additive or substitutive relative to the standard funding package?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Net financial benefit of GRFP to the student; determines whether GRFP award translates into higher actual compensation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: GRFP is additive; student receives full GRFP stipend on top of standard package
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: GRFP is substitutive; student receives no net financial gain from GRFP award beyond potentially freeing up negotiating leverage on non-stipend dimensions

diagnostic_questions.question: For Vanier: Has the applicant completed more than 20 months of full-time doctoral study as of May 1 of the application year?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests the doctoral study duration eligibility cap specific to Vanier, which is narrower than CGRS-D
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for Vanier; may still be eligible for CGRS-D if within 36-month window
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant passes Vanier eligibility threshold; confirm institution is willing and able to nominate

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant currently hold any other Ontario government student assistance?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the combination restriction would disqualify the applicant from holding OGS in the same period
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant cannot hold OGS simultaneously; must choose between OGS and the other Ontario government assistance
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: No combination restriction applies; applicant may proceed

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant's field on the NDSEG eligible fields list?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: NDSEG fellowship eligibility; only specific enumerated STEM fields qualify
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may be eligible for NDSEG if also a US citizen or national (not permanent resident)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is ineligible for NDSEG regardless of citizenship

diagnostic_questions.question: For Vanier: Does the applicant's institution have available nomination slots, and has the department confirmed willingness to nominate the candidate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests whether the institutional nomination gate is accessible to the student
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate may proceed with nomination process through institution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate cannot access Vanier regardless of academic qualifications; no alternative self-application route exists

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a STEM student at an Ontario university considering both OGS and QEII-GSST?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the mutual exclusivity rule between OGS and QEII-GSST applies
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant must choose one award; confirm which is available at their specific institution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: QEII-GSST mutual exclusivity rule does not apply; OGS rules apply independently

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the target PhD program have institutional fellowships not tied to citizenship status?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether international students have access to non-RA/TA funding that domestic students access through federal fellowships
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: International student may be able to partially close the fellowship funding gap relative to domestic peers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: International student is dependent entirely on RA/TA funding with no fellowship supplement; negotiate accordingly

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant hold a Tri-Council award (CGRS-D, Vanier, CGS-M, or equivalent)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant benefits from the 2024 federal budget stipend increases
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is eligible for new stipend levels (PhD: CAD $40,000/year; postdoc: CAD $70,000/year)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant funded through supervisor grants is excluded from the 2024 budget increase

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the institution have a specific international student allocation for OGS, and what is its size?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The effective competition pool for international applicants, which may be substantially smaller than the domestic pool
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Assess the applicant's competitiveness within the international allocation (typically 15–30% of total); confirm by contacting the institution's graduate studies office
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no international allocation exists, international students on study permits may be ineligible at that institution

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant an immigrant or child of immigrants who is a permanent resident or US citizen?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship for New Americans, which is one of the few prestigious fellowships accessible to eligible immigrants
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may qualify for Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship; verify specific eligibility criteria
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Soros Fellowship is not available; focus on other eligible fellowship categories

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the applicant self-identify as a Black student researcher?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for the reserved pool of up to 10 additional CGRS-D awards for Black student researchers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant should self-identify in the application to be considered for the dedicated award pool
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant competes in the general pool; no access to the reserved 10 awards

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a CGRS-D holder at an Ontario university seeking OGS as a top-up?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether OGS stacking is available on top of CGRS-D, which is institution-dependent
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm with the institution's graduate studies office whether OGS top-up is permitted for CGRS-D holders at that institution
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Standard OGS eligibility rules apply without CGRS-D stacking considerations

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant Indigenous?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the applicant may receive consideration beyond standard institutional quotas under CGRS-D special provisions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may be considered outside institutional quota limits; confirm this provision applies to the relevant agency stream
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant subject to standard institutional quota rules

diagnostic_questions.question: What province is the target institution located in?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which provincial award programs are available; award landscape differs significantly by province
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Ontario: OGS and QEII-GSST apply. If BC: BC Graduate Scholarship and BC PNP International Post-Graduate Category. If Quebec: FRQSC/FRQNT. If Alberta: Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship and Alberta Innovates. If Atlantic: limited provincial funding; federal awards are relatively more important.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Not applicable — province is always determinable

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you spoken with a student currently in year 4 or 5 of the specific lab you are considering joining?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has accessed the most predictive information source about advisor behavior during the highest-risk phase of the PhD
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What did that student say about advisor availability, credit attribution, and what happens when students are struggling?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The evaluation of the advisor is based on publicly visible signals (publications, rankings) that are orthogonal to mentorship quality; the most important data is missing

diagnostic_questions.question: How often does your prospective advisor meet one-on-one with PhD students, and what does that typically look like in a given week?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you will have adequate mentoring access — the single most predictive structural variable for PhD success and satisfaction given that 50% of students receive under one hour per week
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they claim frequent meetings, ask current students independently to verify — ask 'how often do you actually sit down with your advisor one-on-one?'
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If meeting frequency is low or vague, ask what the alternative feedback mechanisms are — does the lab have senior PhD students or postdocs who provide day-to-day mentorship?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your primary career goal — academic faculty position, industry role, or are you genuinely uncertain?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student's field and program selection is calibrated to a realistic outcome or to a minority outcome that requires explicit above-average program performance to achieve
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If academic: ask which field, then cross-reference that field's current academic placement rate and 20-year trend from NSF SED data
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If industry or uncertain: assess whether the chosen field has low-friction industry transition (CS/Engineering) or high-friction transition (biology, humanities) and whether the student has modeled that cost

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the 10-year completion rate for the specific program you are considering?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has investigated structural program quality beyond reputation; and whether the program is transparent about attrition
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is the rate above 60%? If below, has the program given a specific explanation and shown evidence of improvement?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is making a major commitment without knowing whether most students who start actually finish; this is a critical information gap

diagnostic_questions.question: Has anyone in the lab or department changed advisors in the last three years, and what was that process like?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the program has functional advisor accountability and whether students have a real exit option if the relationship deteriorates — relevant given that 25% of students would change advisors retrospectively
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask whether the student who changed advisors was able to stay in the program and whether it delayed their degree — this reveals whether the exit option is real or theoretical
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Absence of any advisor changes in a large program may indicate either a healthy culture or a culture where students feel unable to raise concerns — probe which by asking about formal grievance mechanisms

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you know what percentage of graduates from your target program obtained tenure-track faculty positions in the last 5 years?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has done program-level due diligence versus relying on reputation, rankings, or advisor anecdote — and whether the program is above or below the 30% national benchmark threshold
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they know: verify whether the number is above 30% (above-average) and whether it is tenure-track specifically or includes all academic positions including postdocs and adjunct roles
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they don't know: this is a critical data gap; they are making a major life decision without the most directly relevant outcome metric for their stated goal

diagnostic_questions.question: What does your funding package guarantee, and what has the program told you happens to students after the guaranteed period ends?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant understands the funding cliff and has a concrete plan for the 2-3 year gap between guaranteed funding end and statistical completion
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is there documented evidence of teaching assistantships, grants, or fellowships that bridge the gap? Or is the answer vague?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is operating on an implicit assumption that they will finish within the funded period, which contradicts national median data

diagnostic_questions.question: What percentage of PhD graduates from this program over the last five years are in faculty positions versus industry versus other careers?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the program's career outcomes match your goals and whether the program is honest about the academic job market's limits
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they provide data, ask whether career support for non-academic paths is proactive or reactive — do they run industry workshops or only help students who individually ask?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they cannot or will not provide placement data, treat that as a signal that outcomes are poor or that career support is not tracked — both are red flags

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you accounted for postdoc years in your financial and career timeline planning, and do you know the postdoc rate in your specific field?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands that in biology (57.8%), geosciences (64.2%), and physical sciences (46.5%) the postdoc is structurally mandatory, not optional, and adds 3-5 years to time-to-career
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: ask whether their financial planning, visa situation, and personal timeline can sustain 10-12 years from bachelor's to independent career at postdoc-level salary
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: this is a fundamental planning error; recalculate time-to-career and financial requirements before committing to the program

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the program have a formal ombudsperson or student advocate who is independent of faculty?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether there is institutional infrastructure to handle advisor relationship problems without requiring direct confrontation; programs without this concentrate all power in the advisor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you been told how to access this person and under what circumstances they can intervene?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the advisor relationship deteriorates, the only options are direct confrontation (retaliation risk) or leaving; this significantly increases vulnerability

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you personally used the campus mental health services, and if so, did you find them useful?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether institutional mental health resources function in practice — given that only 26% of users found institutional support helpful, direct user experience from current students is far more informative than program descriptions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask specifically what made it helpful or unhelpful — wait times, therapist familiarity with PhD-specific stress, and session limits are the most predictive variables
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask what they would do if they were struggling — their answer reveals what the real support infrastructure is, which is often informal peer networks rather than formal services

diagnostic_questions.question: When did your primary advisor or role model enter academia, and have you cross-referenced their career advice against current NSF or equivalent placement data?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is relying on potentially outdated guidance from an advisor whose academic hiring experience predates the major structural shift in the market (pre-2010 especially)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they have cross-referenced: assess whether they understand the 20-year trend and have adjusted their planning accordingly
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they haven't: the student may be making decisions based on a mental model that is 15-20 years out of date, when academic placements were 20 percentage points higher than today

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you planning to rely solely on your primary advisor for mentorship, or do you have a plan for building additional mentoring relationships?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands single-advisor dependency risk and has or will build a multi-mentor support structure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have specific co-advisors, engaged committee members, or peer mentors been identified? Are they already in relationship with the student?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The student is entering a single-point-of-failure structure; if the primary advisor relationship fails, there is no backup network and attrition risk is substantially higher

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there a mandatory thesis committee with annual reviews that involves faculty other than your primary advisor?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether there is structural oversight of the advisor-student relationship — programs without independent committee oversight have no mechanism to catch or correct advisor mismanagement or bullying
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask whether the committee is truly independent or whether advisors effectively control committee composition and whether students can raise concerns with committee members privately
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If there is no mandatory independent committee, the advisor has near-total power over the student's academic fate — this amplifies the risk of the 21% bullying rate with supervisor as perpetrator

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your contingency plan if you do not obtain an academic position, and has your target program structured support for non-academic career paths?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has a realistic fallback that accounts for field-specific transition friction, or whether the contingency is vague and unmodeled — and whether the program actively supports or culturally discourages non-academic paths
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they have a specific plan: evaluate whether it accounts for retraining costs in biology, identity/cultural shift in humanities, or whether it is seamless as in CS/Engineering
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no plan: in fields where academic placement is now below 30-34%, the contingency is not a backup scenario but a near-majority outcome that requires as much planning as the primary path

diagnostic_questions.question: For underrepresented students: Has any faculty member in the program explicitly acknowledged your background — national origin, gender, first-generation status — as relevant to your graduate experience?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the program and advisor have the awareness and practice of identity-affirming mentorship that the National Academies identifies as predictive of retention for underrepresented students
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Was this acknowledgment superficial (diversity statement) or substantive (specific conversation about how your background might affect your experience and how they will support you)?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The student may be entering an environment where structural mentorship gaps for underrepresented students exist and are unnamed; risk of later internalizing those gaps as personal failure is high

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the definite commitment rate for graduates in your target field at graduation — not eventual employment, but committed plans on the day of degree conferral?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The actual baseline probability of having a clear next step at graduation, which is the most honest signal of career risk in the field
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they know: check whether they understand that humanities (65.8%) and biomedical (68.2%) mean more than 1 in 3 graduates face genuine uncertainty at graduation, and have planned for that scenario
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they don't know: introduce this as the most direct available metric of graduation-day career risk, more honest than vague 'employment rate' figures that programs typically advertise

diagnostic_questions.question: What field are you entering, and have you looked at the median time-to-degree for that field specifically?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student's timeline expectations are calibrated to field-specific data; humanities/social science (8.4-9.5 years) vs. STEM (5-6 years) have dramatically different financial and visa exposure profiles
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Has the student built a financial and visa plan that accounts for the median, not the best-case, completion timeline?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The student is likely underestimating time-to-degree based on program marketing or best-case examples, creating a future financial and immigration planning gap

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you already contacted specific professors at your target Canadian schools, and have any responded positively?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands the supervisor-first nature of Canadian PhD admissions and how far along they are in the actual (informal) admissions process
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you asked about RA funding availability and requested to speak with a current student in the lab?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is your target start date? If it is less than 6 months away, you may have already missed the window for the current cycle.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is any portion of your offered PhD funding contingent on winning an external competition like OGS or CGRS-D?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Distinguishes between guaranteed income and aspirational package; determines real financial floor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is your guaranteed annual funding if you win zero external awards? Is that amount enough to live on in your program city?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is the full amount guaranteed for all years of the program, or only the first 2-3 years?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your country of birth?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the US employment-based green card path is viable or catastrophically backlogged — the single most important variable in Canada vs. US PhD immigration decision
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If India or China: immediately model the EB-2/EB-3 priority date backlog; Canadian PhD path has a dramatically stronger immigration ROI
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If from a country with short EB queues (e.g., most of Europe, Latin America outside Mexico): US path may be viable; evaluate on research quality and career goals rather than immigration alone

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your actual target role — faculty position, research scientist at an AI lab, applied scientist, or software engineer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student needs academic-track or industry-track optimization, or whether a PhD is appropriate at all
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If faculty: Are you targeting top-5 research universities or are you open to a range? This determines how much program rank should dominate your decision.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If SWE: Have you calculated the opportunity cost of 4–5 years at stipend vs. market salary, and do you understand the PhD premium is marginal or negative for SWE roles?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you identify any former students who were in this lab for 2+ years and did not finish, or who finished but left academia unexpectedly?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the prospective student has investigated the full outcome distribution or only the visible success stories
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What did those students say when you contacted them directly, and what reasons did they give?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you actively looked — using LinkedIn, department alumni lists, and your own network — or have you only encountered the students who were referred to you?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have your two prospective co-advisors co-advised a PhD student before, and what happened to that student?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the pair has resolved their working relationship in practice, not just in theory — and whether there is a track record of student outcomes to evaluate
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask to speak with that student if possible; ask whether the student finished on time and whether the arrangement was additive or burdensome
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Treat yourself as the first experiment; probe harder on role division, conflict resolution, and funding structure to compensate for the absence of prior evidence

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this program fully funded — meaning tuition covered plus a living stipend — or will you be paying tuition?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands the full financial structure of their offer and whether they are comparing programs on a like-for-like financial basis
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the funding mechanism (RA, TA, fellowship), and have you confirmed what happens to funding in years 4–6?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do you have the financial resources to cover tuition and living expenses, and have you modeled the return on investment if OPT job conversion is delayed?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you want a PhD eventually, or is the master's your final credential?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the program must produce research evidence (stepping stone) or whether a strong employer pipeline matters more (terminal)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is your target PhD program in the US, and does it typically admit directly from bachelor's or require a prior master's?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Does your target career actually require an MS, or is the credential optional for the roles you are targeting?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your intended next step after completing this MS — industry role, PhD program, or R&D/research scientist position?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: This is the primary fork that determines which MS track is appropriate; the two tracks are optimized for different destinations
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If industry: Is breadth across subfields more valuable than depth in one? If so, coursework MS is likely the right fit.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If PhD or R&D: Does your current or planned MS program include a thesis, RA position, or publishable research output? If not, why not?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is your stipend funded by an RA position from your prospective advisor's grant, or by a TA position from the department?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: RA funding gives the advisor discretion to supplement the stipend from grant funds; TA funding fixed by union contract is not negotiable regardless of competing offers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If RA-funded: ask what the ceiling on stipend supplementation is from the grant, and whether summer RA funding is available
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If TA-funded: shift negotiation focus to non-stipend items — conference travel, start date, coursework waivers, which years require teaching

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name a specific research problem you want to work on — not a field, but a problem?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has the research direction clarity needed to match with faculty and write a credible SOP; vague answers indicate the application will fail the initial faculty-matching screen
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Can you name 2–3 faculty members whose current projects connect to that problem, and have you read their recent papers?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do you need to delay application by one cycle to gain more research experience and clarify direction, or can you develop this specificity in the next 2–3 months?

diagnostic_questions.question: How do you feel about your progress day-to-day — not your research results, but your sense of whether you know what you're doing and where you're headed?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Distinguishes students with functional advising (who can articulate a sense of direction even amid uncertainty) from students experiencing Ghost or Perfectionist Blocker advising (who have chronic directionlessness or stuck-ness)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What does your advisor do that helps you maintain that sense of direction?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How long have you felt that way, and what have you tried to address it?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your prospective advisor's faculty rank?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether institutional departure risk exists at all; 'Assistant Professor' means pre-tenure, 'Associate' or 'Full' means tenured
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Assistant Professor: how many years have they been at the institution, and when is their tenure review?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Associate or Full: tenure risk is essentially eliminated — shift evaluation to research fit, lab culture, and funding

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your intended career outcome — academic research, US industry, or returning to your home country?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which decision variables (ranking, advisor network, location, brand recognition) are actually relevant to this person's situation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If academic: Which specific subfield, and have you identified faculty whose active research directly overlaps with your interest?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If industry or home country: Have you checked actual alumni placement data in that sector, not just assumed prestige transfers?

diagnostic_questions.question: What specifically caused your application to fall short of your target outcome?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the gap is fixable in a year and whether reapplication is likely to produce a different result
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Which of the fixable causes applies — research experience, faculty contact, or application focus? What concrete step in the gap year addresses it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the cause is not clearly identified, the reapplication strategy is not yet defined — stop and diagnose before making a decision

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your country of birth, and have you checked the current USCIS Visa Bulletin priority dates for EB-2/EB-3 for your nationality?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has quantified the actual immigration timeline under a US PhD path — this single factor can shift the entire country comparison for Indian and Chinese nationals
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How many years until your priority date would be current, and how does that compare to the Canadian Express Entry timeline?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Before comparing program stipends or rankings, look up the current cutoff date — if you are Indian or Chinese, this may be the most important variable in your decision

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the exact CIP code for this program, and have you verified it is on the DHS STEM OPT Designated Degree Program List?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student will have 12 or 36 months of work authorization, which determines how many H-1B attempts they get and fundamentally changes the immigration risk profile
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you confirmed this with the DSO in writing, not just from the program website?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is the single most important verification to do before accepting admission — do you have the DSO's contact information to check this week?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this applicant coming from a STEM background or a STEM-dominant advising environment?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether they are likely applying STEM-logic defaults (advisor-first, grant-funding model) to a humanities application context where those defaults produce wrong decisions
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Walk through the structural differences explicitly — especially that humanities advisors do not control funding and that department-level questions are the primary financial evaluation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Check whether they have received humanities-specific advice or are still relying on generic PhD application guides that embed STEM assumptions

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a written funding commitment from your supervisor or institution, or only a verbal assurance?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is exposed to the risk of arriving in Canada without confirmed financial support
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the written commitment specify the funding source (RA, TA, fellowship), the annual amount, and the guaranteed duration?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do not accept the offer until you have this in writing — Canadian PhD funding is not program-guaranteed the way many US funded PhDs are.

diagnostic_questions.question: What city is the program in, and what is the current market rent for a 1BR apartment there?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the stipend is livable or merely nominal; city choice dramatically affects financial stress regardless of stipend level
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you calculated your post-tax monthly stipend and compared it to current rental listings on Rentals.ca or Craigslist?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you haven't researched current rents, your budget assumptions may be based on outdated or national average data that understates costs in Toronto and Vancouver

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have any French language background, and have you taken the TEF or TCF?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals an untapped CRS points opportunity — even moderate French can add 15-50 points, which may be the difference between receiving an ITA or not
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: calculate exact CRS impact at their current French CLB level and at CLB 7+; assess whether preparation investment is worthwhile
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no French background: deprioritize unless willing to invest 6+ months in study; focus on other CRS boosters like job offer or PNP

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you looked up the last 5 PhD graduates of your prospective advisor on LinkedIn to see where they actually work and in what roles?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is evaluating advisors on verifiable placement reality vs. claimed reputation or h-index
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the ratio of research scientist vs. SWE/product roles? Are those research roles at top labs (Google Brain, OpenAI, FAIR) or at less prominent research positions?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is the single most actionable research step — do this before accepting any offer; claimed connections vs. verifiable placement history are very different signals.

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a history of anxiety, depression, or interpersonal stress that significantly affects your functioning?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The individual's psychological risk profile for a toxic advisor dynamic, which is a primary variable in predicting personal outcome
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Do you have external support structures — therapist, strong personal network — that would remain accessible and stable throughout a PhD program?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you previously navigated a sustained high-stakes toxic professional dynamic, and what did that experience reveal about your resilience?

diagnostic_questions.question: What does a completed dissertation in this area look like to each of you?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the two advisors have compatible visions for the scope, methods, and contribution of your work — or whether you will be mediating between two incompatible research agendas
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If answers align, ask about timeline alignment and publication venue preferences to stress-test further
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If answers diverge significantly, ask directly how they resolve disagreements about research direction — the quality of that answer determines whether the divergence is manageable

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you verified the potential advisor's current funding status and looked up where their last 5 graduated students are now?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is evaluating the advisor as an operational mentor and career launcher versus evaluating them solely on academic reputation or paper quality
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What did you find, and did you speak to any of those former students directly?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is the single highest-leverage due diligence action for a PhD admit — what is preventing you from doing it before your decision deadline?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the specific research weakness in your PhD application that the MS is intended to fix?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Distinguishes between applicants with a clear strategic plan and those using the MS as an emotional response to rejection
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the specific MS program you are considering directly address that weakness through thesis research, or only through coursework?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The MS is likely being pursued as a consolation rather than as a targeted fix; risk of repeating the same outcome is high

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your current or planned MS program require a thesis, or is it coursework-only?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the degree will produce research evidence for PhD applications or only coursework credentials
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If thesis required: Have you identified a potential thesis advisor and confirmed their availability to take MS students?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If coursework-only: Do you have a plan to generate research output independently (RA position, independent study, faculty collaboration) alongside the coursework?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the stated stipend cover 9 months or 12 months?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines the true annualized value of the offer and whether you face recurring summer funding uncertainty for the duration of the PhD
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 12 months: confirm in writing that this is guaranteed, not contingent on annual grant renewal
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If 9 months: ask how current students fund summers, whether summer RA support is typically available from the advisor's grant, and what happens if no summer funding is secured

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you talked to current or former PhD students of your target advisors?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has done the actual due diligence required to assess advising quality, or is relying entirely on public reputation signals
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What did they say about meeting frequency, research autonomy, and whether they would choose the same advisor again?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is non-negotiable — what is preventing you from reaching out, and how do you plan to get this information before committing?

diagnostic_questions.question: What do you do when you're having a hard week research-wise — is there a person you go to, and who is that?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals whether the support structure exists and whether the advisor is accessible as a support resource; students with toxic advisors typically name peers, family, or external resources — not their advisor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How responsive is that person, and do you feel like you can bring real problems to them?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What has made it hard to find support within the program?

diagnostic_questions.question: Has your prospective advisor graduated any PhD students?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the advisor has demonstrated the core capability of guiding someone to completion, and whether you would be a first-cohort beta student
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How many, and how long did it take? Were completions on a normal timeline or extended?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you comfortable being the first person this advisor has ever guided through the full PhD process, with no proven template for your mentorship?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you verified the funding status of any PhD offer you've received — specifically whether the stipend is guaranteed for multiple years or contingent on the advisor's grant renewals?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the student understands the difference between a secure multi-year funding commitment and a precarious year-to-year offer
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If guaranteed: Is the guarantee at the department level or advisor level, and what happens if you switch advisors?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If not verified: Treat this as urgent — contact the department and ask directly before accepting

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the offer you're holding funded with a full stipend, or are you being asked to self-fund?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether accepting is financially viable and whether declining is a meaningful sacrifice or a rational pass
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: A funded offer with advisor match is a high bar to clear with a reapplication — verify your reapplication case is strong before declining
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: An unfunded or self-pay offer is a strong signal to reapply or pursue other options; accepting a self-pay PhD without a plan is rarely the right call

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a specific research question you want to investigate, or are you still exploring what you want to study?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is ready for a UK/EU research-only PhD structure or needs the coursework and exploration period built into US/Canadian programs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you identified specific supervisors working on that exact question whose recent publications align with your proposed approach?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: A UK or EU PhD where you begin research on day one is likely a poor fit — consider US or Canadian programs with coursework phases, or do a master's first to develop research focus

diagnostic_questions.question: What country were you born in?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether long-term US permanent residency through employment is a realistic outcome within a career timeframe — for Indian and Chinese nationals, it is not
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If India or China: have you modeled your career assuming you will be on H-1B status indefinitely with no green card, and does that scenario still make the MS worthwhile?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If other country: what are current EB priority dates for your country, and how does that affect your long-term US residency timeline?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the applicant's career goal — tenure-track academic position specifically, or a broader set of outcomes?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines how much program prestige and advisor placement record should dominate the decision versus other factors; also determines whether the 9-year time-to-degree and geographic job market constraint are acceptable
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Academic career as primary goal — then program rank, advisor placement record, and external fellowship infrastructure should dominate the evaluation; advise them to research MLA/AHA placement data by program
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Non-academic career acceptable — then evaluate whether the specific subfield credential and publication profile produced by the program are legible to target non-academic employers, and whether 9 years is worth the investment for those outcomes

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you checked the internal funding deadlines (OGS, institutional awards) at your target institutions, not just the program application deadline?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is at risk of missing the earlier funding competitions that close months before the formal application deadline
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you already submitted or prepared materials for those competitions, or only noted the dates?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Contact the graduate coordinator immediately and ask for all scholarship deadlines for incoming students — if it is past October and you haven't applied, you may have already missed OGS for this cycle.

diagnostic_questions.question: What field are you entering — STEM, social sciences, or humanities?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Field is a major predictor of funding level and funding gap risk; humanities students face structurally different financial conditions than STEM students at the same university
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If STEM: Is your supervisor's grant recently renewed or mid-cycle? If humanities: Is funding guaranteed beyond year 3?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: N/A — answer is categorical

diagnostic_questions.question: Which Canadian province will you study in — and have you checked that province's specific PNP streams for PhD graduates?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether a 600-point PNP nomination pathway exists with no job offer requirement, and whether the student is studying in Quebec (requiring a completely different immigration strategy)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Ontario or BC: immediately evaluate OINP Ontario PhD Graduate Stream and BCPNP International Post-Graduate Category eligibility requirements
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Quebec or province without PhD-specific PNP: must rely on Express Entry CEC or occupation-specific streams; assess CRS score competitiveness realistically

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you directly asked your prospective advisor what their philosophy on student internships is?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the advisor is academic-track or industry-track oriented, and whether they will actively support or passively obstruct internship access
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Did they name specific companies proactively, or were they vague or discouraging? Specificity signals real pipeline; vagueness or discouragement signals academic-track orientation.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask this question explicitly — it is the single clearest diagnostic of advisor track orientation and should not be inferred indirectly

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this advisor genuinely the only viable option for your specific research problem, or are they simply the best available option among several viable ones?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the research uniqueness argument is genuine or is a motivated rationalization for a prestige-driven choice
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is this specific research problem your genuine life's work, or is it one of several directions you find compelling?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How much would working with the next-best advisor actually compromise your research goals in practice?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is my funding departmentally guaranteed, or does it depend on both of your grants?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student faces doubled grant-cycle risk with no clear accountable party for funding continuity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If departmentally guaranteed, confirm the duration and conditions; ask whether RA obligations attached to each grant could still create competing demands on your time
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If grant-dependent, ask what happened to funding for previous co-advised students when grants lapsed and who took responsibility for finding a solution

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you genuinely want to do research as a practice, or are you pursuing a PhD primarily for immigration stability, prestige, or because you are unsure what else to do?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The root motivation for PhD pursuit — which determines whether the student is likely to sustain the commitment through the slow, frustrating middle years of a PhD
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you already done research and found it intrinsically engaging, or is your interest primarily based on expectation rather than experience?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you fully explored whether a well-placed MS program would better serve your actual career and immigration goals with less risk and in less time?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the MS program thesis-based or coursework-only?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Immediately filters whether the program can produce the research evidence that PhD admissions committees need
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you identified a specific faculty advisor you would work with, and do they take MS students on active funded research projects?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: For PhD stepping stone purposes, this program is likely insufficient; for terminal career goals, assess whether employer pipeline justifies the cost

diagnostic_questions.question: If your MS program has a 'project option,' have you confirmed with target PhD programs whether that project counts as research experience?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Identifies whether the student is operating on an assumption vs. verified information about how their credentials will be evaluated
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If confirmed: Which PhD programs explicitly accepted it and which did not?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If not confirmed: This verification should happen before committing to the project track if PhD admission is the goal.

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a real competing offer with a specific dollar amount that you are genuinely considering?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether you have actual leverage for stipend negotiation; without a real competing number, stipend requests are easy to decline
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: use the specific number in negotiation, mention it in a follow-up after expressing initial enthusiasm, and ask each program explicitly what they can do
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: shift negotiation strategy toward non-stipend items (travel, start date, waivers) and focus on gathering information rather than extracting concessions

diagnostic_questions.question: Where did your target advisor's last 5 PhD graduates go after completing their degrees?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant has evaluated the advisor's actual track record of developing researchers, or is assessing the advisor purely by reputation and publications
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Do those outcomes match your intended career path (academia, industry, specific sectors)?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This placement data is publicly available — the absence of this research suggests the applicant is optimizing for the wrong signals

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you tell me about a student who left the program or left this lab in the last few years — what happened to them?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Directly accesses departure information and tests whether the culture treats attrition as discussable or as a taboo topic; evasion or dismissal of this question is itself a signal
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Was their experience typical, or was it unusual compared to most students here?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is that something people don't really talk about here?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your prospective advisor have active funded grants, and have you verified this independently?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Both your stipend stability and the institutional friction against the advisor voluntarily departing; unfunded advisors have both financial incentive and structural freedom to leave
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: When do the grants expire, and are there renewal cycles during your expected program years?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is your funding source if not from advisor grants, and what does the department guarantee in writing if that funding ends?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you considering paying for an unfunded MS? If so, have you evaluated whether a funded PhD in the same field is achievable given your profile?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Identifies whether the student is making a $150,000+ financial decision without exploring the funded alternative
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If PhD is achievable: What is the specific barrier preventing you from applying to funded PhD programs — timeline, research experience, or something else?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If PhD is not achievable: What is the employment outcome data for the specific MS program you're considering, and what is your plan during OPT?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can you name the specific advisor at your target program you want to work with, and have you engaged with their recent work?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the desire to reapply is driven by genuine fit with a specific mentor or by generic prestige-seeking
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you made contact or had meaningful intellectual exchange with that advisor? What is the realistic probability they have bandwidth for a new student?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you cannot name a specific advisor, the reapplication motivation is likely prestige-based rather than fit-based — interrogate whether prestige is actually predictive of your target career outcome

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you verified that the UK PhD funding you are applying for explicitly lists international students as eligible?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has caught the UK funding eligibility trap before investing significant application effort
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Which funding mechanism specifically — UKRI, university scholarship, Industrial CASE, Commonwealth — and have you confirmed this in writing with the department?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Stop application preparation until you receive explicit written confirmation of international eligibility; do not rely on the advertisement text alone

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your total cost including living expenses and foregone salary — not just tuition?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has done a realistic ROI calculation or is anchoring on the sticker price and underestimating the true investment by 50-150%
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the annual salary premium you expect from the MS over your next-best alternative, and how many years of US employment does that require to break even?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Calculate: tuition + living for program duration + what you would have earned working instead — that is your real investment figure

diagnostic_questions.question: What percentage of students in the program's most recent 3 cohorts finished within the guaranteed funding window?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The most concrete indicator of how realistic the program's funding model is relative to actual completion behavior — programs where most students exceed the funding window are implicitly promising less than the offer letter suggests
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Most finish within the window — ask what distinguishes those students (fellowship support, advisor feedback speed, teaching load) to assess whether those conditions apply to you
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Most exceed the window — ask what the department concretely offers students in years 6–8 and how many students currently hold external dissertation fellowships

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you verified whether your target supervisor has active grant funding?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands that Canadian PhD RA funding flows from the supervisor's grant and has assessed the financial viability of the proposed supervisory relationship
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: When does the grant expire, and has the professor indicated whether a renewal application is pending?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Search NSERC or CIHR databases for the professor's name before your next contact — this is not intrusive, it is due diligence.

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you also considering US PhD programs, and if so, have you adjusted the Canadian stipend for the CAD/USD exchange rate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals whether the student is making an apples-to-apples comparison or being misled by nominal dollar equivalence
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: After exchange rate conversion, is the Canadian offer still competitive? Have you also added back $2,000-$4,000 for healthcare savings?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If not comparing to US programs, this factor is less relevant — but cost of living in Canada still requires city-specific assessment

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your target NOC code post-graduation, and does your planned employment on PGWP fall under TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the work experience being accumulated will count toward the 1,560-hour CEC requirement or be wasted for PR purposes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If TEER 0-3: confirm job description documentation matches NOC; track hours carefully from day one
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If uncertain or TEER 4/5 risk: consult an immigration professional before accepting the role; explore whether a different position is feasible

diagnostic_questions.question: What subfield of CS are you targeting, and have you mapped the industry vs. academic job market specifically for that subfield?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands that ML/AI, systems, NLP, theory, HCI, security, and databases have meaningfully different industry demand and academic competitiveness profiles
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: For ML/AI: Are you aware that the academic job market is dominated by top-5 programs, or are you relying on a lower-ranked program for a faculty goal?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Theory and HCI have moderate industry demand; ML/AI/NLP have extreme demand. Career strategy should be calibrated to the specific subfield, not CS broadly.

diagnostic_questions.question: If the advisor relationship deteriorates in year 2 or 3, is there a co-advisor or DGS who has demonstrably intervened in past student-advisor conflicts at this institution?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the support structure is real and functional or theoretical and deferential to faculty power
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have current or former students confirmed that this person actually intervened in a past conflict, not just that the role exists?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What is your plan if the institutional support structure is unavailable when you need it?

diagnostic_questions.question: How do the two of you resolve disagreements about research direction when they arise?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the advisors have an established conflict-resolution mechanism or are passing the resolution burden to the student by default
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they describe a process, ask for a concrete example of when it was used and what the outcome was
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they cannot describe a process or seem surprised by the question, treat this as evidence that conflict resolution has not been thought through

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the program located in a city with dense employer presence for your target sector, and do major employers in your field conduct on-campus recruiting at this program?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student has factored geographic constraints on OPT job search into their program selection, or is treating location as a lifestyle preference rather than a structural career variable
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you spoken to recent international graduates from this program about their actual OPT job search experience?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you modeled what your job search would look like if you needed to relocate during a 12–36 month OPT window in a competitive hiring market?

diagnostic_questions.question: What will your MS advisor's letter of recommendation actually say about your research?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Forces the applicant to assess whether the program structure will generate research-specific evidence versus generic academic performance evidence
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you spoken with the prospective advisor about their willingness to write research-specific letters for PhD applications?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the advisor cannot speak to research independence and original thinking, the letter will be inadequate for PhD applications regardless of GPA

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have existing undergraduate research experience, publications, or prior RA positions?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether a coursework MS can be viable as a PhD stepping stone — if strong undergraduate research exists, PhD programs may not require additional MS-level research
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: Is the undergraduate research recent, documented, and referable? Does it align with the PhD program's research areas?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: The MS must generate research output for the PhD application to be competitive; a coursework MS without independent research activity is insufficient.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have any current PhD students in this program or lab experienced a funding gap during their degree?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Funding gaps signal either poor advisor grant management, unstable external funding, or a program that does not backstop students when funding lapses — all serious structural risks
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: ask how the gap was resolved, who was responsible, and whether the program has a formal policy for bridging funding gaps
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: ask whether there is a formal department policy guaranteeing funding for students in good standing, and what 'good standing' means in practice

diagnostic_questions.question: How many programs on your list have at least 3 potential advisors you could work with?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the application portfolio is constructed with backup options or is dependent on single-point-of-failure advisor matches
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you contacted any of those backup advisors, or only your primary target?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The portfolio is structurally high-variance — any single advisor lacking bandwidth eliminates that program entirely

diagnostic_questions.question: How many first-author papers have students in this lab typically published by the time they're in year 3 or 4?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Assesses exploitation pattern risk; very low first-author counts relative to program duration and lab output volume indicate students are contributing to advisor publications without receiving authorship credit
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What does the process look like from project idea to publication — how involved is the advisor at each stage?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What are students working on that isn't getting published yet?

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the department's written policy for students whose advisor leaves or is denied tenure?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the department has institutional infrastructure for this scenario or leaves students to navigate it ad hoc; vague answers indicate the situation hasn't been well-managed before
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is there explicit bridge funding coverage, and does it apply to international students?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The absence of a clear policy is itself a high-risk signal — escalate questions to the DGS before accepting the offer

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you spoken directly with current PhD students in your target advisor's lab — without the advisor present?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the student has access to ground-truth information about advisor mentorship quality, lab culture, and time-to-degree
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: What did current students say about meeting frequency, feedback quality, and graduation support?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: This is the highest-value information-gathering action available before accepting — prioritize it

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you spoken with graduates of the program you're holding an offer from about their career outcomes?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the prestige gap between the offer and the target is real and consequential, or assumed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Do those outcomes suggest a material gap that justifies one year of lost income and productivity?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You are making a decision based on ranking proxies rather than outcome data — gather this information before deciding

diagnostic_questions.question: For EU programs: Have you resided in the target country for more than 12 months in the past 3 years?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is eligible for MSCA DN positions at that institution — the primary internationally-open funding mechanism in EU PhD programs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: You are ineligible for MSCA positions at that specific institution; look at MSCA positions in other EU countries where you have not recently resided, or pursue non-MSCA funding routes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You are eligible for MSCA positions — prioritize these over non-MSCA EU positions since they have no nationality restrictions and provide stronger funding

diagnostic_questions.question: Which specific employers recruited from this program in the last two years, and do those employers have a documented history of H-1B sponsorship?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the program has a real pipeline to viable employers for international students, versus general employment statistics that may include employers who will not sponsor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Can you get the names of specific companies, not aggregated placement rates? Have you looked those companies up on USCIS H-1B disclosure data?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the program cannot provide this, that is informative — programs with strong international pipelines can answer this question

diagnostic_questions.question: How many students is the prospective advisor currently advising, and are they in a significant administrative role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Predicts the advisor's practical availability for manuscript reading and mentorship — advising load and administrative duties are the primary operational constraints on feedback speed, which directly affects time-to-degree
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: High advising load or administrative role — ask current students how long it takes to get chapter feedback; if over 3 months, treat as a structural problem
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Low load and no major administrative role — verify by asking current students whether the advisor is actively engaged and returning drafts on a reasonable timeline

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you planning to stay in Canada after your PhD, and have you mapped your PhD program choice to specific immigration pathways?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is treating institution location as a neutral variable when it has significant implications for PNP eligibility and CRS points strategy
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you compared the PNP streams available in the province of each target school, and do you know whether any target institutions fall under streams that favor non-major-metro graduates?
